docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Install ChemWorld, define an experimental environment and connect your own agent. These guides describe the interfaces, models and limits of the public implementation.

docs.title: Understand the models and interfaces
docs.text:
• World foundations: state, physical models and experimental contracts.
  • Native foundation: supported models and their finite scope.
  • API reference: interfaces, parameters and executable examples.
  • Current progress: what is available in this public snapshot.
  • Evidence and limitations: what has been checked and where claims stop.

For a visual introduction, capability maps and recorded experiments, visit the ChemWorld website.

docs.title: 编写 Action 与 Recipe
docs.text: Action 是一次操作，Recipe 是一组按顺序执行的 Action。两者都使用普通字典/JSON，因此同一份内容 可以交给 Gym 环境、baseline、轨迹回放和提交验证器。

docs.title: Action：提交一个动作
docs.text:
最小 Action 只包含操作名：

{"operation": "terminate"}

带参数的常见例子：

{"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.03, "solvent": 1}
{"operation": "heat", "temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0, "stirring_rpm": 800.0}
{"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"}

不要凭记忆填写范围。运行时 schema 会告诉你必填字段、单位、上下界和类别选项：

schema = env.unwrapped.action_schema("heat")

docs.title: Recipe：描述一条实验路线
docs.text:
recipe = [
    {"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.03, "solvent": 1},
    {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.012},
    {"operation": "heat", "temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0},
    {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"},
]

Recipe 适合固定 baseline、教程和回放。它只是动作清单，并不提前保证每一步合法：环境仍会结合 当前任务、物料状态、预算和前置条件逐步检查。

docs.title: 动作失败时看哪里
docs.text:
信号 含义 Agent 通常应该做什么 precondition_failed 当前状态还不能执行该操作 补齐前序步骤或换一个合法操作 unsafe / unsafe_by_task_limit 触发环境或任务风险边界 降低强度、缩短时间或改变路线 high_cost 成本超过任务阈值 减少测量或选择更便宜的流程 low_selectivity 当前路线选择性不足 调整条件或先获取信息 constitution_failed 状态账本或守恒检查失败 将运行视为环境/执行失败并保留证据

这些信号是可学习反馈，不是可以忽略的日志。需要查看当前合法动作时，优先使用 available_actions() 和 validate_action()。

与现实设备的边界

Action schema 描述可评测的虚拟实验操作，不等同真实机器人指令。设备驱动、权限、联锁和安全 审批应由独立 adapter 处理。

docs.title: Connect an agent
docs.text:
Start with the environment API and authoring guide. You can supply any planner and choose your own reward, or use no reward. The task-scored runner and preset adapters below are retained historical applications; their CLI is python -m chemworld.legacy.cli.

ChemWorld agents choose one typed operation at a time from public task state. The environment keeps hidden world state evaluator-owned, validates every request, records resource use and writes an exact replay trajectory. Start offline before introducing an external model.

docs.title: Capability matrix
docs.text:
Path Network or key Intended use Public status Custom Python agent No Your own planner or policy Stable protocol Built-in classic agents No Smoke tests and reproducible baselines Stable Replay agent No Re-run a previously captured model trace Stable DeepSeek LiveLLMAgent DEEPSEEK_API_KEY Operation-level online model experiments Optional adapter Codex subscription client Existing codex login Audited structured calls through a ChatGPT subscription Optional adapter Interactive Codex experiment Existing codex login One persistent model context per complete experiment Advanced API Frozen SB3 policy Local checkpoint and .[rl] Evaluation of an already trained RL policy Optional extra

The command-line --agent flag intentionally exposes only constructor-free built-ins. Agents that need credentials, model selection, replay paths, checkpoints or workspaces are created in Python and passed to run_agent explicitly.

docs.title: Minimal custom agent
docs.text:
Subclassing BaseAgent supplies a zero-external-resource manifest. Use only public task information and public history when choosing an action.

from chemworld.agents.base import BaseAgent, HistoryRecord
from chemworld.eval.runner import run_agent


class TutorialAgent(BaseAgent):
    name = "tutorial"

    recipe = (
        {"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.030, "solvent": 1},
        {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.012},
        {"operation": "add_catalyst", "catalyst": 2, "catalyst_amount_mol": 0.0004},
        {"operation": "heat", "target_temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0,
         "stirring_speed_rpm": 800.0},
        {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "hplc"},
        {"operation": "quench"},
        {"operation": "terminate"},
        {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"},
    )

    def act(self, history: list[HistoryRecord]) -> dict[str, object]:
        return dict(self.recipe[len(history)])


run_agent(
    env_id="ChemWorld",
    agent=TutorialAgent(),
    world_split="public-dev",
    budget=8,
    objective="balanced",
    seed=0,
    task_id="reaction-to-assay",
    output_path="runs/tutorial-agent.jsonl",
)

For a capable agent, prefer act_with_context(context) or act_with_public_view(context, public_view). The official runner detects these methods and provides the current legal operations, resource state, observation summaries and lifecycle status without exposing hidden truth.

docs.title: Built-in offline agents
docs.text:
List tasks and run a deterministic connectivity check:

chemworld tasks list
python -m chemworld.legacy.cli run --task reaction-to-assay --agent scripted_chemistry --seed 0

Other constructor-free names include random, lhs, greedy, gp_bo, rf_ei, safe_gp_bo, tool_using_llm_stub and llm_replay. Use make_agent(name) from chemworld.legacy.agent_registry when composing runs in Python.

docs.title: Live DeepSeek adapter
docs.text:
Keep the key out of source files and shell history:

export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="..."

from chemworld.legacy.agents.live_llm import LiveLLMAgent
from chemworld.eval.runner import run_agent
from chemworld.providers.deepseek import DeepSeekClient

client = DeepSeekClient(model="deepseek-v4-pro", thinking=True)
agent = LiveLLMAgent(client, role_id="public-example")

run_agent(
    env_id="ChemWorld",
    agent=agent,
    world_split="public-dev",
    budget=18,
    objective="balanced",
    seed=0,
    task_id="reaction-to-assay",
    output_path="runs/deepseek-reaction-to-assay.jsonl",
)

Model identity, retries, token use and estimated cost are recorded separately. Provider failure is not silently replaced with another model or a host-generated action.

docs.title: Codex subscription adapter
docs.text:
Install the Codex CLI, complete codex login with a ChatGPT subscription, and construct CodexSubscriptionClient from chemworld.providers.codex_subscription. Pass that client to LiveLLMAgent using the same runner pattern above. Subscription usage has no per-run USD price, so the accounting receipt reports that limitation rather than inventing a cost.

InteractiveCodexExperimentAgent is the advanced path for keeping one Codex context alive across a complete experiment. It requires an explicit isolated workspace and role identifier; see the class docstring and focused tests before using it in a formal comparison.

docs.title: Reproducibility and safety boundary
docs.text:
• Never commit API keys, provider response dumps or private reasoning.
  • Do not compare live-agent scores unless task, seed, model identity, prompt contract and resource limits are fixed.
  • Validate and replay every submitted trajectory before reporting a score.
  • ChemWorld is a software-model environment, not a generator of physical laboratory procedures.
  • The checked-in live-agent evidence is finite qualification evidence, not a claim that one provider or agent is generally superior.

docs.title: Public distribution
docs.text:
This repository publishes a selected development distribution of ChemWorld. Install from this checkout with uv sync --locked --extra dev, or build wheel and source archives with uv build. The source version remains 0.5.0.dev0; no new PyPI release is implied by a repository update.

The package contains the runtime, approved simulator resources, environment CLI, Python examples and optional CPU build source. Research inputs, private evaluation sets, credentials, provider payloads, internal UI prototypes and paper assets are outside the distribution. The source-selection hook also supports rebuilding the sdist without the research repository.

The only console command is chemworld. Historical benchmark applications have the explicit legacy entry point. Native workflows need no upstream chemistry solver; optional reference libraries are used for separate comparisons. The current foundation page records validation scope.

For old paper results, use the frozen source and lockfile. Current physics does not reproduce every historical trajectory.

docs.title: Latest development — 25 October 2026
docs.text:
The main development repository has advanced beyond the current public package. The additions below are committed development work; they are not yet included in the public installation described in the next section.

Area Latest development Scope Process networks Finite graphs connect explicit feeds, splitters, mixers, heat exchange, separation and multiple recycle connections. Inventory and trajectory-control consumers use the same world state. Boundary and initialization fixes are being checked; the complete fixed-scope qualification remains in progress. Battery observations Half-cell DFN readouts can be serialized and restored with explicit model and field checks. Measurement records remain derived observations; this does not establish completion of the whole half-cell programme. Mechanism interoperability Supported imported Cantera gas networks can be exported with their original species, reaction and unit declarations. Complete source declarations are required; unsupported or incomplete networks are rejected. Property fitting Physical sensitivity diagnostics now require successful finite-difference evaluations of the original model. An optimizer penalty alone cannot establish parameter identifiability; failed trials remain visible.

The development board currently records 39 of 56 parent tasks complete, five active and twelve pending. The separate CPU programme has 4 of 31 tasks complete. Task completion and software-reference comparisons do not establish universal material accuracy. Full scientific-model execution remains on Python.

docs.title: Available in the public source
docs.text:
The public Python runtime still follows the 25 October source snapshot 823b6b01f. Choose apparatus and action/resource limits with environment authoring, then connect an agent and define an optional reward. The three-action user reward example is included.

Area Publicly available scope Thermodynamics and interfaces Molecular/association/multifluid models, multiphase caloric flash, finite-process consumers and planar interface calculations Reactions and biochemical systems Reactor networks, energy transport, imported mechanisms, SBML/COPASI interoperability and bounded hybrid dynamics Water and electrochemistry Finite membrane/treatment flows, activated sludge, battery parameter and hysteresis families, selected half-cell and thermal workflows Environment use User-defined objectives and rewards, persistent state, resource limits, observations and replay Optional CPU development Semantic declarations, resource/history infrastructure and a C++20 ABI/binding skeleton; full numerical-model migration remains in progress

The installed registry declares 31 modules, 38 component types, 52 operations and 30 instruments. These are software declarations, not independent scientific domains or capabilities available in every world. The website reads these counts from the public registry when it builds; the capability map remains an editorial guide.

Use the Python, CLI or Agent interfaces. The old Student Lab command is retired; Research Workbench and Blender Lab remain internal prototypes.

docs.title: Verification and historical evidence
docs.text:
At the public runtime synchronization, 82 executable API examples passed, and wheel and source-distribution installations passed independently on Windows Python 3.11.15, including native workflows and fresh-process replay. These results belong to that public runtime; they do not qualify the newer development additions above. The record of the public synchronization retains the exact test scopes and denominators.

The homepage, capability atlas and domain guides share the original website interface at /. Documentation opens in the integrated reader with domain navigation, section links and copyable code. Old /explore/ and guide addresses still work. This update changes website content, not the runtime, PyPI release or paper results.

Frozen notebooks and trace demonstrations retain their original runtime versions; see Evidence and Notebooks. Current physics is not a promise of numerical compatibility with those historical records. Complete upstream qualification, wider platform coverage and most CPU execution tasks remain ongoing.

docs.title: Design your own experimental environment
docs.text: Choose supported physical models and equipment, declare operations, instruments and resources, then connect your own agent. Users define the research question, exploration strategy, reward and evaluation. The current entry points are WorldCompositionSpec and ChemWorldRuntime; installed module declarations define the supported capabilities.

docs.title: Customize a working environment
docs.text:
This example reuses the native surface-reaction apparatus and changes both research vessels' temperature bounds, operation duration and total operation budget. Its vessels, finite gas feeds, catalysts and thermal models come from the existing builder. Parameters are synthetic examples, not predictions for a real catalyst. No agent action sequence is prescribed.

import json
from pathlib import Path

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.composition import WorldCompositionSpec
from chemworld.world.surface_world import surface_world_spec

design = surface_world_spec(terminal_assay=False).to_dict()
design["composition_id"] = "my-two-vessel-study"
design["task"]["objective"] = "Investigate how heating changes measured gas composition"
design["task"]["budget"] = 24
for component in design["components"]:
    if component["kind"] == "thermal":
        component["parameters"]["temperature_range_K"] = [330, 410]
        component["parameters"]["duration_range_s"] = [1, 60]

spec = WorldCompositionSpec.from_dict(design)
Path("world.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(spec.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=spec, observation_noise_mode="keyed")
try:
    session.reset(seed=12)
    print(session.task_prompt()["text"])
    print(session.available_actions())
    print(session.action_schema("heat"))
finally:
    session.close()

Save the script and world.json in your own working directory. Parsing and runtime compilation check compatibility and parameters; naming a module does not install a new physical capability. For other domains, consult the domain workflows and installed capabilities before choosing a supported builder or model declaration.

docs.title: Let your agent operate the environment
docs.text:
Your host loads world.json, creates a session and gives the agent the research question, task_prompt(), action schemas and acquired native observations. The agent chooses its next action; the host calls validate_action(action) and execute(action), saves the execution record and returns public results. Reading observe() neither acquires a measurement nor advances the clock.

Read result.observation.to_dict()["native"]["channels"] and preserve units, quality, sample times and uncertainty. Missing values are not zero; cached readings are not new evidence. The world declaration, full result.info and session snapshots belong to the host and may contain physical parameters or internal diagnostics withheld from the agent.

An unscored environment's prompt uses the declared objective. It does not require optimizing a built-in score or submitting an agent manifest. trajectory_validity in structured metadata describes record/replay checks, not agent performance. A reward is optional; see the ordinary Python reward example. Termination follows the declared world: this example needs no terminal assay, while other environments may explicitly require a terminal instrument.

docs.title: Record, resume and inspect
docs.text:
• Save actions and native measurements; use the existing trajectory logger and replay interfaces.
  • session.snapshot() saves private state; ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(...) continues compatible sessions.
  • Account for model usage separately from physical operations and reserve capacity for a final report if needed.
  • Research Workbench and Blender Lab are deferred; use the environment API and CLI.

docs.title: Historical research protocols
docs.text: The Work I world-fork protocol linked from the archive guide specifies single-variable interventions and frozen evidence for a controlled study. It is not the general authoring process for a new environment. Reproducing that study requires its bound version; start here when designing an environment for your own agent.

docs.title: Use the programmable environment
docs.text: ChemWorld provides physical models, composable equipment, experimental operations, native-unit observations, resource records and replay. Users own their agents, objectives, rewards and evaluation methods. Free exploration requires no preset agent and no leaderboard submission.

docs.title: Install and inspect capabilities
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/sunyrain/ChemWorld-Public.git
cd ChemWorld-Public
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run --no-sync chemworld capabilities --format json
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.user_reward

Installed-wheel users run their environment's chemworld and python -m chemworld.examples.user_reward directly. The distribution name remains chemworld-bench; this change does not rename or publish a package.

docs.title: Connect your agent
docs.text:
Use the environment authoring guide to choose equipment, operation bounds and resources, then connect your own agent.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.surface_world import surface_world_spec

session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=surface_world_spec())
try:
    session.reset(seed=12)
    print(session.available_actions())
    print(session.action_schema("add_component"))
    # Your agent chooses the action. No preset policy or reward is required.
    action = {"operation": "add_component", "component": "CO-feed", "amount_mol": 6e-5}
    result = session.execute(action)
    print(result.observation.to_dict())
finally:
    session.close()

Consume native channels with their units, quality, sample identity and timestamps. An unmeasured value is not zero. Reading an existing observation performs no new measurement. Supported operations depend on the declared world and current state. Keep host diagnostics private: do not forward the entire result.info or a private snapshot to a restricted agent.

The existing tool-based research path supplies MCP operations, public history, measurement artifacts and an optional notebook. InteractiveCodexExperimentAgent remains a used provider integration, not a requirement for free exploration. A separate third-party MCP host has not been qualified in this cleanup; callers can directly control the Python environment interface.

docs.title: Write your own reward or evaluator
docs.text:
chemworld.examples.user_reward uses an ordinary Python function over a newly acquired pressure reading. Pass reward_fn=None to use no reward. Changing the reward does not change the physics. Its target and scale are demonstration choices, not official success criteria.

The runtime retains reward, task termination and historical scoring fields used by existing research and Gym consumers. This entry-point cleanup does not alter their execution semantics. New applications can ignore the old reward and compute their own from public observations and resources, or use a separate host evaluator. Private-reference evaluation belongs on the trusted host, not in agent feedback.

docs.title: Environment tools
docs.text:
• chemworld capabilities: inspect installed module declarations.
  • chemworld render --composition world.json --actions action.json --format json: execute actions.
  • chemworld verify --submission trajectory.jsonl: verify replay, not agent performance.
  • session.snapshot() and ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(...): save and continue supported sessions.

docs.title: Interface release status
docs.text:
Research Workbench and Blender Lab are the two retained internal interface prototypes; their public release remains deferred. Task Lab, Lab Console, Experiment Explorer and Asset Preview have been removed from the source tree. Current sdists and wheels exclude these interfaces and their dedicated backends, and do not register chemworld-lab. Use the Python API, chemworld environment CLI or agent tools. The static documentation site provides guides and recorded examples.

See native sessions, domain workflows, shared laboratories and distribution scope. Offline research demonstrates one optional evaluation template. Historical rankings, baselines and step-wise LLM adapters have explicit legacy entry points.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Current main: October foundation update. Existing figures and numerical evidence below describe the frozen August runtime.

ChemWorld v0.3.0 retains the four frozen, sanitized evidence groups from v0.2.0. The presentation layer adds no new benchmark experiment.

Evidence group Frozen result What it supports Composition qualification 64/64 units; 1,786/1,786 recipes Registered world composition and reference execution Deterministic use cases 8/8 cases; 89 submitted actions Lifecycle, failure, resource and exact-replay semantics Controlled world forks 6 pairs; 24 traces Single-component world changes under fixed public experiments Agent instrument use 1 lifecycle; 15 committed actions Persistent use of the public action and instrument interface

docs.title: Why the visual is auditable
docs.text: scripts/build_readme_visuals.py reads only the sanitized compressed reports. It regenerates the README SVG, the interactive site payload and the detailed static tables. --check fails when any checked-in output is stale.

docs.title: Provenance and sanitization
docs.text:
Every compressed report binds its original SHA-256, sanitizer version, public protocol and a digest of removed metadata. Canonical JSON and gzip mtime=0 make repeated sanitization reproducible.

See the complete report map, representative behavior tables and release manifest.

Finite claim boundary

Passing these checks does not establish universal chemical fidelity, general agent intelligence or safe transfer to real laboratory practice.

docs.title: Native extensions and model ranges
docs.text:
The public Python backend now includes the following bounded model families. The current foundation records source and qualification status; the API guide gives executable input/output examples.

Area Implemented scope Shared foundation Owned state, residual/DAE infrastructure, local/shared clocks, finite resources, queued measurements, exact continuation and replay Thermodynamics Activity/UNIFAC/cubic models, Helmholtz, IF97/ice/humid air/incompressible fluids, selected molecular/association/multifluid EOS, local stability and flash Engineering processes Fluid correlations, serial molecular units, single recycle, finite receivers and bounded design Reactions and transport Imported gas/surface chemistry, finite graph/rule growth, energy grains, reactor networks, wall/piston/heat coupling and bounded 1D transport Aqueous and separation Sourced aqueous/mineral chemistry, reactive transport, headspace, RO/NF/MD/ED, adsorption, resin/GAC, precipitation, clarification, filtration and washing Solid phases Selected CALPHAD/ChemSage models, multiphase CEF TP/PH, finite binary/ternary diagram searches Batteries SPM/SPMe/DFN, particle distributions, composite/MSMR/half-cell and other finite families, selected controls/thermal models, SEI/plating, impedance and SOH Stochastic and biochemical analysis Direct/next-reaction, explicit-partition hybrid dynamics and bounded tau-leap; SBML/SED-ML subsets, steady/control analysis, fitting, profiles, flux modes and finite-time growth

docs.title: Current boundaries
docs.text:
Each model declares its sources, units, phases and validity ranges. Some are synthetic demonstrations; others carry sourced parameters. A delivered equation does not validate every material. Battery and molecular parent programmes remain active even where individual submodels have passed their fixed comparisons.

The public package retains bounded serial and single-recycle process consumers. General finite process graphs and their inventory/control integrations have advanced in main development; see latest progress. General freely propagating flames, unrestricted global phase envelopes, complete upstream databases and universal long-term aging remain outside the delivered scope. The optional C++ build skeleton is available; scientific kernels and SIMD migration remain in progress. See shared time for supported couplings.

docs.title: Reference and reuse practice
docs.text: Production models run through the native Python backend. Optional upstream solvers serve as independent references. Analytical limits, conservation and fixed comparison cases check the implemented slices; numerical agreement does not remove source/data attribution or license obligations. Caller-supplied databases retain their own licenses.

docs.title: 安装并跑通第一次实验
docs.text: 这一页只做一件事：从空环境走到一条通过回放验证的 ChemWorld 轨迹。第一次运行建议使用 reaction-to-assay，整个过程通常只需要几分钟。

docs.title: 1. 安装项目
docs.text:
需要 Python 3.11 或更高版本。

git clone https://github.com/sunyrain/ChemWorld-Public.git
cd ChemWorld-Public
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

确认命令行入口已经安装：

chemworld --help
chemworld tasks list
Windows文档与参考验证

如果 python 被解析成 Microsoft Store 别名，可以直接使用仓库虚拟环境：

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

只有在构建站点或运行扩展物理参考检查时，才需要额外依赖：

python -m pip install -e ".[dev,docs,physchem-ref]"

docs.title: 2. 运行一个完整回合
docs.text:
先让内置 Agent 完成一次实验：

chemworld run --task reaction-to-assay --agent random --seed 0

命令会把 trajectory JSONL 和 manifest 写入 runs/，并在终端打印实际路径。这里的 random Agent 不是性能基线；它只是最短的端到端连通性检查。

docs.title: 3. 验证结果
docs.text:
把上一步输出的轨迹路径代入下面两条命令：

chemworld verify --constitution --submission runs/<trajectory>.jsonl
chemworld evaluate --submission runs/<trajectory>.jsonl
  • verify 检查文件结构、合同摘要、状态守恒和确定性回放。
  • evaluate 从轨迹重新计算结果，不采用提交文件自带的分数。

看到验证通过后，你已经跑通了 ChemWorld 最核心的链路：

任务 → Agent → Action → 环境 → 轨迹 → 回放 → 评分

docs.title: 4. 用 Python 查看环境
docs.text:
import gymnasium as gym
import chemworld  # 注册 ChemWorld 环境

env = gym.make("ChemWorld", task_id="reaction-to-assay", seed=0)
observation, info = env.reset(seed=0)

print(info["task_id"])
print(info["physics_maturity"])
print(env.unwrapped.available_actions())

available_actions() 返回当前状态下真正可执行的操作。它比维护一套固定动作模板更可靠，因为不同 任务、阶段和物料状态会开放不同操作。

docs.title: 5. 手动执行一个 Action
docs.text:
先读取 schema，再在不改变环境状态的情况下校验动作：

schema = env.unwrapped.action_schema("add_reagent")
action = {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.01}
check = env.unwrapped.validate_action(action)

if check["valid"]:
    observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
else:
    print(check["invalid_reasons"])

无效动作会带回 invalid_reasons 和前置条件提示，方便 Agent 修改后重试。任务允许哪些操作、 仪器、预算与终止方式，以 reset 信息和任务卡为准。

正确处理未测量值

数组里的未测量值是 NaN，写入 JSONL 后是 null。不要把它当成零；读取数值时同时检查 observed_mask 或 observed_keys。

docs.title: 6. 打开可视化实验室
docs.text:
python -m apps.task_lab.server --port 8876

启动后可以打开：

  • Agent Observatory：观看 Agent 的逐步决策、谱图与资源消耗。
  • 环境API与CLI：执行自己的操作并读取观测；旧Student Lab入口已退役。

经典算法和本地实验不需要在线模型密钥。Provider 凭据和私有评测配置不属于本公开版本。

docs.title: 接下来做什么
docs.text: 如果你想…… 继续阅读 换一个更复杂的任务 查看世界能力地图 编写自己的 Agent 从动作 schema 开始 理解每种操作的含义 认识操作语言 做可复现的方法比较 阅读公开协议

docs.title: Historical applications
docs.text:
ChemWorld is a programmable physical environment. Rankings, preset policy factories and operation-by-operation LLM adapters no longer define the default entry point. Start with the programmable environment.

For new environments, use the current authoring guide. The retained Work I world-authoring contract is a frozen controlled-fork protocol. Its single-variable interventions, certificates and freeze procedures do not govern general environment development. Its original path and contents remain unchanged for bound historical evidence; the retained v1 composition contract likewise describes its first-paper research scope.

Historical feature Explicit archive entry run, evaluate, leaderboard, suite, baselines, submission and old release commands python -m chemworld.legacy.cli --help Ranking aggregation chemworld.legacy.leaderboard Preset policy factory chemworld.legacy.agent_registry.make_agent Eleven baseline/adapter modules chemworld.legacy.agents: bo, greedy, lhs, random, event, rl, llm, live_llm, diagnostic_live_llm, documented_codex_g2, structured_g2

These archived applications remain distributed for explicit research consumers. They are not recommended environment APIs or default scoring methods. Old imports are not silently redirected. The shared runner, free-research MCP tools, notebooks and used research implementations remain available. Runtime/trajectory fields with existing consumers retain their semantics in this cleanup.

Previous documentation and source are in Git commit 3e5fe32598d96c4ab2b83fcfb26b48939c26c967. Frozen experiments must still use their original bound version and data: these archive entry points do not recreate old physics. No historical experiment was rerun or recertified by this cleanup.

docs.title: Limitations and safe interpretation
docs.text:
ChemWorld is a software-model environment for controlled agent research. It is not a protocol generator for physical laboratory work.

  • Qualification covers finite registered tasks, compositions, probes and world forks—not all chemistry.
  • Public observations are generated by the declared software models and instruments; they do not certify experimental fidelity.
  • Tutorial recipes demonstrate interface use. They are not optimized procedures or recommendations for real materials.
  • Exact replay means the software trace is reproducible under the release contract. It does not reproduce laboratory uncertainty.
  • Controlled hidden components are evaluator-owned mechanisms for research design. Agents must not receive direct hidden-state access.

No manuscript files, unpublished results, development matrices, raw provider responses or private evaluator configuration are included in this repository.

For exact release claims, use the Evidence page and scripts/verify_release.py.

docs.title: Finite low-copy worlds
docs.text:
Original SBML inputs can use the same integer kernels through sbml_world:

from chemworld.world.sbml_world import sbml_world

# model is an SBMLModel with original XML, provenance and explicit source units.
world = sbml_world(model, numerical_form="stochastic",
                   solver_method="gibson-bruck-next-reaction-v1", seed=17,
                   maximum_events=100000, controlled_parameters=("k",))

The other choices are gillespie-direct-v1 and adaptive-explicit-tau-leap-v1; tau requires an explicit TauLeapPolicy through tau_policy. The builder seed selects the process stream. Session reset seeds select observation noise independently. The existing wait, set_model_parameters and formal_quantity_meter operations use the original formal equipment coordinates and shared laboratory clock. Pending reaction clocks or tau packets survive full JSON and new-process continuation.

This mode admits explicitly compiled nonnegative elementary source monomials of total molecular order at most three, including full regenerated reactants, declared modifiers and held boundary pools. Original substance, extent, volume, time, local-parameter and conversion-factor semantics determine each molecular quantum. Amounts must resolve to integer molecules; absent chemical formulas, temperature dependence and reaction energies are not invented. The reaction_rate readout retains the source deterministic law in mol/s; it is not a discrete propensity in events/s.

Signed net laws, saturation or fractional species powers, reversible single channels and continuously changing geometry remain outside this integer adapter. Existing deterministic SBML modes retain their source event/rule support and old v1/v2 JSON. Integer declarations use v3. Independent distribution, source-SDK and installed-package qualification of this adapter are recorded separately from its functional checks and from the authored chemical-network results below.

The existing SEDMLProtocol and SEDMLExperimentSession also accept these integer processes in finite SED-ML experiments and COMBINE archives. Declare KiSAO 0000029 for direct, 0000027 for Gibson–Bruck, or 0000084 for the implemented nonnegative Poisson tau strategy. Basic Poisson 0000040 is a different variant and is rejected. Algorithm parameter 0000488 supplies the process seed (default 0); 0000415 supplies the internal-step budget. Tau also accepts 0000467 (maximum step in source time units), 0000228 (epsilon), 0000230 (SSA fallback threshold) and 0000249 (critical threshold).

These declarations use the existing task graph, controls, measurements, reports and full experiment JSON cursor. resetModel="false" continues the same process; resetModel="true" restarts its declared process seed and initial inputs. Equal fixed seeds across resets do not create independent replicates. The experiment caller's seed controls the separate detector stream. Item-based archive models still need an explicit items_per_mole policy when using from_archive.

The developing integer source-event profile also consumes piecewise constant global parameter assignment rules, state-only constraints and the existing SBML event queue. State guards are checked after each actual reaction or tau batch; affine source-time guards and delayed queue deadlines split the advance. Event capture, cancellation, priorities, cascades and source concentration/volume assignments use the existing formal coordinates and unit conversion. The new queue continuation survives complete runtime and experiment JSON. Tau observes whole batches; this does not locate source events inside an approximate leap.

Continuous rate rules, non-affine time guards, time equality pulses, assignment rules for species/geometry and time-dependent constraints are rejected explicitly. The event profile is in development: functional and compatibility checks are available, while independent scientific/source and installed-package acceptance remain open. See the 51K evidence and scope.

Two synthetic worlds run on the native session and task-36 direct SSA strategy: biochemical_world("reversible") (A↔B) and biochemical_world("enzyme") (E+S→ES, ES→E+S, ES→E+P). These are numerical examples, not fitted biological systems. Synthetic E is N2 and ES is CH2N2O so binding preserves atoms. There is no Michaelis–Menten reduction and no implicit ODE/SSA switch.

Authored integer networks can explicitly supply full forward_orders for elementary autocatalysis (A+B → 2A), partial regeneration (2A → A+B) and catalysts with zero net change. Direct, next-reaction and tau-leap share these integer reactants, with total molecularity at most three and unchanged falling-factorial rates. Supply the full orders explicitly; an existing net-only declaration keeps its original meaning. In tau-leap, newly admitted channels also use a conservative initial-stock firing bound without crediting other channels' same-leap production. Invalid proposals are rejected, never clipped; this remains a biased Poisson approximation. See the implementation and qualification boundaries. The fixed fourteen-model development block completed 98,312 trajectories across the exact and two approximate strategies against independent finite-CME laws. The tau acceptance tests include declared approximation allowances; they do not establish exact-law equivalence. Kernel timing in this block found both tau policies slower than direct SSA. Actual source-SDK qualification is separate.

Run without a model key or COPASI:

uv run --no-sync python examples/native_biochemical.py
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_biochemical_worlds.py tests/test_stochastic_kinetics.py -q

The ordinary add_component action accepts mol units, but every dose must represent an exact integer number of molecules (within floating-point conversion roundoff). Feed index 0/1 is A for reversible, E/S for enzyme. No fractional rounding, carrier addition, thermal control or flow is supported in this slice. Elemental transitions are checked in exact integer atoms, not a macroscopic mol tolerance. The mol ledger remains the sole inventory; counts are a derived view.

molecule_counter reports independent Gaussian-noisy, signed calibrated counts (standard deviation 1 count, unit response per molecule), never event truth. molecule_capture independently selects each solute molecule with probability 0.1, exports selected molecules to instrument waste, and measures them with the same detector noise. It is an idealized molecular capture, not a withdrawn liquid aliquot: carrier volume stays constant. Analysis effort is 1 s on the offline instrument clock, with no reactor evolution. Both reads cost 0.01. Captured truth and sampling RNG remain private. Empty/noisy channels are not silently replaced by latent values. No saturation or unknown-species identification is claimed.

Process seed is declared in the world, detector seed at session reset, and capture uses a separate persisted stream derived from the world seed. Reads do not change the next reaction or capture; actual dosing/capture invalidates a pending event. Snapshots retain all continuations, and material/batch/vessel initialization restores the declared discrete state (including its initial process/capture seeds). Thus repeated resets are deterministic reinitializations, not independent replicates: author a world with a new seed for an independent process replicate. Stationary instrument usage survives material resets. Snapshots contain evaluator truth and are not agent observations.

Optional external-reference block (no default dependency, choose a fresh output):

uv run --no-sync --with python-copasi==4.48.309 python scripts/validate_native_biochemical.py --output /tmp/biochemical-attempt.json

The fixed development design and complete 8,288 endpoints are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_BIOCHEMICAL_ACCEPTANCE.md and NATIVE_BIOCHEMICAL_RESULTS.json. It compares transient/effectively equilibrated binomial moments, finite COPASI endpoint distributions and volume/count-scaled ODE convergence. Finite distribution agreement is not proof of all kinetic regimes or wet-lab predictive validity. A generic molecule counter and synthetic capture are explicit simplifications, not models of a named physical assay.

docs.title: Controlled fixed-partition ODE / stochastic chemistry
docs.text:
StochasticHybridSpec and CrossPartitionHybridSpec accept ode_method="RK45" when authoring a world with stochastic_hybrid_world. This selects the shared solver backend's RK45 policy for the continuous state and integrated Poisson hazards. The historical default is DOP853; default JSON declarations keep their original field set and execution signature. The selected method is bound to the numerical continuation and retained across full JSON restoration.

Both methods use the original network, phase inventory, transaction manager and shared clock. The fixed partition keeps its integer and continuous closed stocks; the cross-partition variant additionally records real stoichiometric molecular transfers and enforces whole-jump availability. Existing isothermal, fixed-volume and unsupported-operation boundaries still apply. See the cross-partition example; pass ode_method="RK45" when constructing its physical specification.

Full checkpoints with the same future actions reproduce the complete state and diagnostics exactly. Arbitrary wait splits retain numerical agreement rather than a bitwise trajectory guarantee. A fixed ten-model RK45 development block completed 12,289 native and 81,921 independent analytic trajectories with its physical, marginal/joint distribution and moment checks passing. Separate paired kernel measurements against DOP853 found RK45 slower on most tested models; explicit selection does not imply acceleration. Actual COPASI method-31 output has retained negative-stock and last-bit repeat discrepancies, so full source qualification remains open in task 51G. See the complete results and limits.

docs.title: Continuous reaction SDE (development)
docs.text:
stochastic_sde_world installs continuous Itô reaction noise on the same native session and mol inventory. This is a continuous population approximation. It does not quantize populations or doses into integer molecules.

from dataclasses import replace
from chemworld.foundation.discrete_inventory import AVOGADRO
from chemworld.physchem import StochasticSDESpec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.biochemical_worlds import biochemical_network
from chemworld.world.stochastic_sde_world import stochastic_sde_world

network = replace(biochemical_network("reversible"), stochastic=None)
spec = StochasticSDESpec(volume_L=1e-15, step_s=0.125)
world = stochastic_sde_world(
    network, spec, {"A": 100.5 / AVOGADRO, "B": 20.25 / AVOGADRO}, seed=123,
)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=world)
try:
    session.reset(seed=7)
    session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 0.0625})
    result = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "sde_amount_meter"})
    print(result.observation.to_dict())
finally:
    session.close()

The default drift uses the original elementary mass-action concentration law; each reaction gets independent noise with amplitude sqrt(abs(particle_flux)). ReactionFlux and ReactionNoise can bind safe MathML with typed SDEParameter values in coherent SI. Flux outputs require particle/s and noise outputs require particle/sqrt(s). Populations n0... are dimensionless, amounts a0... are mol, concentrations c0... are mol/m³, and volume_m3 is m³. Default native kinetic constants retain their original mol/L concentration basis. Unknown symbols, incompatible branch units and cyclic flux dependencies are rejected.

RI5 defaults to fixed mesh endpoints and linear output within each accepted interval. Snapshots retain the already drawn weak variables, numerical endpoints and mesh anchor. Splitting waits retains the same numerical trajectory. The weak-order claim concerns smooth interior mesh endpoints; the linear output is not a Brownian bridge. boundary_policy="physical" uses bounded feasible-side step reduction and redraws; "reject" fails on a negative candidate. Neither policy clips negative stock. Work limits fail the original transaction without consuming its process stream. Boundary reduction/redrawing can bias distributions and has no boundary weak-order or exact chemical-master-equation guarantee.

Set output_policy="ri5_fractional" explicitly to evaluate the RI5 map at the requested elapsed time from the saved left endpoint and weak variables. This avoids the variance loss caused by linear interpolation between mesh endpoints. It consumes no additional process draw. Actual callbacks, including saved-output and endpoint verification, count toward the evaluation budget. This remains a weak numerical output, with no strong-path or Brownian-bridge claim. A negative fractional output fails the whole transaction; a feasible full endpoint does not certify every intermediate time. The solver does not clip that output or replace it with linear interpolation. Historical declarations without an output policy retain their original linear codec and saved numerical path.

Set output_policy="ri5_truncated" to make each requested output time an accepted RI5 endpoint. Before drawing a numerical candidate, the step is capped at the requested time; physical acceptance therefore checks the endpoint that will actually be committed. This policy carries no pending dense output. A final interval shorter than min_step_s is attempted as a whole; if it is infeasible, the bounded redraw rule applies without further sub-minimum backtracking. Stock is never clipped or replaced with another output strategy.

With this policy, splitting a wait can change its numerical grid and weak trajectory. The same complete checkpoint and same subsequent actions still reproduce the full state exactly. Instantaneous nonconsuming measurement does not split time or consume the process stream. The linear and fractional options keep their existing fixed-mesh rules and historical snapshot bindings.

Continuous solute dosing uses add_component and the existing feed index (0 is A in the example). It discards numerical lookahead and retains the consumed RNG. The fixed-temperature declaration excludes thermal evolution and carrier addition. Each numerical interval has fixed volume. sde_amount_meter has independent signed Gaussian detector noise with SD 1/AVOGADRO mol and no sampling or reactor time. Integer molecular instruments and unbound consuming samplers are rejected.

For bounded chemical inputs, declare SDEControl entries in spec.controls. Targets are rate_multiplier (dimensionless), flux_parameter, or noise_parameter (the named parameter's coherent SI units). For example:

from chemworld.physchem import SDEControl

spec = StochasticSDESpec(
    volume_L=1e-15, step_s=0.125, minimum_volume_L=0.75e-15,
    controls=(SDEControl("forward_scale", "forward", "rate_multiplier", 0, 4),),
)

Build the world with this spec, then call session.execute({"operation": "set_sde_parameters", "values": {"forward_scale": 0.5}}). The action schema exposes each declared input's bounds, dimensions and current value. A multi-input update is atomic. Unknown names, invalid dimensions, out-of-range values or a currently undefined flux/noise expression are rejected. Changes discard numerical lookahead while retaining the consumed process stream.

An explicit minimum_volume_L enables sde_aliquot_meter when its fixed 1e-16 L withdrawal fits. It uses the original representative liquid sampling and material receipts: actual mol and volume leave the reactor, with no rounding to molecular counts. It measures sample_amount_* in mol, with independent Gaussian SD 1/AVOGADRO mol, and charges 1 s of offline instrument time and 0.01. The reactor clock does not advance during this offline analysis. The sampler has deterministic volume; capture and pipetting noise are not modelled. The volume floor and numerical representability are enforced. Subsequent chemistry uses the remaining real volume and a freshly bound numerical interval.

Material/vessel initialization replaces the declared stocks and volume, retains the world clock, current inputs and process RNG, and invalidates lookahead. Batch initialization reinstalls the declared initial process seed and inputs, so it is deterministic reinitialization rather than an independent replicate. Instrument replacement retains reaction state and pending work. Snapshots and ordinary replay preserve these boundaries. Advance work reports count actual drift/diffusion callbacks, including numerical verification of a saved packet; snapshot restoration retains full numerical endpoint checks.

Native wait/feed/read, shared clocks, rollback, JSON and new-process continuation have functional checks. A wheel rebuilt from the sdist and genuinely installed outside the checkout passes all four native/Gym and detector-noise protocol combinations, exact replay and fresh-process continuation without COPASI. Its dependencies come from the locked caller environment. Independent SDE distributions, moment and step convergence, and boundary statistics remain open in task 51E. Separate sdist-built and genuinely installed wheels also pass all four protocols for each explicit fractional and truncated output policy, including exact replay, material initialization and fresh-process continuation. These results do not close parent task 51.

docs.title: Adaptive stochastic / deterministic partition (development)
docs.text:
stochastic_adaptive_world uses the existing chemical world, phase inventory, transaction manager and shared clock. AdaptiveHybridSpec selects lower and upper particle thresholds, the classification interval, and RK4 or LSODA for the deterministic subnet. Classification retains its previous value inside the hysteresis band. A reaction belongs to the stochastic subnet if any of its participants is low, including products and catalysts. Its persistent next-reaction target survives deactivation and reactivation.

Full integer forward_orders may include regenerated reactants. For A + B => 2 A, declare forward_orders={"A": 1, "B": 1}: rates use both reactants and material changes use the net stoichiometry once. The adaptive variant admits elementary molecularity up to three, including partial regeneration, and rejects missing consumed reactants or fractional orders.

from dataclasses import replace

from chemworld.physchem import AdaptiveHybridSpec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.biochemical_worlds import biochemical_network
from chemworld.world.stochastic_adaptive_world import stochastic_adaptive_world

network = replace(biochemical_network("reversible"), stochastic=None)
quantum = 1 / 6.02214076e23
spec = AdaptiveHybridSpec(
    volume_L=1e-15, lower_limit=45, upper_limit=55, step_s=0.125, method="LSODA"
)
world = stochastic_adaptive_world(
    network, spec, {"A": 50.25 * quantum, "B": 50.75 * quantum}, seed=17
)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=world)
try:
    session.reset(seed=7)
    session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 0.375})
    session.execute({"operation": "add_component", "component": 0, "amount_mol": 0.5 * quantum})
    result = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "sde_amount_meter"})
    print(result.observation.to_dict())
finally:
    session.close()

All material remains real mol in the original phase ledger; classification never rounds stocks to molecules. The stochastic rates use generalized falling factorials and require an available whole reaction jump. Fractional low populations therefore retain an explicit hybrid approximation. Rates are frozen within numerical slabs and refreshed at events, grid boundaries and material interventions. This is distinct from continuously integrated hazards.

This world currently fixes temperature and volume, supports instantaneous solute additions and nonconsuming mol measurements, and rejects consuming meters or other unbound couplings. Material and vessel initialization preserve the process stream and world time while rebinding channel targets; batch initialization reinstates the declared initial state. A numerical failure rolls back physical changes and keeps the existing failed-attempt accounting.

Complete JSON restoration and the same future actions reproduce the full state exactly, including in a new process. Arbitrary observation-time splits can change the deterministic numerical integration. An sdist-built wheel, genuinely installed outside the checkout, passes eight protocols across both ODE methods, native/Gym entry points and detector noise modes: 80 committed steps, exact replay and eight fresh-process continuations. Dependencies come from the locked caller environment. Independent finite-grid qualification covers 11 families across both methods and two step sizes: 44 units, 40,964 native and 163,844 reference trajectories. These tests cover linear ODE subnets and elementary SSA, including fractional stocks, switching and channel reactivation.

Measured resource comparisons show gains and regressions: RK4 is faster on the tested mixed networks, while low-copy and small ODE cases are slower. Replacing high-copy stochastic channels with ODE preserves their tested mean and removes their stochastic variance. Actual COPASI methods 29/30 discard material in the tested switching cases; native stocks remain unrounded.

Nonlinear fixed-grid qualification adds dimerization, trimerization, autocatalytic growth, feedback catalysis and mild/stiff enzyme reactions. All 36 native units pass against independent closed flows: 24,588 native and 98,316 reference trajectories, including two-step-size checks for pure ODEs. The 20,488 previously successful recorded endpoints, event counts, partitions, work and RNG states remain exact after expanding reactant admission. Both the original and autocatalytic installed profiles pass eight protocols each, including real stochastic events, ODE work, replay and fresh-process restoration.

The actual source comparison remains incomplete: 19/36 units pass; 270 SDK calls stop before their requested endpoint and other cases lose material. All failures and partial outputs are retained. Continuous-hazard convergence and full source equivalence remain unproven; this adaptive extension does not expand the separate integer SSA or fixed-partition model admission rules. See the complete qualification and limitations.

docs.title: Installed native capability declarations
docs.text:
Generated from DomainModuleRegistry; not a second module registry. Operation availability and numeric domains are further narrowed by the actual composition, physical specifications, device and task. A module declaration does not guarantee arbitrary cross-domain coupling.

Module Components / strategies Scope aqueous_gas_transfer aqueous_gas_transfer, finite-aqueous-gas-transfer Finite ideal-gas headspace and ideal aqueous liquid in one rigid isothermal vessel; reversible sourced gas/liquid transfer and fast aqueous reactions, actual gas pressure and same-reference internal-energy bath duty; optional seeded pure-mineral kinetics with actual solid volume displacing the headspace. Nonvolatile solvent, fixed liquid volume and zero solute partial volumes; no infinite gas source, pressure flow or spontaneous mineral nucleation. aqueous_mineral aqueous_mineral, finite-carbonate-calcite-equilibrium Authored finite aqueous acid/base/complexation and mineral equilibrium; explicit thermodynamic data and ionic-strength domain, not a geochemical database. Also finite same-T/P solution mixing, nonideal equilibrium precipitation and dilution with liquid-only packets, original solid inventory, same-reference enthalpy and pressure-volume work; instantaneous equilibrium, not nucleation kinetics. aqueous_reactive_transport aqueous_reactive_transport, finite-aqueous-reactive-transport Sealed one-dimensional ideal-dilute aqueous transport at fixed T/P; finite stationary water, zero solute partial volumes, zero-current electrodiffusion, fast equilibrium and declared slow neutral conversion. Also finite feed/collector throughflow with conservative upwind advection, common mechanical dispersion and actual water/solute/enthalpy transfer; prescribed kinematic flow at common T/P, without a pump model. Strictly positive ions; no pressure flow, mineral or external circuit. battery_spm battery_spm, battery_cell, single-particle-battery Synthetic SPM with calorics/SEI, or explicit isothermal SPMe-v1 with conservative electrolyte transport; shared native cycling. Explicit isothermal DFN has coupled spatial reactions and a fixed synthetic qualification at 24 through-plane cells per region / 64 radial cells. Explicit isothermal Newman-Tobias uses two average lithium inventories and spatial porous electrical fields, without radial diffusion or dynamic salt; its fixed CV grid-inventory qualification remains open. Development MPM adds shared-potential size populations with independent inventories; independent MPM scientific qualification remains pending. Isothermal single-material SPM/MPM may declare current-sigmoid OCP or one persistent Axen hysteresis coordinate per electrode; no hysteresis thermal/SEI coupling or equilibrium-SOH interpretation. Through-thickness thermal SPM uses three finite layers and two collectors, constant net OCV and local BV temperature feedback with ambient cooling; no arbitrary external thermal device or general material thermal claim. Isothermal MSMR-SPM uses one or two explicit reactions per electrode with potential-driven radial diffusion and shared branch kinetics; no MSMR thermal, EIS or automatic equilibrium-SOH claim. Isothermal composite DFN resolves two negative and one positive material phase at each thickness cell with shared potentials and dynamic salt; no composite-DFN thermal, side-reaction, SOH, EIS or chemical-energy closure. Collector SPM resolves 1+1D finite-conductivity current collectors with position-resolved single particles and explicit tab potentials; no electrolyte, thermal, side-reaction, PSD, hysteresis, SOH, EIS or chemical-energy closure. Composite SPM supports two independent negative material phases and one positive phase with single-valued monotone OCV, including internal exchange at zero terminal current; no thermal/SEI, EIS, SOH or energy closure. Positive-working half-cell SPM uses finite lithium metal with explicitly fixed geometry; no half-cell thermal/SEI, EIS, SOH or energy closure. Coarser meshes and other parameters need convergence checks; Closed volume-consistent isothermal lead-acid LOQS uses six real chemical inventories and the same runtime; no heat, side reactions, EIS or automatic SOH. Synthetic parameters are not wet-lab validation. Split OCV-R uses two finite mean Li inventories, separate electrode OCV and capacity, and series resistance; no particle diffusion, BV or heat. Its EIS and equilibrium SOH reuse the same declared inventory model. No PyBaMM runtime backend. battery_thevenin battery_thevenin, thevenin-empirical-circuit Sourced empirical RC and two-node cell/jig heat model; shared CC/CV control and persistent apparatus. No chemical inventory/total energy, diffusion element or independent released-model qualification yet. continuous_flow continuous_flow See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. core material_input, sample_storage, reaction Declared bulk reaction networks use the selected caloric model. An explicit homogeneous Peng-Robinson phase supports elementary Arrhenius activity-concentration kinetics, same-source standard thermochemistry and finite isochoric energy/pressure evolution; local single-phase stability only, no general nonideal mechanism family or multiphase reactive flash claim. crystallization aqueous_filter, crystal_thermal, crystallization, finite-crystal-population-temperature Authored crystal seeding, cooling and wet-cake operations; also declared same-T/P instantaneous aqueous mineral filtration into two finite empty receivers, with explicit solid capture and mother-liquid retention, actual leaked solids, wet-cake washing and repeat separation. Database filtration has no drying, pressure-drop or filtration-rate model. distillation distillation See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. dynamic_distillation dynamic_distillation, finite-equilibrium-column Finite tray/receiver inventories, heat and timed cuts; authored small dynamic column, not arbitrary plant design. electrical_control transient_electrode, finite-transient-electrode See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. electrochemistry electrochemistry See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. finite_transport finite_transport, finite-pump-transport Finite pump, pipe, tanks and authored heat exchange; bounded working point; or four finite tanks and two pumps exchanging countercurrent heat at declared UA with independent circuit flows; or declared isothermal zero-order liquid treatment chains with finite product/concentrate stocks and receipt-based engineering economics; or finite pump-fed neutral reactive holdup with ideal overflow to a finite product tank, volume-compatible chemistry and one shared bath; or the complete empirical ASM1 13-component/eight-process single CSTR or five-reactor recycle train, finite original water/quality stocks, oxygen supply/offgas and sludge; source-bound COD/N/equivalent budgets, not full molecular CHON, charge or biochemical reaction heat; or finite neutral aqueous mixed-contact adsorption and rinse with persistent competitive loading, five liquid stocks and one shared bath; or finite ideal-dilute Na/Ca resin exchange with counterion release, salt regeneration and rinse across six liquid stocks, weighted fixed resin charge and one shared bath; or finite neutral suspensions with a declared jar-test endpoint, explicit dispersed/floc particle phases, empirical clarification into actual clear-water/wet-sludge tanks, and mixing/pump work; no additive-driven coagulation prediction or settling dynamics; the adsorption-world feed also supports read-only single-solute fresh GAC design and breakthrough queries at fixed influent, using actual pump flow and feed volume above pickup; not remaining-life prediction for existing LDF media. These are declared finite models, not arbitrary multiphase process-network simulation. gas_reactor_network gas_reactor_network, finite-isothermal-gas-network Finite isothermal ideal-gas reactors, storage and collection nodes; declared molar/mass flow and one-way pressure valves; shared time, material transfers and bath heat; or explicit per-node energy with finite vessel heat capacities, source-temperature enthalpy transport, environment/neighbor heat exchange and one queued anchor heater. Complete imported ideal surfaces can share the same gas network, owned site stocks and calorics. Also sealed or finite-feed/collector isothermal low-Mach planar cells with common grid pressure, independent tank pressures, continuity-derived bulk flow and whole-mixture diffusion; prescribed boundary molar flow has no momentum or compressor model. Explicit nonisothermal cells jointly close continuity, local energy and common pressure with upwind enthalpy, diffusion enthalpy and Fourier heat; finite tanks, node heat exchange and the anchor heater retain original inventories and one shared clock. No Soret or momentum equation is implied. Alternatively one constant-load finite-stroke ideal-gas piston with actual EOS volume and separately booked pressure work, without surfaces or spatial cells. Constant-volume energy networks can instead declare one finite-heat-capacity wall with its own persistent temperature, gas contact conduction and grey radiation/conduction to an environment. No wall/piston, wall/surface or wall/spatial coupling; alternatively two nonreactive constant-volume energy nodes connected by one zero-holdup compressor or expander, using actual endpoint pressures, same-source PS/efficiency/PH calorics, finite shaft power and separate inlet/outlet enthalpy with signed work; no shaft/piston, shaft/wall, shaft/surface or shaft/spatial coupling; no piston inertia, spatial flame field or arbitrary member heat queues. Sourced finite harmonic state counting can compile one-well RRKM channels into the original energy-grain populations and bath collisions, with explicit ZPE and quantization; no rotor, tunneling or general pressure-rate reduction. Read-only single-well QSD rates, product branches and spectral gaps use current original grains and actual bath inventory or explicit fixed T/bath-pressure grids; no dynamic reduction, total-pressure PLog or new heat/inventory model. Read-only trajectory sensitivities include signed species enthalpy parameters through the original H/G/U and reverse rates; fixed-geometry gas/surface steady queries distinguish a complete finite network from explicitly held nonreacting boundary nodes, retain original residuals and solver work, and never commit the hypothetical result. lab_schedule lab_schedule Single process; finite independent closed systems with explicitly declared shared-clock strategies and atomic finite pump/membrane paths; explicit finite heater/analyzer identities with FIFO occupancy; no same-vessel hybrid or general loops. liquid_equilibrium liquid_equilibrium, isothermal-liquid-equilibrium Strict finite liquid phase equilibrium using declared component properties and supported composition domain; no silent extrapolation. mineral_kinetics mineral_kinetics, finite-calcite-kinetics Finite calcite dissolution/precipitation with fast aqueous equilibrium; fixed 298.15 K; or declared database minerals at fixed TP with fast aqueous reactions, finite seeded surface and same-reference heat/work. Database mode currently permits wait only; no mineral nucleation. molecular_process molecular_process, molecular-process-receiver Declared external source through homogeneous serial units or one recycle loop into one finite receiver; wait and snapshots; local clock only. observation observation See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. phase phase See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. programmed_chromatography programmed_chromatography Authored peak/retention response, finite sampling and persistent carryover; not a fitted universal chromatographic transport model. ro_membrane ro_membrane, finite-dilute-ro Finite ideal dilute NaCl RO at 298.15 K with deposited foulant/rinse, or declared binary/multisolute axial RO with real ion inventories, neutral transport channels, pressure loss and three finite tanks; explicit common-G aqueous thermodynamics supports isothermal pressure-work recovery, while MCAS ideal-volume and empirical Sharqawy/Nayar seawater properties use independent H/V/osmotic laws without reversible Gibbs-work recovery; seawater TDS remains a conserved kg quantity alongside molecular water; or ideal dilute multi-ion Donnan/steric/Born NF with a resolved pore and a mixed-feed 0D module; or a periodic internal AEM/CEM electrodialysis pair with two finite liquids, signed ion/water transfer and bounded CC/CV control; or explicit passive reverse electrodialysis with open/short circuit, finite resistive load, signed electrical output and isothermal bath heat; or two-tank direct-contact Knudsen membrane distillation with finite heat/cooling and signed water/energy transfer; model-specific T/P/salinity bounds and operations, no membrane holdup or full WaterTAP flowsheet. sbml sbml_model, formal-sbml-shared Formal 3D SBML quantity coordinates and supported transverse events; no declared chemical formula, carrier mass or heat model. Explicit integer direct/next-reaction/tau modes use elementary source laws, fixed source geometry and the original formal state/clock; source rules, events and constraints are not coupled in integer mode. Read-only finite-time perturbation growth for smooth autonomous reaction ODEs uses an explicit mol metric and the original stoichiometric subspace; periodic QR adds finite-duration Lyapunov estimates, while trajectory spectra distinguish decay, growth, oscillation and resolved time scales; no event/rate-rule tangents, ILDM/CSP reduction or asymptotic chaos claim. Declared source controls and readouts support finite-start constrained steady or finite-horizon optimization from the current inventory; candidate states never replace live state and no global optimum is claimed. Read-only single-parameter steady-branch continuation holds the current conservation class, uses declared amount/parameter scales, and retains stable/unstable segments, fold brackets and failed steps; no all-branch, branch-switching or periodic-orbit qualification. separation separation See the authored physical spec and runtime contract; no universal validity claim. solid_solution solid_solution, calphad_phase, binary-solid-equilibrium Finite binary equilibrium, selected native TDB/CEF phase, or declared multiphase CEF PH equilibrium with latent heat and finite thermal device; finite phase and tangent search, without global uniqueness claims. Fixed-T/P neutral vacancy-free ternary CEF sections retain requested composition nodes, tie lines/triangles and failed points; read-only world queries solve the exact current elemental composition, without interpolating continuous boundaries or replacing live inventory. sorbent_contact sorbent_contact Competitive finite sorbent kinetics, owned carrier and finite wash; explicit condensed calorics and temperature domain. stochastic stochastic, gillespie-direct Integer Gillespie direct, Gibson-Bruck next-reaction, or explicitly approximate adaptive Poisson tau-leaping with critical-channel/SSA fallback and persistent step-held pending batches; fixed volume and temperature, declared mass action, one inventory and process RNG. Fixed-partition ODE/SSA uses integrated hazards and explicit DOP853 or RK45 integration; an explicit stoichiometric-jump mode permits real molecular transfer between integer and continuous stocks with resolved molecular quanta and internal atom-transfer receipts. An explicit adaptive hybrid variant uses lossless real mol, hysteretic classification, RK4 or LSODA drift and persistent next-reaction targets with step-frozen propensities. Its fixed-volume world supports instantaneous solute dosing and nonconsuming mol measurement; consuming hybrid sampling and spatial kMC remain unsupported. An explicitly declared continuous reaction SDE uses RI5 with legacy linear or explicit fractional output, or requested-endpoint truncation before bounded feasible-side physical acceptance. Truncated output has no lookahead and wait splits can change its numerical mesh. Declared bounded inputs and representative offline aliquots invalidate lookahead while retaining the process stream; an explicit volume floor permits sampling boundaries between fixed-volume numerical intervals. surface_kinetics surface_reaction Finite owned sites; declared single/multisite mean-field mechanisms and symmetric interactions; optionally declared constant-activity aqueous chemostats and fixed potential versus SHE, with actual liquid stocks/ports, electron stoichiometry, original charge/work and bath heat. Source electronic-energy scaling and free-energy BEP table fits can author the same mechanisms with explicit known-sigma parameter uncertainty. No dynamic pH, double layer, full-cell calorimetry or spatial kMC; real-catalyst predictive accuracy requires separate validation. thermal thermal, heater_connection, owned-inventory-temperature, static-finite-carrier-stock, legacy-liquid-enthalpy Finite-power or explicitly isothermal device; shared energy accounting; manual reconnection requires one disabled heater in local-clock mode. Explicit finite-jacket P/PI/filtered PID uses actual temperature, heater-owned persistent memory and realized-power anti-windup in the original thermal/shared-clock advance; no extra controller clock, automatic tuning or implicit coupling to other model families. vacuum_concentration vacuum_concentration, finite-vacuum-concentration-enthalpy Finite variable-composition concentration with authored VLE/calorics; unsupported kinetic coupling is rejected. vapor_liquid_equilibrium vapor_liquid_equilibrium, constant-pressure-flash-enthalpy Finite TP/PH closure with explicit phase/caloric models, including simultaneous two-phase molecular PH on a declared local branch with finite thermal devices and explicit constant-pressure boundary work; no simultaneous undeclared kinetic process.

For declared action units, parameter rules, state ownership and dependencies: uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_capabilities --format json

docs.title: Optional CPU build
docs.text:
The Python backend runs without a C++ compiler. The optional C++20 build currently provides an ABI and thin bindings, with fixture operations for checking handles and single/batch calls. It does not execute the existing chemistry models in C++.

uv run --no-sync python scripts/build_cpu.py --test

Build products live in build/chemworld-cpu/. The fixture ABI supports reset, observe, step and step_batch; observe/add/scale are binding demonstrations. Base wheels do not bundle a native compiler or CPU runtime.

from chemworld.cpu import CpuBackendUnavailable, select_backend

backend = select_backend("auto")
try:
    requested = select_backend("cpu")
except CpuBackendUnavailable:
    requested = "reference"

auto chooses an executor at initialization. An execution failure does not silently switch backends. Set CHEMWORLD_CPU_LIBRARY to load an explicitly built library. Scientific capabilities still come from the shared Python module declarations; full numerical execution, state migration and performance qualification remain in development.

docs.title: Run the integrated native examples
docs.text:
These are fixed synthetic development workflows, not autonomous model campaigns or fits to real laboratory data. They use the same ChemWorldRuntime, Gym, CLI, transaction system and replay as the individual native domains. No model key or optional chemistry backend is required. Installed entry points ship in the wheel and sdist; no test helpers or repository-only configuration are imported.

From the locked repository environment:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_domains --output /tmp/native-domains
uv run --no-sync chemworld verify --submission /tmp/native-domains/heater.jsonl
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_capabilities --format json

After installing the built wheel in a virtual environment, the equivalent entry is python -m chemworld.examples.native_domains --output /tmp/native-domains. Use --workflow NAME to select one or repeat it to select several. Outputs are actual action/readout trajectories and terminal snapshots, not invented scores.

Workflow What it exercises heater One calibrated finite heater: gas surface reaction → liquid adsorption → thermal SPM battery. The same device moves, not copies. Each vessel retains its own material and elapsed local time. membrane Three process/rinse cycles on finite feed/pump/RO/permeate and wash/waste inventories; fouling persists, with no refill/reset. mineral Carbonate/calcite kinetics, finite acid input, phase-owned transfer, sampling and pH. shared-clock Independent low-copy A/B SSA and deterministic A/B vessel, two competing requests to one offline molecular counter, delayed results and persistent RNG. distillation Finite tray holdup, retained receiver, timed fraction collection, full reflux and reflux change. crystal Seeding, finite cooling/growth, filtration, resuspension, warm redissolution and a second cooling interval. solid Binary demixing → heating → cooling with local equilibrium and native phase readout. heterogeneous Four closed systems (reaction, SPM battery, adsorption and SSA) advance on one clock with a finite heater. open-closed A finite transport apparatus and a closed thermal bottle share event endpoints, including source exhaustion. device-lifecycle Multiple heaters/analyzers, FIFO contention and local material replacement while an unrelated analysis remains active.

docs.title: Device and time boundaries
docs.text:
reconnect_heater is a zero-physical-time connection action in an explicitly authored local-clock composition. Pause control first; there must be exactly one thermal device in the world and a destination with a compatible native temperature domain. Its identity, calibration and settings are retained; material does not move. Use select_vessel then heat to operate at its new destination. It does not implement robot motion, spatial collision avoidance or general instrument hot plugging. A rejected reconnection follows normal procedure-penalty semantics but does not change material, equipment or physical time.

The shared-clock workflow is different: all enabled vessels age together under the common finite scheduler. It does not couple SSA and ODE inside one vessel, and molecular capture is zero-carrier-volume Bernoulli sampling, not a liquid aliquot. Do not interpret repeated resets with the same seeds as independent runs.

Use --noise-mode keyed to select the existing keyed detector primitive. Examples use world/process seed 7 and independent observation seed 12. Each output includes the parsed composition and literal action sequence in a *-recipe.json file. The shared-clock example explicitly declares subsecond waits so a snapshot can retain a busy one-second analyzer and an unexecuted SSA event; it does not shorten the analyzer's physical analysis time.

An authored shared clock uses LabClockSpec(vessel_capacity=4, ...) to allow four independent closed thermal/SSA vessels. The default is two; the explicit integer capacity is 1–64, separate from the finite job queue capacity. The 1-, 2- and 4-vessel paths have direct functional coverage. All declared vessels evolve to the same event endpoint, including unselected vessels. Changing declaration order or selecting another vessel does not choose the numerical assembly order. One physical heater and one offline analyzer serve persistent FIFO requests. A failed slice discards sampling and RNG changes; the existing rejected-action cost/risk penalty remains in history. Open connections beyond declared finite apparatus and same-vessel ODE/SSA mixing remain unsupported. Multiple devices use explicit identities and per-device FIFO queues; choose a device when the request would otherwise be ambiguous. Local material replacement is evaluator-only and requires the affected system to be idle. It retains the shared clock, resource history, calibration and unrelated queued analyses; it is not an Agent reset action.

chemworld.examples.closed_shared_labs.reactive_closed_lab() authors four independent synthetic systems: a thermal A/B reaction, thermal SPM battery, finite adsorption contact and low-copy SSA. phase_closed_lab() combines finite crystal growth with a separate Al/Cu solid specimen. Construct a ChemWorldRuntime(composition=...) with either recipe and use select_vessel, queue_lab_heat, optional queue_lab_measure and wait. Electrical drive is an explicitly authored initial program; these recipes do not add a controller. The one finite heater moves between systems, and each model keeps its own temperature domain. An isothermal battery advances but cannot accept heating. All strategies must explicitly declare shared_clock=True; installing a module alone does not grant this capability. A physical cutoff aligns every system to that actual time and stops the laboratory. These combinations use the existing native equations and synthetic parameters; they do not establish material fits.

chemworld.examples.open_shared_labs.open_shared_lab("transport") combines the finite source–pump/pipe/heat-exchanger–receiver apparatus with a closed thermal bottle. Choose "membrane" for finite RO, retained fouling, wash/waste and a separate bottle. Select the apparatus's reactor, call set_flow_rate, then use wait to advance the complete laboratory. Select bottle and queue_lab_measure to occupy its one offline chromatograph while flow continues. The existing local run_flow action cannot introduce a second clock here.

Each finite apparatus advances once, including its source and collection containers. The configured vessel capacity counts physical containers: three for the transport example and five for the fouling membrane example. A finite source, collection limit or wash exhaustion aligns all systems to the actual stop.
