Global material, pump work and heat remain in their original ledgers; connected-system references appear in the outcome diagnostics. Extra paths, shared reservoirs, unmodelled loops and overlapping strategy ownership are rejected during compilation. These recipes reuse the original bounded flow, dilute/isothermal membrane and thermal equations.

docs.title: Residual and caloric solver choices
docs.text:
BatterySPMSpec and TransientElectrodeSpec default to numerical_form="residual". Set numerical_form="ode" to select their original ODE path explicitly. The selection is saved with the physical model and survives snapshot restoration. A residual solve failure remains a numerical failure; it does not select another algorithm.

Both paths use the same finite inventories, transport and reaction equations, energy conventions, device bounds and runtime transactions. For SPM, the residual path solves current and voltage constraints together, including constant-current, constant-voltage and finite-source current limits. Nonterminal events locate the limit transitions. Algebraic values appear in solver diagnostics and are recomputed from physical state; they are not another persistent inventory. The planar electrode retains its existing redox, diffusion and double-layer charge model and its isothermal energy scope.

The common backend reduces regular block index-1 residual systems to BDF or Radau. It is not an arbitrary-index DAE solver. Diagnostics identify analytic and finite-difference derivatives separately; the common physical assembly uses an analytic rate matrix and explicit numerical state/time derivatives.

FiniteTransportSpec.caloric_algorithm defaults to "residual", consuming the same liquid enthalpy, analytic heat capacity and apparatus heat capacity. The explicit "brentq" choice remains available. caloric_residual_system also provides native temperature responses to target energy and declared physical parameters. A missing analytic parameter derivative is reported as unavailable. None of these numerical choices expands the underlying synthetic material scope.

docs.title: Capability and validation scope
docs.text:
See the generated module table. Its source is the installed declarations and their scope notes, not a duplicate capability list. Actual numeric domains come from authored physics and device specifications and are narrowed by task permissions. Presence of two modules is not evidence that every coupling between them is supported. Small SPM, dilute 0D RO and finite binary equilibrium are not full PyBaMM, WaterTAP or CALPHAD replacements.

Export the actual bound public action ranges, material connections and installed instrument declarations for a recipe (or a raw composition file):

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_capabilities --composition /tmp/native-domains/heater-recipe.json

This reports the current task and active vessel at reset; future vessel choices or physical state changes may change availability. It reuses the runtime's public contracts, not a separate hand-maintained range table.

Validation commands:

uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_native_domains_end_to_end.py -v
uv run --no-sync python scripts/smoke_test_wheel.py --native-foundation-only --output /tmp/native-install.json

The latter builds both distributions and installs each outside the repository using locked default dependencies. It checks absence of optional upstream libraries, runs the ten examples, and verifies each trajectory in another process. This is a local installation test, not a PyPI upload or formal release. No claim is made about platforms not actually tested in the acceptance record.

The stage-A source qualification passed 10 histories x 2 noise modes x 4 actual entry points: 80 trajectories, 80 independent JSONL replays and 20 fresh-process continuations. These are separate from the Windows installation qualification: Python 3.11/3.12 x wheel/sdist, four passed units with 40 histories and 40 fresh-process replays using default sequential noise. Linux/macOS installation is deferred; its eight planned units remain unexecuted. This does not qualify every later scientific extension or establish real-material accuracy.

docs.title: Native physical sessions
docs.text: The property and source delivery catalog connects all 32 chemicals 1.5.2 public modules to native entry points, retained qualification results and separate EOS/flash responsibilities. It also lists the existing data adapters and shared sources. This is a responsibility map, not a claim of drop-in upstream API compatibility or empirical accuracy for every material. External source files remain caller-supplied; production does not import chemicals.

docs.title: Inspect and choose property methods
docs.text:
ComponentPropertyPackage.selection_report(property_id, temperature_K=..., pressure_Pa=...) lists every declared candidate, source ID, unit, temperature/pressure domain, missing input and the selection reason. It inspects declarations without trying alternative formulas. with_selection returns a new package whose choices are used by ordinary evaluation, caloric integrals, transport, virial gas and VLE.

Three policies are available:

  • PropertySelectionPolicy() preserves declaration order, preferring a candidate whose declared domain contains the requested state.
  • PropertySelectionPolicy("correlation", correlation_id) chooses that exact curve.
  • PropertySelectionPolicy("source_priority", source_priority=("b", "a")) permits only the listed source IDs and orders candidates within that shortlist. Domain compatibility is checked before priority. The list is a caller choice, not a claim about scientific quality.

If all permitted candidates are outside their declared ranges, the selected curve is still governed by the evaluator's raise/warn/ignore policy. Mathematical failure never selects another curve. A missing pressure remains a missing input, and a source shortlist with no match raises PropertySelectionError with its complete report.

This self-contained synthetic example changes which vapor-pressure curve the existing flash calculation consumes:

import json
from dataclasses import replace
from math import log

from chemworld.examples.native_flash_research import synthetic_vle_properties
from chemworld.physchem import PropertySelectionPolicy
from chemworld.physchem.flash_units import VLEPropertyPackage, tp_flash
from chemworld.physchem.property_reports import R_J_PER_MOL_K

model = synthetic_vle_properties()
light = model.packages[0]
original = light.by_property("vapor_pressure")[0]
alternative = replace(
    original, correlation_id="alternative-pressure",
    coefficients={**original.coefficients, "A": log(1e5) + 30000 / R_J_PER_MOL_K / 345},
    metadata={"source": {"source_id": "example-b"}},
)
light = replace(light, correlations=(*light.correlations, alternative)).with_selection({
    "vapor_pressure": PropertySelectionPolicy("correlation", "alternative-pressure"),
})
model = replace(model, packages=(light, model.packages[1]))
restored = VLEPropertyPackage.from_dict(json.loads(json.dumps(model.to_dict())))
result = tp_flash(restored, {"light": .5, "heavy": .5},
                  temperature_K=350, pressure_Pa=1e5)
assert result.vapor_fraction == 0
assert restored.packages[0].selection_report(
    "vapor_pressure", temperature_K=350).selected_id == "alternative-pressure"

For source-backed cards, pass selection_policies to PropertyInputCard.combine to retain overlapping alternatives, or call card.with_selection(...). Each curve's declared source must agree with its uncertainty/source envelope. Original source records and extra provenance survive selection and JSON; a contradictory segment source is rejected instead of relabelled.

ConstantDatabase.inspect_value(identity, field_id, methods=...) reports every requested method, including unavailable files, missing identities/fields/values, unknown units, ambiguous records and conflicting values. Derived data readers share this API. It also retains unevaluated correlations and temperature series; use point= for an explicit series point. IdentifierDatabase.inspect_search likewise preserves all source candidates and distinguishes missing sources from no match, multiple registry identities and structural-field conflicts. Neither diagnostic chooses a record, merges identities or downloads external data.

docs.title: Supply a reviewed component for a source identity
docs.text:
A CAS alias can hide a different stereoisomer or a superseded registry number. When the identifier tables have no exact record, pass an explicit ComponentSpec with reviewed identity evidence to the existing property input API. Do not copy the structure of the first alias search result.

The reviewed CRC component inputs cover 200 identities and 246 original dielectric/refractive-index rows. They retain the source CAS, available full InChI, cited public records, documented stereochemical scope, and explicit superseded-CAS relationships. Their default phase is unknown. These are partial, explicit inputs: they do not modify the identifier database or resolve the other 39 original missing-identity rows. Those rows remain in the 285-row denominator, with 34 explicit CAS diagnoses under source_gaps. The racemate metadata must be retained; a connectivity-only InChI alone does not specify a racemate. Vanadyl tribromide uses the exact name, CAS and VOBr3 formula in INERIS's compound table. Its optional InChI and InChIKey remain empty because that source provides neither; this does not infer a molecular graph or resolve unspecified mixtures.

examples/crc_electro_optical_inputs.py exposes inspect_source_identity(payload, cas, source_unit) and reviewed_property_input(database, payload, identity, method=..., source_point=True). Load payload with its load_inputs() helper. Source units use the fixture's original zero-based table row (for example CRC_RI/3372). The first function reports reviewed input, source gap, unreviewed row or unknown CAS; the second uses the existing native card API only for a reviewed row. SourceIdentityGapError.diagnostic retains the reason and source references. Raw source values remain queryable even when their material cannot be resolved. No alias fallback or assumed mixture ratio is introduced. This example's supplied-input policy is separate from the native API: users can still supply their own reviewed ComponentSpec to database.property_input. Functional acceptance with explicit gaps does not claim 285 complete identities.

Forty-one further inputs use EPA SRS's explicit former-to-current CAS relationship and the current CAS's complete GSRS single-center racemate definition. They retain the original CRC CAS as the input key and equal enantiomer fractions as material metadata. Conflicting original candidates and unsuccessful old-CAS searches remain in provenance. A historical-CAS relationship alone does not resolve a source-name or structural conflict. Fenchone's historical CAS is separately linked to a complete two-center GSRS racemate. Official default and SRac conversions of the original MOL verify its representative structure and racemic encoding. The component retains relative geometry, equal enantiomer fractions and the original CRC key; PubChem's generic connectivity record does not replace this material definition. Nine inputs use explicitly reviewed EPA DSSTox deposits accessed through PubChem: the deposit links the exact source CAS and material name to its standardized CID. Unsuccessful CIR lookups and unselected compound candidates remain in the input provenance.

Two further DSSTox deposits supply an explicit 4S enantiomer and a two-center racemate. The official InChI encoding of each deposited SDF corroborates its representative structure; only the racemate uses the SRac result and equal enantiomer fractions. Two further single-center racemates bind their exact CAS through explicit source annotations; their CIR results corroborate connectivity only, because the resolver reports name_by_cir, not cas_number. The CAMEO record supports a fixed 1:1 boron trifluoride/dimethyl ether adduct. Its disconnected Standard InChI is a formula-unit representation, not an arbitrary free mixture or a dissociation model. HTTP failures remain recorded.

Three inputs retain geometry from the original deposited SDF where the standardized compound loses it: trans-p-menthane, trans-1-ethyl-4-methylcyclohexane and E-azobenzene. Their exact CAS and geometry names are bound by the deposits, and the official default InChI conversion preserves the full relative-ring or azo-double-bond layer. The two 1,4-substituted rings are achiral: their /t layers do not imply a selected absolute enantiomer or a 1:1 racemate. The incomplete standardized compounds remain in provenance, together with other source candidates and failed queries.

Eight racemates with defined relative configurations use non-standard InChI=1/ identifiers with /s3, generated from the saved GSRS structures by the official InChI 1.07.5 executable with SRac. Their keys come from the same conversion. The original standard representative enantiomer remains provenance, together with every PubChem candidate; it is not used as the bulk material identity. Relative /s2 alone denotes a single enantiomer of unspecified absolute configuration and is not a replacement for the 1:1 racemate definition. No InChI executable or network service is required to consume the supplied JSON.

Where a CAS query returns several structures, the supplied input retains every candidate and the reviewed selection. Nicotine also retains the previously observed NIST stereochemistry disagreement: its explicit S assignment follows the original L-nicotine label, GSRS and corroborating material identity records. These decisions do not silently merge identifiers or repair external databases.

The two azoxybenzene isomers retain their full GSRS/ChEBI double-bond geometry; PubChem's generic candidate does not identify either specific material. Twelve additional achiral structures use explicitly reviewed NCI CIR exact-CAS records and matching, CAS-annotated PubChem candidates. All candidate structures remain in metadata; shared upstream sources are not independent laboratory validation. The E alkenes and Z-cyclododecene retain exact CAS annotations that explicitly name their geometry; opposite-geometry and mixture synonyms are not aliases. For trans-1-methyl-2-propylcyclopentane, GSRS's original structure and Sander's identity fields support the trans racemate; the conflicting PubChem cis name is retained as provenance and excluded from the material aliases.

Three further Z alkenes use explicitly reviewed Sander identity pages and full PubChem structures with exact CAS annotations. Sander attributes its structures to NIST; these are not independent measurements. For 1501-60-6, the complete-key query resolves the 2-methyl structure, while the original empty CAS query and NCI's conflicting 3-methyl structure remain provenance. Neither becomes an alias.

Eight further single-stereocenter racemates retain exact CAS annotations naming the racemate, their reviewed stereogenic atom and 1:1 enantiomer fractions. Their connectivity-only InChI does not encode that material definition by itself: the full ComponentSpec metadata and provenance must accompany the input. No absolute enantiomer is selected and no SRac conversion is claimed for this group.

Run the cis/trans example with your directory containing the original external CRC source tables:

uv run --no-sync python examples/crc_electro_optical_inputs.py SOURCE_DIRECTORY

It loads the ordinary ComponentSpec JSON, creates source-point input cards, round-trips them, and evaluates the original dielectric values before computing capacitance for an explicitly supplied example geometry. At the source's 298.2 K, cis-1,2-dibromoethene gives 7.08 and trans gives 2.88. Their distinct double-bond stereo layers survive the card JSON; cross-binding their CAS identities is rejected. The example imports no external property implementation and downloads no data. It does not extrapolate a single observation into a temperature-dependent model.

docs.title: Critical estimates as explicit inputs
docs.text:
hekayati_raeissi_critical estimates missing critical properties using molecular weight and either saturated liquid molar volume at 298.15 K or a supplied critical volume. Supply at least one of critical temperature and pressure. A supplied critical volume selects a different fitted equation from the saturation-volume route; passing an estimated volume back as Vc deliberately changes the model. Known critical values are preserved, including when both temperature and pressure are supplied. This does not reconcile inconsistent measurements.

Use estimate_critical_property to keep sources, units, component identity and the selected equation with each derived result. Select output_property when more than one field is missing. Estimates remain configuration inputs and never overwrite measured constants:

from chemworld.data.scientific_inputs import InputValue
from chemworld.physchem import (
    ComponentSpec, CubicEOSSpec, estimate_critical_property,
    eos_component_from_critical_inputs, evaluate_cubic_eos,
)

component = ComponentSpec("toluene", "C7H8", cas_number="108-88-3")
inputs = {
    "MW": InputValue(92.13842, "g/mol", None, "Explicit example input"),
    "V_sat": InputValue(.10686, "L/mol", None, "Saturated liquid at 298.15 K"),
    "Pc": InputValue(41.08, "bar", None, "Explicit example critical pressure"),
}
temperature = estimate_critical_property(
    component, method="Hekayati_Raeissi", parameters=inputs, output_property="Tc",
)
eos_component = eos_component_from_critical_inputs(
    component, Tc=temperature, Pc=inputs["Pc"],
    omega=InputValue(.2, "dimensionless", None, "Explicit example acentric factor"),
)
state = evaluate_cubic_eos(
    CubicEOSSpec("estimated", "peng_robinson", (eos_component,)), {"toluene": 1},
    temperature_K=700, pressure_Pa=1e6,
)

The fitted equations and coefficients were read from the public chemicals 1.5.2 implementation attributed to Hekayati and Raeissi (2020, DOI 10.1002/aic.17004); the original paper was not directly verified. The native implementation expands those equations independently and has no chemicals runtime dependency. Reference agreement and positive fit outputs do not establish predictive accuracy for an arbitrary material. Missing, nonpositive and nonfinite inputs are rejected; saturation-volume predictions also require a critical temperature above 298.15 K. There is no implicit source ranking, fit selection by compound name, uncertainty estimate or new EOS runtime.

docs.title: Derived parameters in finite processes
docs.text:
critical_correlation_input binds selected ConstantValue, CriticalEstimate and unit-bearing InputValue parameters to the existing volume or virial correlations. Supply the application range and an InputSource for the derived model. Each parameter's original report remains in metadata["parameter_sources"] through the property card and JSON. No measured source field is overwritten. Source aliases such as ChemSep's CriticalTemperature and CriticalVolume use the original database mapping. Their source field names and units remain in the report while the consumer converts them to SI and checks the component identity. estimate_critical_property(..., method="Zc_definition", parameters={"Tc": ..., "Pc": ..., "Vc": ...}) explicitly identifies the derived critical compressibility.

from chemworld.data.scientific_inputs import InputSource
from chemworld.physchem import critical_correlation_input
from chemworld.physchem.data_conflicts import DataSourceProvenance

model_source = InputSource(DataSourceProvenance(
    "example-derived-volume", 0, "Explicit Rackett application using estimated Tc",
    version="1", license="synthetic example",
), "synthetic")
volume_input = critical_correlation_input(
    component, family="volume", method="Yamada_Gunn",
    parameters={"Tc": temperature, "Pc": inputs["Pc"], "omega": .2},
    temperature_range_K=(300, 400), source=model_source,
)

Combine this volume card with explicitly selected heat capacity, viscosity and conductivity cards using PropertyInputCard.combine, then use the existing LiquidTransportProperties and FiniteTransportSpec. Source-backed volume fits can also consume these estimates as their declared supplemental inputs through VolumeDatabase.property_input. Source-owned coefficients cannot be overridden.

For mixtures, LiquidTransportProperties.volume_mixing_method selects Amgat (the default), Rackett_mixture, COSTALD_mixture or COSTALD_mixture_compressed. The optional volume_mixing_parameters map is keyed by the existing component IDs: Rackett needs Tcs/Pcs/Zrs; COSTALD needs Tcs/Vcs/omegas. Molecular weights come from those components. Compressed COSTALD also requires explicit saturation-pressure parameters. Provide volume_mixing_note to identify their source and scope. Each finite transfer uses the current reservoir temperature, declared pressure and actual composition; JSON snapshots retain the selection. Amgat uses the current pure volumes and rejects frozen-volume overrides. Liquid enthalpy is still the separately declared additive model, so these volume laws do not establish a complete liquid EOS.

Pure gas heating uses VirialGasThermodynamics and the original coupled solver. Its ideal heat-capacity datum can be outside the residual coefficient's domain: the ideal integral must cover its own reference path, while residual Helmholtz terms must be valid at every actual gas state. Neither domain is silently widened. Unlocated constant-volume observations retain an explicit single application temperature; solid volumes remain solid properties. They cannot supply an undeclared temperature-dependent liquid process.

docs.title: Source-backed transport inputs
docs.text:
The Lennard-Jones, viscosity, conductivity and interface databases expose 19 external source tables containing 4,573 records. Select a source explicitly: ViscosityDatabase.property_input, ConductivityDatabase.property_input, InterfaceDatabase.property_input and LennardJonesDatabase.viscosity_input return the original PropertyInputCard. Tables are read from a caller-supplied directory; native execution does not import chemicals or download missing data. Missing identities and unknown validity intervals are reported, not filled in.

PropertyInputCard.combine(cards, reference_note=...) assembles selected inputs for the same complete component declaration. It retains source and uncertainty metadata, shares identical declarations and rejects conflicting data or caloric references. Choose one correlation where the same property domains overlap; input order never selects a preferred source. A transport source alone does not provide heat capacity, density or a caloric datum. Supply those explicitly:

from chemworld.physchem.property_inputs import PropertyInputCard
from chemworld.physchem.transport_devices import FiniteTransportSpec, LiquidTransportProperties
from chemworld.world.transport_world import transport_world_spec

def source_backed_liquid_world(viscosity, conductivity, calorics_and_density, bounds):
    card = PropertyInputCard.combine(
        (viscosity, conductivity, calorics_and_density),
        reference_note="Explicit source choices and liquid enthalpy reference",
    )
    if card.reference is None:
        raise ValueError("Supply an explicit liquid enthalpy reference")
    key = card.package.component.identifier
    properties = LiquidTransportProperties(
        (card.package,), temperature_bounds_K=bounds,
        pressure_Pa=card.reference.pressure_Pa,
        caloric_references={key: card.reference},
    )
    return transport_world_spec(
        FiniteTransportSpec(properties),
        feed_mole_fractions={key: 1.0}, receiver_mole_fractions={key: 1.0},
        feed_temperature_K=300, receiver_temperature_K=300,
    )

The finite liquid apparatus consumes these curves during actual pump, pipe and heat-exchanger calculations. Mixtures use declared ideal volumes, log viscosity and DIPPR9H conductivity. The optional viscosity_pressure_parameters mapping selects Lucas for named components using critical_temperature_K, critical_pressure_Pa and acentric_factor; each affected package must also provide its vapor_pressure curve. Saturation viscosity and pressure are evaluated at the current temperature, and the actual reservoir pressure enters the correction. Missing baselines, temperatures above Tc and pressures below Psat are rejected. Input JSON and full runtime snapshots retain this declaration.

ideal_gas_transport_state(packages, amounts, T, P, references) supplies the same FluidState, molar enthalpy and total volume tuple for gas pipe and heat-transfer consumers. It uses explicit ideal-gas volume, Wilke viscosity and Wassiljewa–Herning–Zipperer conductivity; it does not imply a dense EOS or a compressible-flow solver. Amounts and reference maps use canonical component IDs. LJ binary diffusivity can feed the existing conservative finite-volume operator. Interface tension feeds Young–Laplace pressure and the pump's pressure-load function; fixed-curvature qualification does not describe dynamic wetting.

All 19 sources have process-consumption examples with independent equation checks. Supplementary properties in those examples are explicitly synthetic. Material prediction accuracy is a separate question. At large NTU, heat transfer can reach the stream-capacity limit: changing conductivity need not measurably change the outlet heat, even though the property is correctly consumed.

docs.title: Pure virial coefficients
docs.text:
virial_correlation declares seven second-virial methods (Pitzer_Curl, Abbott, Tsonopoulos, Tsonopoulos_extended, Oconnell_Prausnitz, Xiang, Meng) and two third-virial methods (Orbey_Vera, Liu_Xiang) for the existing property package and input card. For example:

from chemworld.physchem import virial_correlation, virial_temperature_report

curve = virial_correlation(
    "Tsonopoulos",
    parameters={"Tc": 425.2, "Pc": 3.8e6, "omega": 0.193},
    temperature_range_K=(300, 900),
    source_note="Explicit example critical parameters; application range chosen by caller",
)
value, first, second, third = virial_temperature_report(curve, temperature_K=510)

Inputs use K, Pa and m³/mol; B is m³/mol and C is m⁶/mol². Signed coefficients are valid. virial_derivatives and virial_fast return the value through the third temperature derivative; virial_vector and virial_matrix apply the same kernel to explicit parameter sets. They do not generate cross parameters or perform mixture rules. All parameters remain fixed during differentiation.

virial_value(..., order=-1) and order=-2 provide the documented indefinite integrals for Pitzer–Curl, Abbott and the two Tsonopoulos variants, with zero constants in the dimensional-temperature basis (log(T / 1 K)). Other methods do not declare these indefinite integrals. Normal integrate_correlation remains available for definite integrals within the declared application range.

Extended Tsonopoulos requires explicit a and b, or a polar selection with species_type and the dipole in debye where required. The default documented polar convention includes methanol and the zero-dipole alkanol limit; explicitly select convention="chemicals_1_5_2" to reproduce that API's different behavior. Meng requires explicit a, or polar={"dipole": ..., "haloalkane": ...}. Choices and source notes survive JSON. Unknown classes and conflicting choices are rejected. Xiang/Liu constants were recovered from public calls in their documented mathematical basis and checked on separate inputs; their original paper tables have not been directly verified. Development mathematical agreement does not establish material accuracy or the validity of a truncated gas EOS.

docs.title: External density and volume sources
docs.text:
chemworld.data.volume.VolumeDatabase(data_root) reads explicitly supplied Density tables and the existing ChemSep/VDI sources. It uses the same lazy identity and source database as other property inputs. Call db.volumes("64-17-5", method="PERRY_VOLUME") to inspect candidates, then db.property_input("64-17-5", component, method="PERRY_VOLUME") to obtain a normal PropertyInputCard; its evaluate_state consumes liquid density and molar_volume with the component's molecular weight.

Select curve_id if a source has multiple candidates. Missing critical inputs must be supplied in parameters; unknown temperature bounds require temperature_bounds_K. Source coefficients cannot be overwritten. CRC constant observations require application_temperature_K and application_note and remain single points. VDI tables require interpolation="linear"; missing intervals and extrapolation are rejected. These temperature paths do not imply an independent pressure equation or caloric data. Source identity and molecular weight must agree with the component. External scientific datasets are not bundled or silently discovered through an upstream library.

These development examples use the installed current runtime, without a model API key or Cantera. They describe a finite synthetic CO oxidation model, not a general chemistry predictor or a newly qualified release. Python 3.11 or 3.12 is the validation target.

For the current ten cross-domain workflows, shared-clock boundaries and the separate source/install denominators, start with native domains. Both sequential and keyed detection are supported on the qualified shared-clock histories. Explicitly declared multi-device queues and idle-system material replacement use the same runtime, transaction and continuation machinery. The sections below also describe later scientific extensions; their individual acceptance scope does not follow automatically from stage-A completion.

After installing the wheel or sdist in an isolated environment:

python -m chemworld.examples.native_surface_research --bulk --mobile --terminal-assay
python -m chemworld.examples.reuse_native_equipment

In a development checkout, prefix Python commands with uv run --no-sync. The first example feeds finite stocks, heats, measures, routes material and ends the task. --no-surface runs the same apparatus as an inert or bulk-only system; --bulk adds the declared bulk reaction. --mobile attaches a material-borne surface. Without it, the stationary surface remains on its vessel when gas moves.

The second example uses the same heater model in inert, bulk, surface and combined systems. It initializes fresh material in the reactor between two batches and checks that the retained heater keeps its identity and calibration. It also binds one compiled physical world to two tasks: direct termination and termination followed by a required final assay. Their physical response before ending agrees.

docs.title: Use the same session through other entry points
docs.text:
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.surface_world import surface_world_spec

spec = surface_world_spec(terminal_assay=True)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=spec, observation_noise_mode="keyed")
session.reset(seed=12)
result = session.execute({"operation": "add_component", "component": "CO-feed",
                          "amount_mol": 2e-5})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "gas_pressure"})
for channel in reading.observation.channels:
    print(channel.channel_id, channel.value, channel.unit, channel.quality)
session.close()

ChemWorldEnv(composition=spec) provides the Gym reset/step interface over the same runtime. chemworld.eval.runner.run_agent accepts composition=spec.to_dict() for an Agent. Both entry points retain transaction outcomes, physical duration, resource accounting and the native observation in info.

To execute JSON actions from the CLI, save spec.to_dict() as world.json and each action as a separate JSON file, then run:

chemworld render --composition world.json --seed 12 --noise-mode keyed \
  --actions feed.json pressure.json --format json --trajectory run.jsonl \
  --snapshot continuation.json
chemworld verify --submission run.jsonl

The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing trajectory or snapshot. Snapshots and trajectory provenance contain private simulator state/configuration for evaluator continuation and replay; they are not Agent observations. JSON can reorder map keys, so physical replay uses a numerical tolerance (the CLI default is 1e-5), while categorical outcomes must agree. Replay requires the original runtime semantics; current main does not substitute for frozen paper physics.

docs.title: Readings, time and reuse
docs.text:
Native channels own physical values and units, uncertainty, quality, axes and acquisition times. Invalid or unobserved channels are explicit; a valid physical reading need not fit in [0, 1]. The fixed Gym scalar view is a derived compatibility projection. Use info["native_observation"] or session results for the complete channel record. Calling observe() returns cached readings and does not acquire another sample.

In-situ acquisition advances the world through the same physical integrator. Offline analysis keeps its acquisition snapshot and accounts for analysis time separately. A task requiring a final assay first freezes production, then ends after that assay; it does not advance the frozen production vessel again.

session.snapshot().save(path) and ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(SessionSnapshot.load(path)) support private continuation with compatible bindings. session.reset() creates a fresh world. Evaluator-only reset(options={"scope": "material", "vessel_ids": ["reactor"]}) replaces that material while retaining attached stationary equipment and its calibration. Partial initialization retains clocks, budgets and RNG state; it is not a free Agent operation. SessionSnapshot is also exported from chemworld.runtime.

Current private sessions use chemworld-session-v2. Their phase identities and material coordinate order survive sorted JSON, including retained samples; pending events, apparatus queues, RNG and resource events remain part of the same continuation. Configuration comparison uses the installed model codecs. Supply the same domain_modules registry when restoring a local extension; callable names in a saved binding describe installed code and are never imports.

Older v1 sessions require an explicit SessionSnapshot.migrate_v1(payload) call. This converts the encoding only when runtime semantics match and omitted assembly order is unambiguous. Multiple records without saved order require the original ordering information. Restoration still checks the complete execution binding. Older physical-world inputs retain their supported boundary conversions; this does not authorize reinterpretation of frozen session evidence.

docs.title: Model and acceptance boundaries
docs.text:
The gas reaction, five-step surface rates, finite material transfers, shared internal-energy/heat-capacity balance and heater model are executable physics. The tests' injected numerical failure, process failure and invalid readout are interface fixtures, not implemented failure mechanisms. Thermal stopping uses a real event. Property tables and rate parameters are finite synthetic contracts. Surface flow, arbitrary thermodynamics and new electrode kinetics remain outside this foundation slice.

The native acceptance covers fixed native/Gym/CLI/Agent histories, both observation noise modes, direct/assay endings, replay and retained equipment. Installation checks build both archives and run the installed modules outside the checkout, with Cantera absent and model keys removed from the child environment. Reported platform results apply only to actual runs; this is development acceptance, not a formal release or a claim of general chemical validity. See distribution boundaries for packaging and frozen releases.

docs.title: Properties at the current state
docs.text:
ComponentPropertyPackage.evaluate_state(...) evaluates a pure state; evaluate_property_state(packages, amounts_mol, ...) evaluates a composition. Both use the existing component IDs, declared aliases and CAS identifiers. Supply temperature_K, pressure_Pa, phase and the requested quantities. The report retains units and validity warnings for each property. For example:

from chemworld.physchem.curated_properties import curated_property_package

report = curated_property_package("7732-18-5").evaluate_state(
    temperature_K=400, pressure_Pa=1000, phase="gas",
    quantities=("cp", "enthalpy", "internal_energy", "density"),
)
cp = report.properties["cp"].quantity().to("J/(mol*K)")

Energy values are molar J/mol, heat capacities J/(mol K), volume m³/mol and mass density kg/m³. The default caloric datum is explicitly sensible H=0 at 298.15 K; it supplies no formation enthalpy or absolute entropy. Supply a CaloricReference when another datum is needed. Entropy and chemical potential require an entropy datum. The six curated packages currently supply gas Cp and vapor pressure; their default material phase does not imply liquid Cp or transport data. Missing quantities raise an error.

Gas states default to the ideal-gas closure. An explicit existing CubicEOSSpec selects PR/SRK volume, fugacity, departures and derivatives on the requested gas/liquid root. This is a single-phase evaluation; phase equilibrium belongs to the flash model. Its Cp derivative follows the selected outer root and does not support root-topology changes. validity_policy="warn" or "ignore" can evaluate beyond a correlation range, but this API retains the invalid-domain record under either policy.

Native reactor and equipment consumers can share PropertyPackageThermodynamics with SpeciesCaloricModel data. They obtain U(n,T), Cv and composition derivatives from the same evaluations at the current candidate state. The common integrator owns time and heat accounting; material mixing solves the same U relation for temperature. Accepted states and authored operating intervals must remain inside the declared caloric domain. This additive caloric runtime does not claim a nonideal closed-volume EOS balance. Existing constant-Cv declarations delegate to this evaluation path; the older liquid volumetric-Cp model and fixed-capacity phase plateaus remain explicitly selected models. Variable-caloric phase change requires a flash/latent closure.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.state_property_research in an installed environment for a property query and an actual variable-Cv reactor history. Its temperature dependence is synthetic and retains the original native U datum; it is an interface example rather than new material data. Production evaluation imports no reference backend. The optional physchem-ref tools are used only for the separate same-equation and model-bias checks documented in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_PROPERTY_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: TP/PH flash and finite phase inventories
docs.text:
VLEPropertyPackage combines existing property packages, explicit gas enthalpy references and a declared liquid activity model. tp_flash(...) updates K from the current liquid and vapor compositions; an optional existing gas EOS updates vapor fugacity and departure enthalpy. Liquid enthalpy is the temperature derivative of the same Psat/activity free energy, sharing the gas datum. ph_flash(..., pressure_Pa=..., enthalpy_J=...) holds total H fixed and solves T. Pure saturation uses an enthalpy lever rule. Missing/vanished phases carry zero inventory. Unreachable H and nonconvergence raise explicitly.

TP returns a state query when no inlet H is supplied; its heat duty is then unavailable. With explicit feed_enthalpy_J, TP reports the heat required to maintain the specified T. PH reports zero added heat and its actual enthalpy residual. It does not close the balance by assigning the residual to a heater.

This first slice supports one liquid plus one gas, two/three components and a convex ideal liquid or certified convex binary Margules liquid. Other activity models and uncertified/nonconvex liquids require the separate LLE/stability solver. Critical transitions and three-phase states are outside this model. The Raoult liquid thermodynamic model neglects liquid volume/Poynting work; its nominal liquid holdup is a separate geometric filling approximation. No exact liquid internal-energy/PV-work balance is claimed.

FlashSystemSpec declares a finite constant-pressure thermal system. A native vapor_liquid_equilibrium component selects its enthalpy strategy through the existing physical advance coordinator. Candidate H is integrated once, PH closes each candidate, and accepted liquid/gas quantities occupy the normal phase ledger. The normal device, feed, material routing, measurement, transaction, resource and snapshot services consume that same inventory. Registered liquid species explicitly declare their carrier representation, preventing a second legacy solvent-volume inventory from being inferred from geometric volume. Element and carrier balance checks remain active.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_flash_research for a PH query followed by actual finite feeding, cross-phase heating, a timed phase probe, transfer and termination. phase_state is an explicitly noiseless synthetic sensor, not a claim of experimental phase identification. See workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_FLASH_ACCEPTANCE.md for the fixed 27-state thermo comparison and development boundaries.

docs.title: Molecular multiphase equilibrium and finite thermal exploration
docs.text:
chemworld.physchem.MolecularMultiphaseSpec declares one MolecularCaloricModel, named density basins, temperature/pressure bounds and an explicit phase budget. solve_molecular_multiphase(spec, amounts_mol, inputs={"T": 300, "P": 600000}) returns actual phase amounts, densities, caloric totals and stability diagnostics. The same entry accepts P/H, P/S, U/V and declared mass/volume coordinates. H, S, U and V are totals for the supplied material; mass-specific inputs use explicit molar masses. Check success and the diagnostics before consuming a result. Finite composition/density searches do not certify global uniqueness.

For a live environment, map each possible phase to a MolecularPhaseTarget in MolecularMultiphaseInventorySpec. Several liquid targets may share a density basin. equilibrate_molecular_multiphase_inventory updates selected material in the existing PhaseLedger, removes vanished phases and preserves unrelated stock and failed transactions. molecular_multiphase_stream reads the selected live phase. Solver candidates and stored observations are not separate inventories.

MolecularMultiphaseThermalSpec declares a fixed pressure or fixed volume. chemworld.world.molecular_multiphase_world.build_molecular_multiphase_world combines it with explicit initial material, H or U, component formulas and a finite ThermalDeviceSpec. The returned composition goes directly into ChemWorldRuntime(composition=composition) for ordinary heat, wait, measure with phase_state, and JSON snapshot continuation. At fixed pressure the runtime records PΔV once; at fixed volume it advances U with zero boundary work. This thermal world supports phase appearance/disappearance within its declared model and bounds; continuous material feeds/transfers are not declared by this strategy.

MolecularPhaseBoundarySpec provides bubble/dew points, isolated binary azeotropes and pseudo-arclength envelopes, including turning points. Its local-coexistence mode is explicitly distinct from a finite stability search. An optional MolecularSolidBoundarySpec maps molecular chemical potentials and atom counts to the original solid-equilibrium API with explicit element-reference shifts. It supplies onset tangents and solid-consumer seeds, not a coupled fluid/solid precipitation inventory.

The current development qualification covers explicit PR mixtures and analytic regular-solution controls, original runtime consumers and the solid interface. It does not qualify every EOS or every state in a declared rectangular domain.

docs.title: Molecular interfaces from current phase inventories
docs.text:
chemworld.runtime.molecular_interface_from_state(state, inventory_spec, influence, ...) queries a named pair of phases in the current WorldState. Pass the same MolecularMultiphaseInventorySpec (or MolecularPhaseEquilibriumSpec) used by the environment. The query takes its EOS from that declaration and reads the current temperature, pressure, amounts and phase volumes. It checks phase identity, type, density basin and coexistence; a vanished or changed phase is never replaced with a cached equilibrium result.

For a pure fluid, provide interior_density_grid; for a freely varying mixture profile, provide a planar DiffusionMesh and explicit component-density bounds. SquareGradientInfluence declares constant positive-definite coefficients. PolynomialSquareGradientInfluence declares temperature-dependent pure coefficients and pair interactions; SingularSquareGradientInfluence explicitly declares a deficient-rank gradient factor. Their JSON declarations are decoded by molecular_influence_from_dict. A singular model does not acquire artificial diagonal gradient energy to make it numerically invertible.

Check result.interface.success and its stationarity, curvature and resolution diagnostics. Optional area_m2 returns surface_excess_grand_potential_J = gamma*A. This is an excess grand potential, not internal energy or heat; the query does not advance time or write any ledger. An environment author can expose the computed response through an explicitly designed tool or instrument. The query itself is not a timed measurement or a capillary-flow process.

fit_molecular_influence fits explicitly selected pure coefficients or pair interactions using uncertainty-weighted training observations and bounded parameters. It reports failed forward trials, training sensitivity rank and condition, active bounds, local covariance and held-out prediction errors. Optimizer success and predictive applicability are separate results. The current real-data development block uses Rolo et al.'s alkane measurements in saturated air and explicitly approximates the boundary by hydrocarbon VLE with no noncondensable air; its errors must be read with that modeling assumption.

The current consumer checks track the extension in development. Full multicomponent/source and real-data fitting qualification remains under parent29 until all required blocks finish.

docs.title: Strict liquid stability and finite washing
docs.text:
liquid_tpd_minimum(activity_model, composition, temperature_K=...) minimizes the actual tangent-plane distance on a deterministic set of simplex starts. equilibrate_liquids(activity_model, amounts_mol, temperature_K=...) minimizes constrained mixing Gibbs energy, refines equality of phase chemical potentials, checks component balances and repeats TPD searches on both resulting phases. A stable feed returns one liquid. A remaining negative post-split TPD rejects an unsupported additional phase. Binary/ternary models support at most two liquids; the finite numerical search is not a proof of exhaustive global optimization for arbitrary activity functions.

mixing_chemical_potentials_RT reports ln(x_i gamma_i), relative to the common pure-liquid standard and divided by RT. Common pure reference terms cancel across equal-T liquid phases; these are not fabricated absolute chemical potentials. Activity coefficients use the existing parameter model, shared with the property and contact calculations.

StrictLiquidSystemSpec declares an isothermal material law, component molar holdups and finite wash policy. A liquid_equilibrium component and matching CompositionPhysics.liquid_models entry enable the normal mix/wash, feed, clock, measurement, material routing and snapshot services. Actual wash liquid comes from a finite named supply; discarded material is an explicit molecular outlet. A miscible wash retains one mixed liquid. Droplet entrainment uses the same inventory transfer function as the empirical contact model. The phase probe reports liquid count and second-liquid fraction as synthetic native channels. Mixing heat and PV work remain explicitly unmodeled in this isothermal slice; no heat-control operation is implied.

The older distribution-coefficient contact model remains a separate model. Its minimum_tpd_like includes an empirical partition drive and is explicitly marked thermodynamic_stability_certified=False. Strict liquid equilibrium does not use that drive or fall back to it after a solver failure.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_liquid_research for finite mixing, washing, a timed observation, transfer and termination. The example's Margules parameters and component identities are synthetic. See workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_LLE_ACCEPTANCE.md for common-tangent, ternary and actual PhasePy validation.

docs.title: Conservative diffusion primitive
docs.text:
chemworld.physchem.finite_volume provides planar and spherical one-dimensional Fick operators in SI units. DiffusionMesh defines physical volumes and face areas; ConservativeDiffusion.evaluate(amounts_mol) returns molar derivatives and signed face rates without advancing time. Positive prescribed boundary flux means outward flux in mol/(m² s). A spherical center requires symmetry.

operator.couple(existing_inventory_keys, process_id=..., owner_id=..., boundary_enthalpies_J_mol=...) supplies a process and material ports to an existing CoupledSystem. Explicit boundary enthalpies are required for open boundaries. BDF/Radau use the assembled sparse stencil; outward fixed-flux depletion stops at its actual event. The caller retains inventory ownership. This is the shared spatial primitive for subsequent electrode/particle models; these mathematical consumers do not implement a battery or a new PDE runtime.

docs.title: Finite dynamic distillation
docs.text:
DynamicColumnSpec reuses ShortcutColumnSpec for the hardware envelope and VLEPropertyPackage for the thermodynamic law. It has 2–8 equilibrium trays, a finite reboiler, condenser and product collector. Each compartment advances actual component amounts and H; task-18 PH closes its phase allocation at each candidate. Vapor withdrawal and liquid overflow use declared finite holdup laws. Heat and material streams enter one shared BDF advance. This model excludes full tray hydraulics, pressure-drop networks and simultaneous reactions.

A dynamic_distillation component and matching CompositionPhysics.column_models entry select this strategy. dynamic_column_world_spec(spec, initial, ...) constructs a native apparatus from explicitly supplied properties and initial inventories. Real distill, heat/wait and timed observations use the common coordinator; dry, flood, temperature, collection and native vessel-volume boundaries stop at their actual roots. Product history records actual collector increments over time. collect_fraction moves actual liquid n and H into its separate retained phase; it never resets the column or manufactures recovery.

Distill controls are target temperature, duration and finite reflux_ratio. Native event JSON additionally accepts numeric full_reflux: 1 (with the usual required reflux field present); full_reflux: 0 resumes finite collection. The unchanged fixed Gym numeric carrier explicitly rejects this additional field and directs callers to event JSON. The old distillation component remains a labelled shortcut_estimate, without stage histories or a fallback from failed dynamic integration.

PhaseLedger alone owns bulk n. Material and stationary support H occupy separate typed slots. Replacing material retains apparatus heat and device calibration, then equilibrates the new fluid plus retained body through PH. Batch reset uses the declared initial thermal boundary while retaining hardware settings. Snapshots retain all compartments and controls. The synthetic phase probe observes the reboiler compartment. Liquid volume remains the geometric holdup approximation of task 18, with no exact liquid U/PV-work claim.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_distillation_research for five actual actions: distill, timed measurement, finite collection, reflux change and stop. The example needs no optional reference packages. Its Cp, latent heat and vapor pressure data are explicitly synthetic. The fixed dynamic grid, IDAES MESH steady comparisons, Fenske limit and time refinement are documented in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_DYNAMIC_DISTILLATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite vacuum concentration
docs.text:
CoupledConcentrationSpec uses the same state-dependent VLE properties and PH closure as flash and distillation. A finite pot and receiving bottle each own component inventory and H. Actual retained pot vapor supplies the withdrawal port. The existing equipment capture fraction routes vapor to the bottle; uncaptured vapor crosses an explicit component/H boundary. Captured vapor remains bottle inventory until PH and the finite cooling port condense it. There is no separate instantaneous condensate calculation or latent-heat debit.

A vacuum_concentration component and matching CompositionPhysics.concentration_models entry select the strategy. concentration_world_spec(spec, initial, ...) constructs a native apparatus. concentrate enables heating and vapor transport. Heat/wait and timed in-situ measurements continue the same physical advance. Heater pause leaves the transport setting unchanged. An operating stop closes transport and heat at its actual root; subsequent passive measurement can cool the bottle. Duration exhaustion with an unmet solvent endpoint is a valid result.

Pot, bottle, condenser gas saturation, residual liquid, target recovery, temperature and vessel volume are finite boundaries. Accepted time, heater delivery, cooling and outlet integrals settle once. Native material receipts authenticate the capture split, component withdrawal and transported enthalpy; reusing an action name does not authorize a new outlet. Numerical failures roll back current material, H and time. PhaseLedger owns all current bulk material; typed material and vessel slots distinguish fluid H from stationary heat capacity. Material replacement retains body heat and calibration, and PH reconciles the fresh charge without advancing time. Snapshots retain actual inventories, controls and cumulative boundary receipts.

An explicitly nonvolatile component uses a liquid Cp/H reference at the model pressure and exactly zero gas allocation. Missing gas properties remain unavailable. The shared RR report retains a trace liquid fraction independently when its vapor fraction rounds to one; the undefined beta=1 objective is null for positive nonvolatile material. This slice supports ideal mixtures with one or two volatile species and an optional nonvolatile target, at fixed pressure, without simultaneous reactions. Liquid volume remains a declared geometric holdup approximation; liquid PV/Poynting work is neglected.

simulate_vacuum_concentration(CoupledConcentrationRequest(...)) and the native operation use the same contribution and common compartment solver. Existing VacuumConcentrationRequest inputs explicitly prescribe a fixed evaluated operating profile. Their differential approximation remains labelled declared_fixed_operating_profile, shares phase-advection and solver utilities, and is never a fallback for a failed native solve. Its legacy service now charges actual elapsed time and delivered heat, including early stops.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_concentration_research for concentrate, timed measurement, heater pause, wait and termination. The source/installable example uses synthetic properties and needs no optional reference package. The fixed nine-control grid, two material fixtures, Rayleigh holdup limit and native snapshot continuation are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_CONCENTRATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Persistent finite sorbent contact
docs.text:
SorbentKineticsSpec supplies competitive Langmuir affinities, local LDF rates and adsorption energies. Fluid concentration and temperature come from the same candidate used by CoupledSystem; bound molecules enter its inventory once. Temperature-dependent affinity and bulk/bound U offsets must use the same adsorption energy. Carrier heat capacity joins the common temperature balance; no separate adsorption heat is charged. Unequal component mobilities use the documented finite-vacancy uptake constraint to preserve shared sites. This is a zero-dimensional, single-site-class liquid contact with two competing components, without axial bed, pressure-drop or intraparticle resolution.

sorbent_contact components select CompositionPhysics.sorbent_models and the existing coupled thermal strategy. A fixed carrier owns its loading in an equipment slot; a mobile carrier moves actual mass, sites, heat capacity and bound molecules with its material portion. Material replacement retains fixed loading and apparatus heat, mixing fresh material through the common U model. Actual dry/heat/wait advances share one clock and solver. Solver failure rolls back fluid, loading, temperature and physical time; established failed-action cost/risk penalties still apply.

CondensedBackgroundSpec explicitly defines volumetric Cv and U for an L-only carrier, with condensed PV/Poynting work neglected. It does not invent molecular carrier or gas data. A native sorbent fixture must declare a finite carrier source vessel. Existing add_solvent debits that actual stock and transports its energy; routing carries solute U, carrier U and mobile bound material. The static wash source has no active thermal process. Source exhaustion rejects the input, and normal material/batch initialization preserves finite supplies. Explicit entity replacement and new-world reset remain lifecycle boundaries.

The legacy standalone isothermal drying request now delegates to the same instantaneous finite-fluid LDF contribution. It retains an explicit finite fresh bed request and the final spent outlet, without certifying unprovided caloric data. The legacy laboratory runtime owns a 20 g unused-media kit per vessel; each actual dry packet debits it and leaves through an authenticated kg entity receipt. Repeated dry or material reset cannot manufacture fresh media. No second current spent-bed stock is maintained.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_sorbent_research for eight existing operations through adsorption, finite wash, heating, timed measurement and stop. All constitutive data are explicitly synthetic. The fixed 12-condition contact grid, independent equilibrium references and three native cycles are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_SORBENT_REGENERATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite transient working electrode
docs.text:
electrode_world_spec() creates a native finite planar O + e ↔ R system. The shared conservative diffusion operator and CoupledSystem advance both species profiles, Butler–Volmer exchange and double-layer charge together. The Robin boundary includes the first half-cell diffusion resistance; the outer boundary is closed. Positive current is anodic. Material and signed charge relations are checked before a candidate is returned for transaction validation. Electrical work is recorded, without claiming complete cell energy closure or counterelectrode chemistry.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.electrode_world import electrode_world_spec

session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=electrode_world_spec())
session.reset(seed=7)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control", "potential_V": 0.1})
session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 5})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "electrical_meter"})
print(reading.observation.native_record())

Set ramp_duration_s on the control action for a linear potential ramp from the current setpoint. Configuration does not advance time; wait and the meter's one-second in-situ acquisition use the same physical coordinator. Measurements expose terminal V and total A, without internal concentrations or interfacial potential. This synthetic meter is noiseless and nonconsuming.

Profiles live once in material phase compartments. Charge and cumulative electrical work belong to the electrode equipment; material reset preserves them, while explicit equipment replacement leaves the actual electrolyte profile intact. Snapshots preserve the control programme, inventories and charge. Static equipment supplies remain separate from moving liquid; dynamic or unsupported material state still requires a compatible advance strategy.

The first model uses constant diffusivities, sufficient supporting electrolyte, isothermal operation and finite series resistance. It excludes migration, convection, homogeneous reactions, current control and full-cell thermal physics. Existing fixed diffusion-layer and RC models remain explicit simpler alternatives sharing the same electrochemical constants and BV factors.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_electrode_research for three controls, waits and native measurements followed by termination. Fixed numerical checks and development failures are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_ELECTRODE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Programmed chromatography and persistent instrument state
docs.text:
chemworld.world.chromatography_world.chromatography_world_spec("hplc") (or "gc") creates a finite synthetic three-analyte world with source bottles, a receiver, material routing, waste and one persistent chromatograph. It uses the same runtime, resource ledger, measurement records, snapshots and replay as other native worlds; no model provider or API key is required.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.chromatography_world import chromatography_world_spec

session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=chromatography_world_spec("hplc"))
session.reset(seed=12)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_chromatography",
                 "instrument": "programmed_hplc", "program_index": 1})
# Initially the receiver contains blank solvent. Route a finite source aliquot
# into it to measure a standard or sample (see the complete example below).
result = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "programmed_hplc"})
print(result.observation.channel("peak_1_area"))

Program 0 is constant (298.15 K, HPLC mobile-phase fraction 0.2); program 1 ramps over 30 s to fraction 0.8 for HPLC or 338.15 K for GC. Program 2 uses knots at 0, 15 and 30 s, reaching 20% of that change at 15 s. These programmes reuse the existing retention equations, with explicit programme delay and a time-integrated elution criterion; the constant case regresses to the existing isocratic/isothermal method. Curves reuse the Gaussian peak basis.

Each acquisition consumes 0.0002 L, costs 0.05 currency and adds 60 s of offline analysis time without evolving the host. Actual analyte residue belongs to an equipment-owned state slot. A blank washes this inventory into the recorded external waste outlet; it is not a reset. Use count, gain/baseline drift, programme and calibration persist through material replacement and snapshot restore. Full reset restores the declared initial instrument.

The public record contains a signal curve, fitted peak areas and concentration estimates with units and quality, plus the declared peak templates and response calibration needed to reproduce the inverse fit without simulator state. This finite instrument assumes known peak identities/shapes; it does not identify an unknown retention mechanism. calibrate_chromatography records the last acquired public peak areas with declared standard_1_M, standard_2_M and standard_3_M; at least three standard acquisitions fit the existing response calibration. It does not inspect hidden concentrations, detector gain or baseline. Saturation, overlap and incomplete elution invalidate estimates, not completed sampling. Re-reading cached observations consumes no sample, time or random draw.

Run the complete standard–sample–blank sequence twice for both instruments and all three programmes, including JSONL replay and independent residue/waste checks:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.programmed_chromatography --output /tmp/chromatography-example

Choose a new output directory; existing results are never overwritten. The same module runs from an installed wheel. This is a finite development example, not a fitted real column: three synthetic analytes, symmetric peaks, lumped residue, fixed offline duration and a non-evolving host. Continuous mobile-phase usage, column spatial transport and instrument thermal utilities are not modelled, so no energy-closure or general gradient-column claim is made. See development acceptance.

docs.title: Native single-particle lithium battery
docs.text:
battery_world_spec() installs a finite battery with one spherical particle population per electrode. Each population uses the same conservative diffusion operator as the planar electrode. An internal lithium transfer couples the two surfaces to the applied current; voltage follows the synthetic OCV curves and symmetric Butler–Volmer overpotentials. Current, lithium and delivered electrical work advance in the common solver, with actual surface and voltage cutoff events.

from chemworld.physchem.battery_models import BatterySPMSpec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.battery_world import battery_world_spec

spec = BatterySPMSpec()
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=battery_world_spec(spec))
session.reset(seed=4)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control",
                 "current_A": spec.current_at_c_rate(0.5)})
session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 600})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "battery_meter"})

The same electrical-control action accepts exactly one supported quantity: current_A or potential_V for this battery, potential_V for the finite working electrode. Both share scalar ramp interpolation and the native meter contract; a source rejects modes and limits it does not support. Positive battery current means discharge. C-rate is defined from the initial usable lithium capacity, not recomputed from subsequent measured capacity. The native meter exposes only terminal V and A. Its one-second acquisition advances the same battery state.

Lithium profiles, signed charge and work belong to the battery equipment and are saved only once. Material reset retains them; replacing the actual battery requires explicit new device state. A surface cutoff preserves the real elapsed time and inventory. Reconfiguring to zero current allows subsequent relaxation. The shared ledger uses positive electrical work into the system, so delivered battery work is recorded with the opposite sign.

The default parameters are synthetic and use uniform unresolved electrolyte. The default isothermal option remains available; electrolyte transport remains unresolved, and the optional finite SEI extension is described below. Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_research for a discharge/rest/recharge history. PyBaMM is used only by the optional reference block; the ordinary installation runs this example without it. Numerical scope, all development failures and fixed comparisons are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_BATTERY_SPM_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Released Chen2020 parameters in the original SPM
docs.text:
battery_parameter_set("Chen2020", version="PyBaMM-25.4.2") reads a bundled, immutable catalog of all 94 released entries: 86 numerical inputs, six named constitutive functions and two metadata entries. Every field retains its source, unit and explicit consumed or retained-not-consumed classification. Production does not import PyBaMM or execute external parameter callbacks.

from chemworld.physchem import battery_parameter_set

parameters = battery_parameter_set()
cell = parameters.build_spm(maximum_current_A=10.0, radial_cells=64)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=battery_world_spec(cell))
session.reset(seed=4)

This projection is a single-material, fixed-temperature, fixed-electrolyte SPM without heat or side reactions. It derives particle volumes, reaction areas, initial lithium and exchange-current coefficients from the source values. The separately sourced OCV endpoint convention applies its clipped coordinate to both the material expression and rational barrier. The declared cell envelope occupies 0.0242 L; active volumes still determine lithium capacity. Snapshots verify the parameter binding against the actual physical declaration. Other material sets and concentration-dependent transport consumers remain open.

parameters.current_at_nominal_c_rate() uses the source's nominal 5 Ah. The existing cell.current_at_c_rate() keeps its initial usable stoichiometric capacity convention; neither is a measurement of voltage-window capacity. The caller declares the source current limit explicitly: the released default 5 A current is not an equipment limit. Queue, meter, signed work and reset semantics remain those of the original battery runtime. Full dynamic source qualification is recorded separately from catalog and functional checks.

docs.title: Cycles and a consistent synthetic thermal model
docs.text:
Pass BatterySPMSpec(thermal=BatteryThermalSpec(...)) to evolve temperature. The cell's chemical energy is integrated from the same linear OCV functions, and the common solver balances terminal electrical work, chemical storage, heater input and ambient loss. Kinetic, ohmic and diffusion dissipation are independently derived and checked; they are not added again as reaction heat. The OCV curves have no explicit temperature dependence, so reversible entropy heat is zero. Positive OCV slopes are excluded from this convex thermal model. series_resistance_ohm optionally adds actual voltage drop and Joule heating.

battery_world_spec(spec, thermal_device=ThermalDeviceSpec(...)) attaches the existing heater or isothermal bath. heat, wait and thermal pause/resume use that same device; stirring_speed_rpm is optional on heat. A finite-power heater changes actual temperature gradually. An ideal bath must start at its setpoint and records its actual compensation heat.

Use queue_electrical_stage with exactly one of current_A/potential_V, a finite stage_duration_s, and optionally one native terminal condition: stop_voltage_below_V, stop_voltage_above_V, or stop_abs_current_A. Zero-current stages are rests. Stages append to the source-owned queue; wait advances the common controller, whose interval loop also serves the existing thermal/gas programmes. No battery-specific scheduler is installed. Completed queues switch to zero current. Explicit configure_electrical_control clears the queue and installs a manual step/ramp. Voltage control solves for the current from the actual profile; an unreachable voltage remains at the source current limit, with the actual voltage and limit status recorded.

Each stage transition records the terminal reading and actual elapsed time. Physical cutoff events retain the reached state; numerical failures roll back the complete candidate action, including preceding candidate stages, while retaining diagnostics. Snapshots preserve the queue, cursor, temperature and inventories exactly. Material initialization is an evaluator boundary: it retains battery SOC/profiles and uses the declared initial temperature, recorded in its lifecycle receipt. Continuous cycling uses no such initialization.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_cycles for two CC/CV/rest/charge cycles. The nine thermal comparisons against optional PyBaMM and two native cycles are documented in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_BATTERY_THERMAL_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite SEI growth and retained degradation
docs.text:
Add sei=SEISpec() to BatterySPMSpec to enable solvent-diffusion-limited SEI. The explicit total reaction is 2 Li + EC -> Li2CO3 + C2H4, corresponding to two lithium ions and two electrons at the negative interface. EC, carbonate, retained ethylene and both active-lithium profiles live once in the cell's equipment slot. Film thickness and resistance are derived from carbonate stock; there is no independent thickness inventory or per-cycle capacity decrement.

The side current is -2 F r. Negative intercalation carries I + 2 F r, while the positive electrode carries I. Both the particle boundary and negative BV relation use that main current. Film resistance changes measured terminal voltage. Its dissipation and reaction heat use the same chemical state function as the thermal model. The irreversible side process stops at its electrochemical driving-force boundary; high-rate or unfavorable conditions are not silently extrapolated into an endergonic growth regime.

The initial film is explicitly present in the initial elemental inventory. A closed cell consumes its actual finite EC; no hidden solvent reservoir is used. The analytic maintained-solvent check adds a declared external feed instead. Species formulas make Li/C/H/O checks meaningful at the runtime transaction. Material initialization preserves the whole cell's chemical history; replacing the cell uses a new explicit equipment inventory. Snapshot and Agent replay retain film, solvent, gas, active lithium, electrical controls and temperature.

The source queue bounds pending work at 32 stages. Completed stages remain in operation history and are removed from the pending list when new work is added; stage_index remains absolute and stage_offset locates the retained list. Thus repeated finite programmes do not exhaust a lifetime queue limit.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_degradation for ten continuous native cycles. The synthetic model includes finite solvent, film resistance and the two-electron accounting; it excludes plating, cracking, electrolyte transport and gas-pressure mechanics. Fixed analytic, nine-condition PyBaMM and ten-cycle checks are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_BATTERY_SEI_ACCEPTANCE.md. Windowed discharge charge and lost-lithium equivalent charge are reported separately: neither is used as a direct substitute for the other.

docs.title: Finite pump, pipe and heat-exchanger transport
docs.text:
transport_world_spec() installs a real finite feed and receiver connected by a bounded pump, pipe and optional Ergun bed resistance. set_flow_rate sets a request in mL/min without advancing time; run_flow or wait advances both inventories together. Zero request stops pumping. run_flow may set the utility temperature through target_temperature_K; otherwise the installed value is used.

The pump solves the greatest flow permitted by the requested rate, pressure head and shaft-power limits. PumpSpec and pump_operating_point accept the connected device's monotone pressure-load law for reuse by a membrane. The example reaches about 12.21 mL/min for a 20 mL/min request and stops at the finite pickup heel without charging the unexecuted time tail.

The common finite-inventory solver advances component amounts and enthalpy. Liquid properties use native packages at the candidate T/x; the exchanger uses the actual mass rate after pump heating. Hydraulic work heats the fluid, shaft inefficiency is explicit external loss, and utility heat uses the existing Nu/U/NTU functions. Source and receiver share pressure and elevation; the pipe/exchanger has negligible holdup and the utility is a declared constant temperature boundary, not an untracked coolant inventory.

Material slots own fluid enthalpy; vessel slots own container heat. The pump owns its specification and control. Default batch initialization preserves the finite feed and its local age. Explicit receiver material replacement retains the actual container heat and recloses temperature without advancing time. Source exhaustion, full receiver and outlet property limits stop the process; numerical failure rolls back the candidate with a diagnostic.

flow_meter reports mL/min, Pa, W, K and L through native channels. Native, Gym, CLI and Agent interfaces share execution, accounting and exact replay. Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_liquid_transport. The bounded synthetic model excludes reactions, recirculation, cavitation, two-phase flow and an empirical industrial pump curve. Existing spatial PFR experiments retain their declared geometry model. Validation and optional fluids/ht comparisons are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_TRANSPORT_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite crystal growth and dissolution
docs.text:
crystal_thermal components install CompositionPhysics.crystal_models beside an explicit thermal model. Existing seed, cool_crystallize, heat, wait, filter and resuspend operations advance the same finite slurry at its actual temperature. A requested setpoint supplies bounded heating or cooling; it does not allocate dissolved molecules in advance. PhaseLedger owns current bulk molecules. Cohort constituent rows decompose the solid into particle counts, diameters, seed provenance and occluded impurity; they are not additional stock.

The declared van't Hoff curve and finite radial growth/recession law share liquid/solid caloric references. One rate/energy assembler and ODE backend advance material, temperature and utility integrals. Geometry coordinates have units m and mol/mol, reconstructing actual molecular stocks for each candidate. Zero-diameter roots remove hosts and release their actual occluded material. Finite impurity capture tapers only below the serialized inventory resolution (default 1e-8 of total impurity); actual remaining stock and numerical corrections are retained and checked against unchanged independent balances.

Nucleation uses explicit temporal birth quadrature, normally 30 s: actual molecules enter nucleus-size reservoirs and join growing cohorts at interval ends. This finite-resolution approximation has a separate interval-refinement check. There is no aggregation, breakage, polymorph or axial population model. Authored condensed Cv and U require negligible condensed PV work; missing phase calorics remain unavailable. Simultaneous bulk reaction and crystal thermal processes are outside this slice.

The native ideal filter retains all particles, solid target, seed and occluded impurity, and 8% wet mother liquor. Its 480 s advances the same active thermal control. Resuspension stores historical filtrate at its own temperature and mixes declared incoming carrier through U, without instant dissolution. Existing resource cards limit fresh carrier and seed. Material replacement retains apparatus heat; snapshots retain cohorts, controls and resource continuation. Current container transfers require equal temperatures when mixing occupied native crystal compartments. Numerical failure rolls back physical state and time, retaining the established failed-action penalties.
