The legacy laboratory slurry also uses the finite radial contribution, with its explicit condensed enthalpy boundary. Its carrier Cp is not relabelled Cv. The legacy 96%/92% mechanical retention approximation remains separate and does not certify a complete native U balance. Quench legacy bulk reactions before slurry thermal holds. The standalone prescribed-temperature crystallization provider remains an explicit reference approximation, not a failed-native-solver fallback.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_crystal_research for eight operations and 901 s of actual time using synthetic properties and no optional reference library. Fixed contact, birth-refinement and two-cycle coverage and all attempted outcomes are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_CRYSTAL_THERMAL_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON.

docs.title: Finite carbonate water chemistry
docs.text:
aqueous_world_spec installs a declared aqueous_mineral component with actual water, H+/OH-, CO2*, bicarbonate/carbonate, Ca, Na, Cl and finite pure calcite. Molality uses actual remaining water kg; geometric liquid volume is a separate declared holdup. Element, carbon, charge, water dissociation and carbonate mass action close together. Finite calcite may appear or deplete; no balancing ion or mineral reservoir is supplied after the solve. Derived speciation is checked against PhaseLedger before a read and is not another material stock.

The same closure serves add_component from finite neutral solution stocks, wait, aqueous-only sample and the non-destructive aqueous_ph electrode. Sampling retains the separate mineral phase. The existing pH meter model uses hydrogen activity and the session RNG; the older simplified acid/base model remains explicit for historical tasks. Both observation noise schedules support exact snapshots and resource continuation. Invalid inputs and numerical failure preserve physical inventories and time under the existing transaction rules.

This synthetic system is restricted to 298.15 K, low pressure and ionic strength <=.1 mol/kg. Constants are pKw=14, pKa1=6.35, pKa2=10.33, log10 Ksp=-8.48, Davies A=.509/b=.3, neutral gamma=1 and water activity=1. Actual water still participates in the reaction element balance. These equilibrium constants do not provide caloric data, temperature dependence or mineral kinetics. Mineral advection and thermal mixing are outside this slice.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_aqueous_research without optional libraries. scripts/check_native_aqueous.py --reaktoro-prefix <compatible-prefix> runs the fixed 33-condition block, including 32 comparisons against Reaktoro 2.13.0 with the same custom standard states and activities, one domain rejection and four analytical limits. The reference lives outside the default runtime dependency set. Its CLI flushes results before bypassing an observed Windows callback-finalization failure; calculation failures retain nonzero exit status. Coverage and all outcomes are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_AQUEOUS_MINERAL_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON.

docs.title: Finite calcite kinetics and material surface ownership
docs.text:
mineral_world_spec installs a mineral_kinetics owner beside the same bounded carbonate chemistry. A single shared BDF solve advances finite calcite while every candidate closes fast aqueous reactions at the current solid amount. The shrinking-area law is dn/dt=-A k(1-Omega), A=A_ref(n/n_ref)^(2/3). PhaseLedger owns molecules; a phase-bound material slot owns reference area and reference mol, without registering that reference as another atom stock.

The native aqueous and calcite ports move their own phases. A solid aliquot carries proportional reference geometry; aqueous transfer/sampling retains the solid and its surface. Equipment stays in place. The first model supports one evolving mineral family per compartment. Different origins or different size histories require separate compartments. Same-progress portions of one lot can split and recombine without changing their reference area or stock.

At exhaustion, actual dissolved atoms remain and the exhausted surface is removed. Seedless supersaturation has zero area and does not nucleate. A declared zero rate/surface retains its stock. Chemical exhaustion or a numerical saturation tolerance stops reaction while the supported isothermal hold fills the remaining physical wait; these times are recorded separately. Finite acid input changes the same water state before subsequent kinetic time. The pH electrode uses the committed speciation after its actual acquisition interval.

The temperature, activity and caloric limits of task 32 still apply. This is neither a reactive-transport database nor a distribution of independently evolving crystal sizes. Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_mineral_research for ten native actions, phase transfer and a 1402 s shared-clock history without an upstream dependency.

The optional scripts/check_native_minerals.py compares twelve fixed trajectories/120 states and nine early-time limits. Its independent reference uses Reaktoro 2.13.0 constrained Gibbs chemistry and DOP853 integration; it does not call the native algebraic solver/ODE backend or treat an upstream implicit finite time step as an exact continuous trajectory. Coverage, all failures and results are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_MINERAL_KINETICS_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON summary.

docs.title: Finite dilute reverse osmosis
docs.text:
membrane_world_spec() installs a finite, well-mixed feed chamber, a persistent membrane/hydraulic drive, and a finite permeate collector. The initial example contains 1 L of water plus dilute NaCl. Native physical-world capacities come from the declared vessel hardware; the legacy template size range is unchanged.

set_flow_rate requests a swept water flow in mL/min. run_flow and wait advance the same common finite-inventory solver. The task-24 pump function limits actual flow by required membrane pressure, pipe resistance, maximum head and shaft power. Pressure is derived from the coupled solution-diffusion and concentration-polarization equations, not from requested rejection. The remaining feed is the concentrate: there is no duplicate concentrate stock.

The native membrane_meter exposes water flux in m/s, membrane pressure in Pa, shaft power in W, feed/outlet/collected salinity in mol/m^3 and collected L. Instantaneous permeate salinity differs from the collector's accumulated composition. collected_fraction is collected water divided by all currently retained water; after explicit material replacement it is not cumulative recovery against all historical feed. Task-specific recovery uses the actual input/output history. Zero-flow outlet salinity reports the model's right limit.

With finite salt permeability, zero-drive permeate concentration tends to the bulk concentration. A perfectly rejecting membrane instead has a finite osmotic threshold. These are distinct limits. Reverse drive is unsupported; finite pickup, collector capacity, no forward pump drive and concentration domain limits retain the reached state/time. Numerical failure rolls back the candidate. Batch initialization preserves both actual liquid inventories and their local ages. Explicit material replacement records its exchange while preserving membrane identity and the other vessel.

This first model is isothermal at 298.15 K with ideal dilute osmotic pressure, water density 1000 kg/m^3 and negligible salt partial volume. Bulk/interface concentrations stay within 0–100 mol/m^3. Hydraulic displacement pressurizes a dead-end chamber with negligible compression storage and membrane/pipe holdup. No recirculation, compressible transient or collector backflow is implied. Fouling is an explicit option described below. Ideal mixing enthalpy is zero; the boundary removes actual pump work as heat. This scope does not predict solution heats or high-pressure calorics.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_membrane for two successive half-hour intervals and native readings. Independent WaterTAP local SD/CP equation comparisons use the same imposed ideal boundary properties; they do not claim a full WaterTAP flowsheet or its default property package. Coverage and all attempts are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_MEMBRANE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Persistent membrane fouling and finite rinsing
docs.text:
Pass MembraneSpec(fouling=MembraneFoulingSpec()) to membrane_world_spec to include an inert SiO2 pollutant, a finite pure-water wash tank and a finite waste tank. Feed pollutant moves into an equipment-owned film; the same film inventory sets resistance in the same RO flux/pump solve. Desorption returns material to feed. No second membrane solver, clock or mass copy is introduced.

set_flow_rate accepts optional flow_path="process" or "rinse". Omitting the path retains its current selection. The clean-only membrane, finite transport path and old PFR reject a rinse path they do not implement. Switching the ideal valve consumes no time or liquid; wait or run_flow performs the actual operation. The rinse bypass isolates feed, carries wash over the membrane surface and sends all detached pollutant into waste. It has zero holdup and no membrane permeation. Water use and pump work follow actual flow; zero flow does not clean. Empty wash or full waste stops at the reached time.

Batch boundaries and replacing feed preserve the membrane and bound film. Replacing a membrane uses the common equipment lifecycle and records the removed bound inventory. This evaluator initialization is not free agent cleaning. The public meter adds wash/waste volumes, rinse flow and waste pollutant mass; it does not expose hidden fouling parameters or bound inventory.

This is a synthetic dilute suspension model: SiO2 has zero partial volume and adds only hydraulic resistance, with no osmotic, reaction or caloric term. The 298.15 K boundary removes shaft work. The rinse route is not a model of chemical cleaning, backwash or pump/valve transients. Clean limits retain the task-34 WaterTAP comparison; fouling uses independent mass balances, analytic desorption and time-step refinement.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_membrane_fouling for three process/rinse cycles using the same finite tanks. The nine fixed development cycle units and all attempted outcomes are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_MEMBRANE_FOULING_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON.

docs.title: Finite binary solid equilibrium
docs.text:
solid_world_spec() installs a finite A/B specimen, the existing thermal device and a synthetic phase meter. SolidSolutionSpec declares one or two substitutional phases with ideal mixing and L0/L1 Redlich–Kister terms. The solver checks common tangents against every stationary point of every declared phase. A nominal phase can split into two composition domains; a grid only initializes the tangent solve. The existing phase ledger stores each domain's actual A/B inventory, with no separate mass copy in equipment settings.

heat and wait use the common finite-compartment enthalpy integrator. At each candidate enthalpy, stable phase equilibrium determines temperature and phase composition. The existing finite-power heater/cooler supplies the actual heat; time and utility use are settled once. Material and batch replacement retain the specimen holder's sensible heat and equilibrate it with the fresh material; vessel replacement initializes the holder too. These are recorded evaluator initializations, not free experimental actions.

The meter reads committed phase fractions/compositions and temperature in K. Native/Gym/CLI/Agent sessions and independent-process JSON continuation share the same implementation. The module declares its own 290–850 K validity range; the historical liquid action range does not silently cap a solid at 430 K. Authored limits and device/vessel limits still narrow the permitted request.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_solid_solution to heat a demixed solid and then cool it back into two composition domains. This is a synthetic binary, constant-pressure, instantaneous local-equilibrium model with common constant Cp. Al/Cu formulas provide elemental counters only; it is not a fitted Al–Cu alloy, a nucleation/growth model, a magnetic or multisublattice description, or a runtime TDB interpreter. The optional pycalphad reference uses the same synthetic energies and explicitly aligns its rounded gas constant with the native constant. No upstream solver is required by the runtime. The fixed 33-unit development block and all attempts are in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_SOLID_SOLUTION_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON.

docs.title: Selected native TDB/CEF material
docs.text:
TdbDatabase accepts declarative TDB text with an explicit InputSource. CefPhaseModel evaluates the selected phase's sublattices, vacancies, charged constituents, ordering, magnetic and caloric contributions without an upstream runtime dependency. CefMaterialSpec adds an authored temperature interval, fixed pressure, holder heat capacity and mechanical atom-molar volume. calphad_world_spec(model, element_amounts_mol=..., temperature_K=...) installs that material on the existing solid/thermal strategy and finite-power device.

Inventory keys are real TDB elements and amounts are mol of nonvacant atoms. Charged constituents and vacancies belong to the committed phase's site fractions; they do not create another material inventory. The model is stored once in the versioned calphad_material physical declaration. Its equipment record only references that binding. calphad_phase_meter reads committed temperature, element amounts and site fractions. It does not synthesize a diffraction spectrum or pretend that real elements are the old A/B counters.

heat/wait integrate the same finite-inventory total enthalpy. Internal constitution and relaxed heat capacity come from the common constrained root; temperature comes from the common caloric root. Constant element amounts are eliminated from numerical unknowns in this heat-only process, and every contribution must have zero matter rate. Holder heat is retained on material replacement; snapshot continuation, history replay, failure settlement and thermal controls retain their existing contracts.

This consumer holds one explicitly selected solid or liquid phase at a local internal minimum. It does not select a globally stable multiphase assemblage. Line compounds may have valid thermal response but underdetermined individual element potentials; no arbitrary multiplier is reported as a determined chemical potential. Nonpositive effective heat capacity, failed constraints and unsupported derivative boundaries reject the closure. Gas EOS and general phase selection require their separately declared models. The mechanical volume is authored geometry, not a pressure derivative inferred from TDB.

ChemSageDatabase.from_file(path, source=...) accepts original declarative ChemSage DAT input on that same Gibbs/material interface. The immutable input retains source provenance, phase occurrences, suppression flags, original stoichiometry, all intervals and model metadata. Repeated labels use NAME#OCCURRENCE1, etc.; phase_records exposes the original labels and records. G and Cp descriptions compile to the common caloric evaluator, including reference H/S, latent heat, extended powers and magnetic terms. QKTO uses the declared chemical groups and directional Kohler/Toop exponents. Auxiliary electron balances constrain CEF internal constitution without adding atoms.

Source suppression requires explicit activate_suppressed=True. Nonzero excess pressure coefficients require an explicit excess_pressure_unit="Pa" or "bar". Select MQMQAPhaseModel for SUBG/SUBQ quadruplet phases. It consumes source coordination numbers and their mixed/reciprocal recurrences, reference pair energies, both entropy models, and directional G/Q/R interactions with chemical groups and ternary terms. Quadruplet fractions are internal constitution; actual atom amounts remain in the existing material inventory. It shares Gibbs responses, constrained constitution and CefMaterialSpec with CEF. Original pair atoms and quadruplet charge must be consistent; the model rejects contradictory input and preserves its original declarations. Legacy annotations with no defined energy effect remain visible in diagnostics. Nonzero MQMQA source auxiliary balances need a separately declared consumer. The CEF consumer rejects MQMQA input. Unsupported real-gas, aqueous, volume and group override physics are also rejected explicitly. JSON stores original input and declared options, then recompiles through known native codecs.

The complete seven-file ChemSage qualification covers 114 original phase declarations: 111 valid phases pass 666 response points; three inconsistent source phases are explicitly rejected, leaving 18 original numerical points unexecuted. A separate 96-input, 576-point synthetic block covers additional-ion chemical groups on both ionic lattices. These are software development qualifications, not a claim of measured accuracy for every imported material. The fixed coverage, independent reference and preserved failures are documented in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261023-completed/convergence/41/NATIVE_CONV41D3_EXPERIMENT.md.

docs.title: Two-site surface interactions
docs.text:
Pass MultisiteSurfaceSpec to the existing surface_world_spec(surface_spec=...). Both site classes belong to the same carrier, with separate finite capacities, CO/O inventories and CO exchange between classes. The existing surface process factory, thermal coordinator, gas instruments and material-routing operations perform the experiment. There is no second catalyst service or time loop.

The new mechanism uses reversible adsorption/oxidation and a common transition state for each forward/reverse pair. Standard Gibbs potentials and caloric energy share the declared U/Cv table and reference entropy. A symmetric interaction_matrix_J_mol contributes G_ex=U_ex=1/2 n.epsilon.n/N_ref. The same energy and its gradient enter the heat balance; it is not an extra external reaction-heat source. State-slot declarations reference existing adsorbate/site amounts, so carrier splitting, merging and material transfer retain extensive energy. A conflicting authored caloric table is rejected.

The historical five-step mechanism remains the default and retains its exact rates. It contains irreversible oxidation. Selecting that legacy specification restores the original model; removing B from an explicitly reversible model does not silently turn its A reactions into the old irreversible kinetics. The optional old bulk reaction can still contribute through the common solver; the reversible-pair validation concerns the declared new surface channels.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_multisite_surface. The example uses finite gas sources and the existing in-situ detector latency. It has 120 s of requested heating/waiting and 10 s of acquisition, counted once. The fixed 57-unit development comparison uses CatMAP's actual local interaction and rate-constant kernels with independently solved steady equations; it does not exercise descriptor fitting or CatMAP's mapper. All attempts remain in workstreams/world_foundation/archive/20261020-native-extension/evidence/NATIVE_MULTISITE_RESULTS.json. This is a finite synthetic mean-field model, with no spatial kMC or real-catalyst prediction.

docs.title: Empirical circuits and stationary model analysis
docs.text:
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_thevenin --output /tmp/circuit.jsonl runs the authored RC/two-temperature example through the original laboratory clock, control queue, native voltage/current readout, transaction records and replay. An existing trajectory is never overwritten. These are synthetic sourced parameters, not an identified real battery or a substitute for the electrochemical models.

Add --analysis to explicitly enable a stationary small-signal model analysis before the example begins charging. The fixed public 13-point grid spans 1e-4–1e2 Hz. This computes the local response of the same residual, not a physical sinusoidal acquisition: it advances no physical time, consumes no sample and costs one declared analysis use. It returns only real/imaginary impedance in Ohm. Nonstationary polarization/temperatures and nonzero-current or voltage control are rejected; state is not quietly relaxed. Parameter uncertainty is not propagated.

The pure read-only API is chemworld.physchem.thevenin_impedance(spec, frequencies_Hz, state=state). It retains the actual cell and jig temperature responses. Its derivative modes, per-frequency failures and linear residuals are explicit; it is not a nonlinear stability or real-material accuracy certificate.

Add --controls to exercise algebraic power, a resistive load, differential power and genuine CCCV through the same operations and replay. It can be combined with --diffusion and --analysis. TheveninControlSpec declares sourced current memory, scales and response times; TheveninControlProgram declares the named mode and native-unit target. Power requires an explicit current-root interval. The original configure_electrical_control and queue_electrical_stage accept control_mode, power_W, resistance_Ohm, current_limit_A and branch_lower_A/branch_upper_A only on explicitly capable circuit equipment. CCCV uses a negative charging-current limit and a persistent internal current state. Switching to CC/CV pauses that memory; returning to dynamic control resumes it. Snapshots and material resets preserve it. Differential resistance retains the published source equation, including its possible instability; zero-current singularities and current limits stop or reject explicitly. Arbitrary executable callbacks and undocumented control defaults are not accepted.

Add --diffusion to the example to enable a sourced, authored 16-cell planar SOC diffusion model. --diffusion --analysis also analyzes its initial uniform state. TheveninDiffusionSpec declares the diffusion time constant in seconds, normalized cell faces on 0–1, and the explicit surface-ocv-passive-pr5869 convention. The original mean SOC and N−1 independent deviations form one persistent equipment state; there is no second charge inventory. The same profile changes voltage, heat, finite-source voltage control, surface stopping events and impedance. A material reset preserves the profile, and a full session reset restores the declared uniform initial state. Nonuniform profiles are not stationary analysis points merely because the applied current is zero.

The voltage and heat equations include the explicitly attributed corrections in PyBaMM PR 5869. The unmodified 25.4.2 reference remains recorded as a version comparison, not a target for the corrected physics. Instantaneous diffusion heat can be negative after reversal; it is not clipped. The model declares empirical heat and charge balances, not a complete chemical-energy function. Spatial resolution must be checked for the requested transient: the fixed coarse-grid surface-cutoff qualification did not meet its original convergence criterion. Independent refinement and all failures are recorded with the task's development qualification, rather than hidden by a changed acceptance tolerance. Other control modes and the rest of task 45 remain separate implementation and qualification work.

docs.title: Cross-domain examples
docs.text: The installed native domain workflows exercise shared equipment, finite process inventories, delayed stochastic readouts, and replay. The capability table is generated from the installed module declarations; supported composition domains remain explicitly bounded.

docs.title: Parameter and measurement inputs
docs.text:
Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.scientific_inputs for a complete import example: an existing water property package, six synthetic cooling-curve records in two experiment groups, and two heat-loss parameters applied through the native model declaration. The example emits JSON with sources, uncertainties, train/validation counts and public pressure readings. It performs no fitting.

chemworld.data.scientific_inputs.ScientificTable.from_json(text) reads either parameter or measurement tables. Columns declare a quantity, unit, role, finite valid range and reference state. Each cell contains value, unit, standard uncertainty, uncertainty_note and quality. A source has an explicit citation, version, licence declaration and synthetic, measured or literature label. Unknown uncertainty stays None; it must have an explanatory note. Celsius values receive the temperature offset, while uncertainty uses the scale only.

Each row supplies row_id, source_id, group_id, sample_id, split and all declared cells. sample_id identifies one acquisition, including all its channels; repeat acquisitions need separate IDs. Measurement splits are train, validation, test or unused. All rows in one experiment group must share a split. Parameter rows use parameters. Missing or invalid observations remain in the table with their quality flags; conditions and parameters must be valid. The importer rejects duplicate identities, unknown columns, incompatible units and valid values outside their declared range.

table.to_csv() writes a wide CSV with the row identifiers and five cell fields per quantity, for example pressure.value and pressure.uncertainty. ScientificTable.from_csv(text, metadata) reads it using the same contract; metadata is table.to_dict() with the rows entry removed. No split is inferred or randomized. table.summary() reports complete counts, and table.rows_for("validation") selects the declared holdout.

chemworld.physchem.property_inputs.PropertyInputCard imports the existing component/correlation format with per-correlation source and uncertainty records. Its evaluate_state method uses the existing property evaluator. Energy and entropy requests require an explicit imported caloric reference. The curated example preserves unknown upstream table redistribution terms and unquantified uncertainty; successful parsing does not establish a licence or calibration.

chemworld.world.parameter_inputs.bind_parameter_row(physics, table, row_id, targets) applies one parameter row to new model configuration. The application supplies ModelParameterTarget objects independently of the input, defining the installed model/version, binding, numeric field path and quantity contract. The function returns new physics and an import receipt; pass that configuration through the usual composition/session constructor. Model codecs validate coupled changes together. Measurement tables cannot be bound as parameters, and imports never write observations or inventory into a running world.

docs.title: Finite native calibration
docs.text:
chemworld.data.calibration.NativeCalibration fits a finite parameter whitelist by executing fixed histories in fresh native sessions. Supply a ScientificTable, CalibrationParameter declarations and one NativeCalibrationExperiment per data group. Each CalibrationReadout binds an observation column to an actual measurement step and public channel, with an optional sampling-time column. Parameter paths may address existing continuous model configuration fields; network structure, task targets and live inventory cannot be fitted.

Only training rows enter uncertainty-weighted, bounded least squares. Successful fits execute the validation groups separately and report errors in original units, weighted errors, active bounds and local Jacobian rank. Non-valid input observations remain in the exclusion counts; valid observations require positive declared standard uncertainties. Failed forward histories retain actual readings, operation outcomes, time, cost and sampling. They stop the fit instead of becoming artificial residual penalties. The forward limit counts actual group executions, including finite-difference evaluations.

Run the fixed synthetic thermal, SPM and confounded thermal examples with:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_calibration --output $env:TEMP/chemworld-calibration.json

The thermal example uses an explicitly ideal synthetic pressure gauge and fixed data perturbations. The SPM example fits one diffusion coefficient from public terminal voltage. Joint heat-loss/heat-capacity fitting demonstrates that a good curve fit can still leave parameters unidentifiable. These examples establish a calibration workflow; empirical material validation requires separately sourced data and a fixed validation design.

docs.title: DIPPR correlations and caloric requests
docs.text:
PropertyCorrelation accepts dippr100, 101, 102, 104, 105, 106, 107, 114, 115, 116, 127 (each with the dippr prefix), plus dippr100_reciprocal, dippr105_reciprocal, and dippr106_reciprocal. Declare a supported property_id, output unit, absolute-K input, coefficients and a material validity interval. property_equation_contracts() exposes the required/optional parameters, property dimensions, equation source and domains. Material parameters still need their own source and uncertainty metadata.

The existing evaluate_correlation and property package use these declarations. correlation_temperature_derivative returns the analytic first derivative; integrate_correlation returns a definite integral or, with over_temperature=True, its integral divided by T. Its numerical error estimate and quadrature evaluation count describe the adaptive integration only, excluding domain checks. Failed quadrature and intervals crossing poles are rejected.

caloric_correlation_change, evaluate_caloric_correlation and the existing phase-path enthalpy reports consume these same equations. Output-unit conversion scales the result while retaining characteristic temperatures and exponents. Gas Cv-to-entropy conversion uses the declared ideal-gas reference. Other phases still need an explicit closure before H and U can be interchanged.

The fixed development block compares 142 cases with chemicals 1.5.2; production evaluation does not import chemicals. This covers formula behavior, not a new material database. Polynomial inventory admission stays unchanged pending the later process-integration task; the full chemicals expansion remains in progress.

The same 14 DIPPR expressions now support temperature derivatives through order three and named coefficient/mixed partials through total order three:

from chemworld.physchem import (
    PropertyCorrelation, dippr_temperature_response, dippr_parameter_jacobian,
    dippr_mixed_derivative, dippr106_coefficients_from_point,
)

curve = PropertyCorrelation(
    "example-cp", "dippr107", {"A": 25, "B": 30, "C": 800, "D": 10, "E": 400},
    {"temperature": "K"}, "J/(mol*K)", "ideal_gas_heat_capacity",
    {"temperature": (200, 500)}, "Synthetic example; not a material fit",
)
response = dippr_temperature_response(curve, temperature_K=300, order=3)
jacobian = dippr_parameter_jacobian(curve, [250, 300, 400], parameters=("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"))
mixed = dippr_mixed_derivative(curve, temperature_K=300, coordinates=("temperature", "C"))

Response entry n uses the declared output unit divided by K**n; response.to("kJ/(mol*K)") converts all entries consistently. Jacobian columns use the named source-coefficient coordinates, including critical temperature when explicitly selected. To fit an omitted optional coefficient, first add it explicitly to the declaration. These are analytic chain rules, not finite differences. The existing application-range policy and mathematical domains remain in force; no extension through a critical singularity is inferred.

dippr106_coefficients_from_point matches value/first derivative (A/B), or also second derivative (A/B/C), with D=E=0. Inputs must share one output-unit basis. The ABC system is locally rank deficient at T/Tc = 1-exp(-2) and is rejected; recovering coefficients at one point is not a fitted temperature interval. The additional fixed block covers 84 states and 2,136 comparisons against public Jacobian/recovery functions and an independent 80-digit formula implementation. This completes the DIPPR mathematical increment. Its fitting consumer and the remaining G2 boundaries are described below.

chemworld.data.correlation_calibration.CorrelationCalibration now fits an existing declaration to a measurement ScientificTable, sharing the bounded TRF optimizer, weighted metrics and local rank diagnostics with NativeCalibration. Its analytic mode consumes the DIPPR, vapor-pressure, volume and Yaws-viscosity coefficient Jacobians. For other scalar declarations, derivative_mode="3-point" must be selected explicitly; numerical differences are labelled in the report and are not presented as analytic derivatives.

from chemworld.data.correlation_calibration import CorrelationCalibration, CorrelationFitParameter

# observations: a ScientificTable with temperature/value columns, declared
# standard uncertainties and preassigned train/validation experiment groups.
fit = CorrelationCalibration(
    observations, curve,
    (CorrelationFitParameter("A", (10, 50), 25),
     CorrelationFitParameter("B", (10, 60), 30)),
    fitted_correlation_id="my-fitted-cp",
)
report = fit.fit(max_nfev=100)
if report["status"] == "fitted":
    fitted_curve = PropertyCorrelation.from_dict(report["fitted_correlation"])

Parameter bounds and initial values use the formula's original coefficient coordinates; the report binds them to the equation and input/output units. Observation values and standard uncertainties are converted together. Log parameter normalization contributes its own chain-rule factor to the Jacobian. Only training rows enter optimization or sensitivity calculations; validation is evaluated once after convergence, with no model selection. Test/unused rows are not evaluated. Invalid observations remain explicitly excluded, failed forward evaluations retain their attempted rows, and rank deficiency is reported even when predictions fit well. A failed or unconverged fit exports no curve.

The fitted curve has a new requested identity and a new fit: source. Original coefficients/source metadata, measurement provenance, residuals and rank are retained, so a regression is not mislabelled as the original published fit. Declared application bounds remain bounds, not a claim of material validation. The fitted declaration can enter existing property packages, JSON and caloric consumers without adding a runtime or a second property database.

The fixed synthetic qualification fits every explicit coefficient of all 14 DIPPR forms, in two parameter sets each: 28/28 fits pass 2,524 checks. Among these, 23 are rank deficient under the declared local threshold; this is retained as a limit of the observation design. This qualifies fitting behavior, not unique parameter recovery or empirical chemical accuracy. The six other public fitting Jacobian families (Antoine, extended TRC Antoine, both Wagner forms, Yaws pressure and Yaws viscosity) also pass full-column regression: 12/12 fits and 948 checks, with four locally rank-deficient cases retained. Critical constants and log bases remain fixed where the public fitting API defines them as fixed inputs.

The derivative and inverse review also binds the existing pressure, pure/mixed virial and Henry numerical evidence. Direct PPDS9/Yaws checks cover six states and 36 public/high-precision comparisons through third temperature order. Lastovka H/S inversion uses the existing temperature_from_caloric_change with an explicitly bounded Cp curve; a positive multiplicative heat-capacity factor is represented by dividing the specified caloric change by that factor. Its 74 direct public-reference states pass 218 comparisons, including cyclic and non-cyclic choices, different reference temperatures and negative/zero/positive changes. The full G2 mathematical review maps 159 relevant public interfaces; it does not establish the unresolved component identities or the final G3 whole-source/process qualification. Scientific utility and signed-virial reference discrepancies remain explicit rather than being counted as agreement.

docs.title: Read-only battery impedance (development)
docs.text:
The existing isothermal SPM, SPMe and DFN expose local rest-point analysis through chemworld.physchem.battery_impedance.battery_impedance. It consumes their actual inventory rates and electrical constraints, not an independently fitted circuit:

from chemworld.physchem.battery_models import BatterySPMSpec
from chemworld.physchem.battery_impedance import battery_impedance

cell = BatterySPMSpec()
state = cell.initial_state()
spectrum = battery_impedance(cell, [1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2], state=state)
report = spectrum.to_dict()  # per-frequency real/imaginary ohm and failures

This does not advance time, spend experimental resources, expose a new agent instrument, or modify a snapshot. Positive current means discharge; passive impedance is -delta_V/delta_I, with exp(+i*2*pi*f*t) phasors. Frequency must be strictly positive. A nonstationary concentration profile or a stopping boundary is rejected rather than silently relaxed. Thermal and side-reaction combinations are not yet supported. The present quasi-static BV models have no double-layer capacitance, so their spectra must not be interpreted as including its RC arc.

The shared residual_frequency_response in physchem.residual_frequency also supports general declared residuals, non-diagonal mass matrices and algebraic feedthrough. It uses the existing derivative modes and sparse linear solver, retaining singular-frequency failures rather than substituting a least-squares answer. Physical input/output units and derivative provenance remain in the report. This is local response, not a nonlinear stability certificate.

The first independent development block compares six SPM cases against continuous spherical diffusion, including four radial resolutions and a flat-OCV limit. The subsequent SPMe/DFN block checks terminal impedance and the complex mean salt concentration response in each of the three electrolyte regions against released PyBaMM 25.4.2 equations, independently differentiated with CasADi and solved with SciPy. Ten cases, each at 13 frequencies, pass the fixed comparison and native / reference refinement bounds. The original uniform-radial reference was insufficiently resolved for five SPMe cases (5/10 overall); that result is retained separately. Changing only the reference radial mesh to boundary refinement gives 10/10 without changing native physics or error bounds. This is a finite, synthetic, constant-property domain, not validation for arbitrary materials, nonstationary points or wet experiments. Other model families in NATIVE-CONV-45 remain outstanding. The fixed inputs, limits and all attempts are linked from NATIVE_CONV45_IMPEDANCE_EXPERIMENT.md in the workstream.

docs.title: Sourced nonlinear electrode OCV
docs.text:
physchem.battery_materials.ElectrodeOCV represents a bounded polynomial plus exponential and tanh terms. It stores the material, source, model compatibility and stoichiometry domain. Use from_parameter_row to bind explicitly named columns from the existing ScientificTable; amplitudes use V and scales/shifts use dimensionless. The original parameter values, units and uncertainty notes remain in its JSON.

from chemworld.physchem.battery_materials import ElectrodeOCV
from chemworld.physchem.battery_models import BatterySPMSpec

# table is a validated ScientificTable of kind "parameters".
ocv = ElectrodeOCV.from_parameter_row(
    table, "electrode-row", material_id="my-electrode",
    polynomial=("constant_V", "linear_V"),
    tanh_terms=(("transition_V", "transition_scale", "transition_center"),),
)
spec = BatterySPMSpec(negative_ocv=ocv)

An explicit curve replaces that electrode's linear OCV fields. The actual SPM, SPMe and DFN voltage laws consume it, and DFN uses its analytic slope in the coupled Jacobian. Chemical potential and integrated electrode energy derive from the same expression. Public curve evaluation rejects a point outside its declared domain; solver trials may explicitly evaluate its analytic continuation while the battery's physical stopping surfaces still govern accepted states.

The fixed eight-unit development block compares two Chen2020 OCV relationships, three continuous discharge/rest/charge trajectories and three local spectra against released PyBaMM 25.4.2 functions and models: 8/8 passed. Geometry and transport remain synthetic in that block. It is not a complete LGM50 parameterization. Nonlinear OCV with thermal or side-reaction models is currently rejected; the full material, transport, thermal and other model-family scope of CONV-45 remains open. Inputs and all outcomes are in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV45_OCV_EXPERIMENT.md and NATIVE_CONV45_OCV_RESULTS.json.

docs.title: Equilibrium electrode SOH (development)
docs.text:
physchem.battery_soh solves the voltage-window geometry using those same OCV functions. ElectrodeSOHSpec accepts known electrode capacities and either known="cyclable_lithium" (active electrode Li charge) or known="cell_capacity". HalfCellSOHSpec is explicitly a positive working electrode versus Li/Li+ at 0 V; this is an equilibrium analysis, not yet a native half-cell dynamical process. Capacities are C; ScientificTable parameter bindings can explicitly convert Ah or mAh while retaining original units, uncertainty and source. No estimator is added: native public-observation calibration remains the existing data calibration workflow, and local implicit sensitivities do not prove parameter identifiability.

from chemworld.physchem import soh_from_battery, battery_spec_at_soc
from chemworld.physchem.battery_models import BatterySPMSpec

cell = BatterySPMSpec(minimum_voltage_V=3.38, maximum_voltage_V=3.92)
state = cell.initial_state()
soh = soh_from_battery(cell, state)  # active Li only, not electrolyte salt or locked SEI
if soh.status == "unique":
    solution = soh.branch()
    energy_J = soh.theoretical_energy_j()  # reversible OCV integral, not loaded work
    fresh_cell = battery_spec_at_soc(cell, soh, .5)  # a NEW initial configuration

This does not advance time, spend resources, relax a live concentration profile, or reset an existing device. SPM, SPMe and DFN read their actual electrode bins. at_soc() and soc_at_voltage() use the selected equilibrium branch. Complete multiple results require an explicit branch index; incomplete isolation retains unresolved boxes and cannot be treated as unique. Known capacity at a declared electrode face is handled without widening the domain. Impossible inventory, no voltage-window solution, and numerical/rank uncertainty have distinct statuses. The shared bounded interval/Krawczyk search uses the existing point-root solver; outward floating-point enclosures are not a formal exact-real proof. Cutoff roots must delimit a complete physical path, not merely solve two endpoint equations.

Offline example: uv run --no-sync python examples/native_battery_soh.py. The fixed 12-unit development block compares released PyBaMM 25.4.2 SOH equations, hand algebra and independent polynomial roots, including multiple/infeasible/ nonidentifiable cases. Inputs and all attempts are in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV45_SOH_EXPERIMENT.md and the matching NATIVE_CONV45_SOH_RESULTS*.json. MSMR-specific SOH, ageing inference, wet-cell accuracy and the remaining task-45 model families are not covered by this block.

docs.title: Many-particle electrodes (development; scientific qualification pending)
docs.text:
BatteryMPMSpec is an explicit ideal-uniform-electrolyte MPM. Each electrode retains its total active volume and material coefficients in ParticleSpec. Optional ParticleSizeDistribution declarations allocate that volume across positive radii. Every size has its own actual radial inventory, diffusion and interfacial current; currents are solved together at the shared electrode potentials, never assigned in advance from the volume fractions. With no size distribution, the declared particle radius gives the monodisperse SPM limit.

from chemworld.physchem import BatteryMPMSpec, ParticleSizeDistribution, mpm_fields
from chemworld.world.battery_world import battery_world_spec

# source is the common InputSource for this distribution.
sizes = ParticleSizeDistribution((5e-6, 15e-6), (.5, .5), source)
cell = BatteryMPMSpec(negative_distribution=sizes, positive_distribution=sizes)
fields = mpm_fields(cell, cell.initial_state(), current_A=.2)
world = battery_world_spec(cell)

Direct weights are normalized volume fractions. from_weights(..., basis=...) explicitly converts and normalizes positive relative number, area or volume weights. from_parameter_table retains original common source rows, units and uncertainty; um is an explicit length conversion, not an inferred unit. lognormal_size_distribution discretizes a stated truncated density in the specified input basis, preserving median, log-standard-deviation, bounds and quadrature count. It does not recover unobserved distribution tails.

All sizes use the existing battery equipment slot, source controls, shared clock, native measurements, snapshot and replay. Surface readouts are area averages; bulk stoichiometry is volume weighted. Stops check every size, not only an average. Rest can redistribute Li between sizes at zero terminal current. Electrode chemical energy, dissipation, SOH totals and read-only local impedance consume the same bins. A sourced nonlinear OCV must explicitly declare MPM compatibility; stored older material compatibility lists are not widened.

Offline workflow: uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_mpm --output /tmp/mpm.jsonl. Functional checks include true CC/CV/source limits, analytic derivatives, conservation, energy balance, both measurement noise modes and cross-process continuation. Independent released-model comparisons and subsequent resolution blocks retain their separate denominators and failures in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONVERGENCE_ACCEPTANCE.md. Do not infer arbitrary-mesh accuracy, measured-cell accuracy, composite electrodes or thermal/ageing capability from these functional checks.

docs.title: Directional OCP and electrode memory
docs.text:
Isothermal SPM and MPM cells can declare negative_ocp and positive_ocp using ElectrodeOCPSpec. Explicit lithiation/delithiation ElectrodeOCV branches and a source-bearing parameter table select current_sigmoid or axen. The sigmoid uses effective collector area in m² and an inverse-current-density scale in m²/A. Axen uses an initial dimensionless memory and separate positive decay parameters. The existing single/absent declaration retains the original equilibrium curve.

Each Axen electrode owns one persistent h coordinate, shared by all its MPM sizes and driven by its total current. Rest holds h while particle profiles may relax; current reversal changes it continuously. Material reset preserves the installed cell's history, while replacing the cell uses the new declaration. Snapshots and exact replay retain both inventories and memory. Meter acquisition still advances its declared duration, so it does not secretly pause the cell.

The authored offline example exercises discharge, rest, reversal and replay:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_hysteresis --output /tmp/hysteresis-spm.jsonl
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_hysteresis --many-particle --output /tmp/hysteresis-mpm.jsonl
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_hysteresis --mode current_sigmoid --output /tmp/directional-spm.jsonl

These are synthetic branches, not calibrated materials. Operational OCP is distinct from a single-valued equilibrium free-energy curve. Thermal/SEI coupling, equilibrium SOH for these branches and full hysteresis energy accounting are not provided. The original chemical-energy helper evaluates only the declared single-valued reference; it does not include the memory state's energy, and directional-OCP dissipation requests are rejected. Axen ordinary rest EIS is rejected because its two directional current derivatives generally differ; smooth sigmoid analysis uses the same physical residual. Wycisk/MSMR and SPMe/DFN directional OCP remain separate model extensions.

docs.title: Finite lithium-metal / positive-working half cell
docs.text:
BatteryHalfCellSPMSpec declares a real finite lithium-metal reservoir and one positive working particle. It has no negative intercalation particle. The metal's area, thickness, conductivity, molar volume, exchange-current density, temperature and salt condition come from an explicit ScientificTable row in LithiumMetalCounterElectrodeSpec; the working electrode declares a sourced ElectrodeOCV. This first scope is isothermal, uniform-electrolyte SPM.

Positive current removes lithium from the metal and inserts it into the working particle. Both inventories, passed charge and delivered electrical work live in the existing equipment-owned state. Their shared solver enforces total lithium and both Faraday balances. The measured voltage includes the working OCV, both Butler–Volmer overpotentials and metal ohmic loss. Finite current or voltage programmes, staged controls, meter acquisition, snapshots and exact replay use the existing battery runtime. A material reset cannot replenish installed metal.

Metal depletion stops discharge at its actual event time. The depleted state is valid: further positive current stops immediately; explicit rest or negative current permits relaxation or replating. Metal geometry and interface area stay fixed, including during replating. This is a fixed-interface approximation, not a moving-boundary or morphology model. Working-particle surface and voltage limits also remain real stopping events.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_half_cell --output /tmp/half-cell.jsonl

The example uses authored synthetic inputs. Half-cell thermal/SEI coupling, full chemical-energy/dissipation accounting and automatic full-cell SOH conversion are explicitly unsupported. The older explicitly declared HalfCellSOHSpec equilibrium calculation remains separate; it is not silently substituted for finite-metal dynamics. Functional tests and independent released PyBaMM comparisons have distinct scopes and denominators in the native convergence reports. The reference adapter's finite-metal inventory and depletion event are an explicit Faraday extension of PyBaMM's positive-working SPM, not a claim that the upstream model already has a finite-metal state.

Stationary half-cell impedance is available through the existing read-only chemworld.physchem.battery_impedance API. It uses the original metal and working particle residual, both interface kinetics and the fixed metal resistance. Every radial state must be stationary, metal inventory strictly positive, and working surface and voltage strictly inside their allowed ranges. A worked particle still relaxing after current shutoff is rejected; analysis never waits or modifies inventories. The original time-domain depleted-metal recovery behavior is unchanged.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_half_cell_impedance --output /tmp/half-cell-eis.json

The output retains full complex state responses, signed charge/work and both inventory responses. With positive discharge and exp(+iωt), iωF δn_metal = −δI, iωF δn_working = δI, and iω δW = V_rest δI. Fixed geometry does not create an extra metal-capacity impedance pole; finite metal still constrains the operating domain. These derivatives do not guarantee that a finite oscillation at an arbitrary low frequency avoids depletion. The analysis consumes no experimental time or resources and is not a new instrument. Independent frequency comparisons and the earlier half-cell time-domain grid qualification gaps remain separate.

The fixed 80/160-cell frequency block completed all 50 routes and 680 frequencies, but only 2/10 complete units met every precision criterion. Surface extrapolation differences caused 32 failed comparisons, including 10 impedance comparisons; the slow-diffusion coarse-grid surface discrepancy reached 5.70%. Conservation, full state checks and read-only behavior passed. The eight fine native spectra met the continuous-sphere comparison, which does not replace the failed whole block qualification. Mesh and frequency accuracy remain explicit limitations.

docs.title: Dynamic-salt DFN lithium-metal half cell
docs.text:
BatteryHalfCellDFNSpec adds a separate two-domain half-cell declaration: separator and positive working electrode, with one radial particle per working thickness cell. It has no artificial negative porous electrode. Finite metal lithium, spatial electrolyte salt, particle lithium and signed charge/work use the same equipment slots, shared clock, queue and snapshot codec as other native batteries. half_cell_dfn_fields() returns local reaction currents, salt and potential fields; the agent-facing meter still returns only terminal V and A.

Positive current strips metal and inserts working-electrode lithium. The real left salt flux balances the working reaction source. Its reconstructed boundary concentration enters metal Butler–Volmer kinetics and the liquid potential. Metal geometry is fixed while its inventory changes. Empty metal can rest or recover under reverse current; actual stripping stops at depletion.

CC accepts an explicitly sourced nonnegative metal salt exponent. Finite CV requires an analytic passive-branch certificate over all surface trials, a positive zero-current salt reconstruction and last-cell bulk fractions in [0,1]. Unproved or nonunique constitutive branches are rejected. This does not clip local reverse currents or repair inventories. Heat, side reactions, impedance, automatic SOH and complete chemical-energy closure are not supplied by this family. Independent released-model and mesh qualification remains separate from its functional and runtime tests.

docs.title: Independent material phases in a composite electrode
docs.text:
BatteryCompositeSPMSpec declares two negative active-material phases and one positive phase. Each ActiveMaterialPhaseSpec has its own particle radius, diffusivity, active volume, capacity, exchange-current scale, initial lithium fraction, sourced single-valued ElectrodeOCV and parameter source. These are material identities, not particle-size bins or a fitted average electrode.

The composite and existing MPM use one particle-electrode residual kernel. It solves a common electrode potential and individual Butler–Volmer reaction currents, together with conservative spherical diffusion. The two negative currents sum to the external current; they are not assigned by fixed volume fractions. At zero external current, unequal material potentials can drive opposing internal currents and transfer lithium between the negative phases. The positive inventory and external charge then stay constant. This process continues through the existing runtime's wait, measurement and queued stages.

Every phase inventory remains equipment-owned through snapshots and material resets. The shared clock, electrical work and Faraday balances are unchanged. Replacing a compatible cell introduces the replacement's explicit inventories. Current/voltage control, individual material-surface stopping events and terminal voltage cutoffs use the same phase-resolved electrical solution. A monotonicity certificate for each OCV defines the supported current-sharing branch; an unavailable physical root is rejected instead of clipping a phase current to the external source limit.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_composite --output /tmp/composite.jsonl

The example uses authored synthetic material parameters, with an initially unequilibrated pair of negative phases. The first scope is isothermal, fixed salt, one particle population per material and single-valued monotone OCV. It does not claim the graphite tables or directional silicon curves of Chen2020_composite. Thermal/SEI coupling, phase-specific size distributions, directional hysteresis, composite DFN, half-cell combinations, SOH and chemical-energy/dissipation closure are explicitly outside this scope. Independent comparisons use the actual released PyBaMM multi-phase SPM; functional tests and fixed-grid scientific qualification are recorded separately in the convergence reports.

The subsequent composite frequency API accepts explicitly stationary operating points. Each particle must be uniform and both negative materials must have the same OCV; equal lithium fractions alone do not guarantee this. It evaluates the original algebraic closure at the supplied inventories, then checks every inventory equation. Zero external current with opposing internal phase currents is rejected, as is a nonuniform particle that would continue diffusing. The API never advances time or modifies a caller's lithium fractions to find equilibrium.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_composite_impedance --output /tmp/composite-eis.json

This separate example explicitly declares negative fractions .6/.6, giving .13 V for both authored curves. The original time-domain example retains its unequal potentials and internal redistribution. The output includes terminal impedance, complete complex state responses and all three phase-current responses with their identities. Currents divide according to the coupled frequency response, rather than fixed area fractions; each phase obeys iωF δn = −δq. The shared BatteryImpedance and FrequencyResponse reports keep failed frequencies and linear-solver diagnostics. This remains a read-only physical analysis, not a new agent-facing instrument or measured material fit.

The independent continuous-sphere comparison is limited to the predeclared frequency/grid block. Finite-volume surface reconstruction contributes a half-cell surface term at very high frequency, so a fixed finite mesh is not claimed to reproduce the continuous infinite-frequency intercept. Ordinary EIS for hysteresis, side reactions or nonstationary states, composite SOH/SOC initialization and complete chemical-energy closure remain unsupported.

docs.title: Spatial composite electrodes with dynamic electrolyte
docs.text:
BatteryCompositeDFNSpec resolves two negative material phases and one positive phase at every electrode thickness cell. Each phase reuses the original sourced ActiveMaterialPhaseSpec with its own radius, diffusivity, capacity, exchange scale and single-valued OCV explicitly supporting DFN. Its active volume is the whole electrode phase volume; the model divides it among the thickness cells. The sum of phase volumes must fit the non-pore electrode volume. Zero binder is allowed; extra active volume is rejected.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_dfn_composite --output /tmp/composite-dfn.jsonl

The example uses synthetic inputs, three CC/rest/charge stages, actual meter time and exact native replay. composite_dfn_fields returns each local phase reaction current, the summed cell current, radial-surface and mean fractions, electrolyte concentration, solid/liquid potentials and face currents. Material identities and all local inventories survive JSON continuation. CompositeDFNReadout summarizes the three phases while retaining the port voltage/current.

All phases share the local electrical potentials. Their independent BV currents sum into the original DFN charge and salt equations. Rest can transfer lithium between phases with zero terminal charge; fixed phase-current weights cannot represent that behavior. A single coupled residual advances particles, salt and signed terminal charge/work, using the existing finite-source CC/CV controls, phase/salt/voltage stopping events, session queue and equipment ownership.

This first combination is isothermal with constant transport and single-valued OCV. Heat, SEI/plating, hysteresis, particle-size distributions, MSMR, half-cell, SOH and impedance combinations are unsupported. Signed terminal work is retained; it does not define a complete chemical-energy closure. Independent qualification uses the actual modular PyBaMM DFN with two/one phases and single OCP, and is reported separately from functional tests. This scope does not reproduce the silicon directional-OCP default of BasicDFNComposite or calibrated cell data.

The fixed development comparison completed all 14 units and 72 routes, including 60 histories and 12 refusals, with no execution or assessment exception. Strict qualification remains open: 2/14 units and 929/964 checks passed. The failures include actual source salt conservation, finite-grid responses and cutoff endpoints; successful functional/runtime tests do not establish those accuracy bounds. The complete original trajectories and all failures remain archived.

docs.title: Multiple-reaction MSMR particles and stationary impedance
docs.text:
BatteryMSMRSPMSpec uses one lithium inventory per radial shell. Its sourced MSMRMaterialSpec rows describe one or two overlapping reactions in each electrode, with a shared potential and overpotential. They are not independently conserved material phases. The original runtime supports CC, finite-source CV, queued stages, measurements and exact JSON continuation at fixed temperature and electrolyte concentration.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_msmr --output /tmp/msmr.jsonl
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_msmr_impedance --output /tmp/msmr-eis.json

The read-only chemworld.physchem.battery_impedance API differentiates that same residual, retaining every shell, signed charge/work and the electrical closure. It requires a stationary operating point with strictly interior shell amounts, surface occupancy and voltage. It never relaxes a worked particle or changes the experiment's clock, queue or future. The example exports the complete complex response, sourced reaction identities and both total inventory responses; it does not invent separate inventories for individual reactions.

The potential-driven transport law gives chemical diffusivity Dchem = -D F x(1-x)/(RT dx/dU) at uniform rest. A single unit-capacity reaction with width 1 gives D, while width 2 gives 2D. The original linear extrapolation of surface potential is retained. Reaction current shares follow their exchange currents, whereas occupancy shares follow the derivatives of their occupancy curves; these shares generally differ. Only each electrode's total lithium satisfies its own Faraday balance.

These examples use authored synthetic parameters. The fixed 10-unit development frequency block passed all 50 routes, 680 frequency points and 1336 checks, using 80/160 radial cells and 1e-5–1e-2 Hz. Its actual PyBaMM reference retains all original states; the distinct electrolyte reference concentration is mapped explicitly, with each authored/source parameter retained. This bounded result is separate from functional compatibility and the original 12-unit time-domain result; it does not qualify arbitrary materials or frequencies. Thermal coupling, side reactions, MSMR-specific SOH and complete chemical-energy closure remain unsupported.

docs.title: Average-electrode Newman–Tobias model
docs.text:
BatteryNewmanTobiasSpec keeps one finite lithium inventory per electrode while solving the spatial solid/liquid potentials and local Butler–Volmer currents. AveragedElectrodeSpec declares radius, active volume, maximum concentration and exchange-current scale; radius determines reaction area, not a radial mesh. PorousElectrodeGeometrySpec declares the three layer thicknesses, area, porosities, thickness mesh and conductivities. Solid conductivities are effective values; the liquid value is bulk conductivity with the declared porosity factors. The charge integration kernel is shared with the existing DFN model.

Positive current removes lithium from the negative electrode and inserts it into the positive electrode. The original equipment state contains those two amounts, passed charge and terminal work. Fixed electrolyte concentration is a declared approximation, not an additional mutable salt inventory. Local current density, solid/liquid potentials and face currents returned by newman_tobias_fields are derived from that same state. Spatially uniform concentration does not imply spatially uniform reaction current.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_newman_tobias --output /tmp/newman-tobias.jsonl

The authored example performs charge/discharge, rest, measurement and exact replay through the existing battery runtime. CC, finite-source CV, queued stages, shared laboratory time and JSON continuation use their original interfaces. Material reset preserves installed lithium; device replacement installs the newly declared inventory once. Stoichiometry and voltage cutoffs stop the actual advance, and reversing current can move inward from a stoichiometry limit.

This finite model is isothermal with constant electrolyte concentration and fixed geometry/transport. It has no radial diffusion, dynamic salt, side reaction or thermal closure. Supplied ElectrodeOCV expressions must explicitly include NewmanTobias in supported_models; existing material declarations are not silently broadened. Chemical-energy, full dissipation and automatic SOH requests remain explicitly unsupported. The example uses synthetic inputs, not a calibrated commercial cell. Functional checks and released-source scientific qualification have separate denominators in the native convergence records.

Stationary impedance uses the existing read-only chemworld.physchem.battery_impedance API and the original mean-inventory and porous electrical residual. Both lithium stocks and terminal voltage must lie strictly inside their event bounds. Unlike a spatial concentration model, these mean inventories have no concentration gradients to relax after resting a worked cell. The analysis neither advances a session nor alters its queue, noise, charge or work ledger.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_newman_tobias_impedance --output /tmp/newman-tobias-eis.json

The example exports every complex state response, each thickness-cell reaction current, the two lithium-stock responses, signed charge and signed terminal work. At uniform rest the finite electrical network is resistive; the OCV derivatives and conserved mean inventories supply an inverse-frequency contribution. Local reaction-current and face-current responses are frequency independent. This model does not imply a diffusion impedance or double-layer relaxation. Independent continuous-network electrical-loss checks do not define a full chemical or thermal energy model. The previous time-domain qualification and its unresolved CV mesh difference remain separate.

The first fixed stationary-NT comparison block solved all 45 routes and 455 frequency points. Strict qualification passed 3/8 units. After correcting an evaluator summation-order bug, a complete unchanged rerun remained 3/8: source current/Faraday invariants and one high-conductivity initialization current exceeded the original bounds. All 45 complete route objects, except elapsed time, matched the first run exactly. Both complete records and all failed checks are retained. Functional availability does not close that qualification gap.

docs.title: Closed-volume-compatible lead-acid LOQS
docs.text:
BatteryLeadAcidSpec adds a finite isothermal lead-acid model on the original battery runtime. Six equipment-owned inventories represent negative Pb/PbSO4, positive PbO2/PbSO4, and electrolyte H2SO4/H2O. Discharge consumes actual Pb, PbO2 and acid; charging reverses that reaction. Pore volume, acid concentration, water concentration and Bode molality OCPs follow those same stocks. Terminal charge/work, ordinary CC and finite-current CV, the existing meter, queues, shared time and JSON continuation use the original session interfaces.

from chemworld.physchem import BatteryLeadAcidSpec, lead_acid_readout
from chemworld.world.battery_world import battery_world_spec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime

cell = BatteryLeadAcidSpec()
world = battery_world_spec(cell)
runtime = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=world)
runtime.reset(seed=4)
runtime.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control", "current_A": 0.5})
runtime.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 3.0})
measurement = runtime.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "battery_meter"})
runtime.close()

The public instrument exposes terminal potential/current. LeadAcidReadout provides explicit model analysis of concentration, porosity and electrode response; it does not invent lithium surface fractions or laboratory sensors. Run an eleven-action discharge/rest/partial-recharge example with exact replay:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_lead_acid --output /tmp/lead-acid-new.jsonl

Defaults are an explicitly synthetic, volume-compatible closed material, not the default Sulzer material set or measured-cell qualification. Changing geometry or material requires all six initial amounts explicitly. Initial acid and water must fill the real pores, and reaction molar volumes must preserve closed saturation. Unsupported combinations are rejected; water is not added to repair volume. Initial zero sulfate permits discharge, while finite reactant, acid/water, pore and voltage boundaries stop the actual trajectory. Inward reversal may resume it. Old lithium device/slot codecs remain unchanged; the lead-acid cell uses its own chemical slot type in the same runtime. Equipment replacement continues to require the same equipment type.

This finite leading-order model has no spatial transport loss, double layer, hydrolysis, thermal/chemical-energy closure, side reactions, EIS or automatic SOH. Its independent source comparison and any unresolved cases are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV45_LOQS_EXPERIMENT.md; functional availability alone is not a claim of complete scientific qualification.

docs.title: Separate electrode OCV and resistance
docs.text:
BatterySplitOCVRSpec represents two finite electrode Li inventories, separate capacity/OCV declarations, and a series resistance. It has no radial particles, BV kinetics or electrolyte concentration state. Discharge moves Li from the negative electrode to the positive electrode; the same two amounts determine both OCVs and terminal voltage. Capacities are in coulombs, resistance in ohms, and initial mean fractions and each electrode's lower/upper limits are explicit.

from chemworld.physchem import BatterySplitOCVRSpec, split_ocvr_readout
from chemworld.world.battery_world import battery_world_spec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime

cell = BatterySplitOCVRSpec()
runtime = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=battery_world_spec(cell))
runtime.reset(seed=4)
runtime.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control", "current_A": 0.5})
runtime.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 3.0})
measurement = runtime.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "battery_meter"})
runtime.close()

Run the eleven-action example with exact replay:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_split_ocvr --output /tmp/split-ocvr-new.jsonl

The model uses the existing generic electrical equipment declaration and Li inventory slot, meter, queue, shared clock and initialization semantics. Its readout reports mean electrode fractions and ohmic drop, without inventing surface fractions. A positive resistance supports finite-current CV. With zero resistance, CC remains defined, but CV is rejected because current is nonunique at the requested OCV and otherwise cannot attain that voltage.

Ordinary battery_impedance uses this model's same residual at an interior state; its response represents the OCV inventory derivative and resistance, not an RC or diffusion model. soh_from_battery and battery_spec_at_soc reuse the original equilibrium root/branch analysis with the declared capacities, actual total Li and physical fraction domains. A requested voltage window must be reachable; an absent or ambiguous branch is not a valid SOC estimate. These analyses do not advance or rewrite the real cell state.

Defaults are explicitly synthetic curves and capacities. Thermal coupling, complete chemical-energy closure, side reactions and particle transport are unsupported. The actual released SplitOCVR reference contains only two mean fractions and charge under prescribed current; native CV and terminal work are checked against separate analytical references. Numerical qualification and all retained differences are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV45_SPLIT_OCVR_EXPERIMENT.md.

docs.title: Finite SPM lithium plating and stripping
docs.text:
An optional LithiumPlatingSpec on BatterySPMSpec adds two actual metal-Li inventories to the original cell equipment slot. A sourced parameter table declares the kinetic rate (m/s), transfer coefficient, fixed electrolyte concentration (mol/m^3), and negative electrode geometric volume (m^3). The reversible mode transfers Li between the active negative particle and plated metal; the irreversible mode deposits into dead Li and has no stripping term. Initial plated and dead amounts are explicit, independent inputs.

The side current and intercalation current share one negative electrode potential and sum to the terminal current. The two original radial diffusion problems, circuit constraint and side-current equation use the same residual solver and analytical Jacobian. At zero terminal current, reversible metal can reintercalate while external charge and terminal work remain zero. Neither metal stock is a post-step SOC correction, and side current is not bounded by the external source's current limit.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_plating --output /tmp/plating-new.jsonl

This eleven-action synthetic example charges, rests, discharges and verifies exact replay through the original runtime. CC, finite-current CV, the existing I/V meter, staged control, shared clocks and JSON continuation use the ordinary battery interfaces. Measurement time advances the cell. Material reset preserves the equipment-owned stocks; replacing the cell initializes new stocks once. The occupied volume is the fixed negative geometric volume plus positive active volume, not a complete cell geometry or dynamic porosity model.

The SPM declaration is isothermal with fixed electrolyte and certified nonincreasing, single-valued electrode OCVs. SEI combinations, partial reversibility, thermal coupling, pore evolution, cracking and complete chemical-energy closure are not defined by this model. Existing EIS, SOH and SOC analyses reject a plating-enabled cell rather than silently omit its metal inventory. The default example is not a calibrated commercial-cell degradation model. Actual released-source comparison and all numerical differences are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV46_PLATING_EXPERIMENT.md.

The same LithiumPlatingSpec can be declared on BatteryMPMSpec for a single-material particle distribution in each electrode. Each size bin retains its actual radial Li profile and its own reaction current at the shared electrode potential. There is still only one negative plated/dead Li pair. The side reaction uses the sum of actual particle surface areas; a nominal representative radius does not replace that sum. The particle distributions retain their sourced number/area/volume basis and explicit volume weights.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_mpm_plating --output /tmp/mpm-plating-new.jsonl

plating_fields exposes per-bin reaction currents and profiles alongside the shared metal response. battery_readout reports capacity-weighted mean fractions and area-weighted surface fractions and overpotentials. These averages do not replace individual bin cutoff checks. battery_particle_flux returns the total molar flux for the requested electrode, not one bin's flux. All original equipment and electrical actions apply to this model; replacing a cell can install a different distribution without preserving the old cell's metal stocks. Thermal, SEI, directional OCP, multi-material composites and porosity evolution remain outside this combination, and EIS/SOH/SOC stay explicitly unavailable. Continuous-distribution source comparisons and their finite-grid limits are documented separately in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONV46_MPM_PLATING_EXPERIMENT.md.

docs.title: SPM metal deactivation at an explicit constant rate
docs.text:
LithiumPlatingSpec(mode="partially reversible", ...) adds an explicit, sourced gamma_s_inv column in 1/s to the original four plating parameters. Its separate schema version is required for that five-column declaration; the original reversible and irreversible declarations remain unchanged. The interfacial current still follows reversible plating/stripping kinetics. Independently, the declared constant rate transfers actual plated Li to dead Li: d(plated)/dt = -q_strip/F - gamma*plated and d(dead)/dt = gamma*plated. This transfer creates no additional terminal current or charge receipt. Both inventories remain in the original equipment slot.

With gamma=0 the response reduces to reversible plating. With k=0, seeded metal still deactivates exponentially; turning off electrochemical exchange does not silently turn off the declared loss process. Zero plated Li has zero deactivation rate and is an admissible initial state. Replacing material retains the cell history; replacing equipment installs the explicitly declared new cell.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_partial_plating --output /tmp/partial-plating-new.jsonl

The example uses synthetic parameters, including an explicit nonzero initial dead-Li stock. This initialization extension is distinct from the actual PyBaMM source comparison, whose initial dead concentration is zero. The constant-rate source function is defined at zero SEI thickness; no fictitious film or inverse-thickness default is inserted. This version supports SPM only: the actual reference version's MPM partial-plating model fails during domain construction. Existing MPM reversible/irreversible modes remain available. SEI coupling, thermal physics, porosity, cracking, EIS/SOH/SOC and complete chemical energy remain outside this mode. A synthetic constant loss rate does not establish a material mechanism or a calibrated battery lifetime.

docs.title: Axen memory coupled to reversible SPM plating
docs.text:
An isothermal BatterySPMSpec can combine the existing Axen electrode OCP declarations with LithiumPlatingSpec(mode="reversible", ...). Each electrode may use its single OCP or an explicitly sourced Axen branch pair. The original particle amounts, metal stocks and electrode memory coordinates are retained in the same equipment slot.

The memory follows the actual main intercalation current. With stripping current positive, the negative electrode uses q_main = I - q_strip; the positive electrode uses -I. Consequently, at zero terminal current, internal stripping can continue to change negative-electrode memory while terminal charge and electrical work stay zero.
