The evolving branch mixture feeds the same Butler–Volmer closure and finite-voltage controller. Current-sigmoid OCP has a different source definition and is not silently reinterpreted here.

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.battery_axen_plating --output /tmp/axen-plating-new.jsonl

The example reuses the synthetic OCP and plating declarations and executes the original charge/rest/discharge workflow with exact action replay. Meter acquisition time, queued stages, shared time, material reset and equipment replacement all act on the same persistent cell. The two supported noise modes remain available via --noise.

This combination requires certified nonincreasing branches and the existing isothermal finite-source domain. MPM with directional OCP and plating, current-sigmoid with plating, Axen with partial/irreversible plating, SEI, thermal physics, ordinary stationary EIS/SOH/SOC and complete chemical energy remain outside this combination. Operational memory does not itself define a thermodynamic hysteresis-energy law or a calibrated degradation mechanism.

docs.title: Historical temperature calibration
docs.text:
temperature_convert(value_K, current, desired) supports ITS-90 and the complete tabulated ITS-68, ITS-48, ITS-27 and ITS-76 ranges. Historical IPTS/EPT aliases are accepted explicitly. Each historical scale uses one cubic calibration and the shared bounded root solver for its inverse; domains use actual mapped endpoints. temperature_scale_conversion also returns the derivative of that same mapping. The Kelvin/Celsius unit system and world temperature semantics remain unchanged.

from chemworld.foundation.units import Quantity
from chemworld.physchem import temperature_quantity, water_refractive_index_iapws

calibrated = temperature_quantity(Quantity(26.85, "degC"), "IPTS-68", "ITS-90")
index = water_refractive_index_iapws(calibrated.value, 997)

temperature_input preserves original input and scale provenance in the existing InputValue note. temperature_observation retains the raw scalar channel and adds a derived channel in the original Observation, with sample/timestamps and native JSON roundtrip. Measurement uncertainty uses first-order derivative propagation; unknown calibration uncertainty stays unknown. Invalid numeric readings and curves requiring per-point uncertainty are explicitly rejected by this scalar adapter.

its90_68_difference is a separate approximate polynomial method. Its default published_overlap fills the old documentation's low-temperature gap with the published middle polynomial. Explicit convention="chemicals_1_5_2" reproduces the older API's zero correction in that gap and its junction choices. Such zeros are compatibility behavior, not evidence that the scales coincide. Neither method asserts thermodynamic-temperature accuracy or silently modifies caloric references. Full node/interval, cross-function and source-inventory development evidence is recorded in the foundation acceptance document. The original 285-row primary-CAS gap remains the qualification denominator: 221 rows now have reviewed component mappings, while 64 rows across 54 CAS numbers remain unresolved. Earlier source failures and conflicting structures remain visible.

docs.title: Composition, flow and partial-molar utilities
docs.text:
The native composition_math and fluid_response modules cover the 63 scientific public functions in chemicals.utils 1.5.2, through shared mathematical operations. They require no reference package at runtime. MixtureSpec uses the same fraction conversion and normalization functions; pure virial gas reports use the same density, compressibility and heat-capacity identities.

from chemworld.physchem import (
    fraction_basis, convert_component_flows, solve_stream_composition,
    partial_molar_properties, composition_gradient_to_moles,
)

molecular_weights = (18., 44., 70.)  # g/mol
mass_fractions = fraction_basis((.2, .3, .5), molecular_weights)
mass_flows = convert_component_flows(
    (2., 3., 5.), source="molar", target="mass",
    molecular_weights=molecular_weights,
)  # kg/s from mol/s
flows, zs, ws = solve_stream_composition(
    (2., None, None), (None, .3, None), (None, None, 350/518),
    molecular_weights,
)
partial = partial_molar_properties(13., (-5., 3., 9.), zs)
dn = composition_gradient_to_moles((-5., 3., 9.), zs, total_moles=10.)

Reference-liquid volume conversion requires the component reference molar volumes in m³/mol; it does not calculate the actual volume of a mixed stream. A mixed flow specification supplies exactly one molar flow, mole fraction or mass fraction per component, including a positive absolute flow scale. Merging streams retains component identities. Unknown partial-flow streams contribute zero only when explicitly supplied as None. Zero total has no defined composition.

weighted_property supplies linear, logarithmic and real power means. The power mean has the geometric limit at exponent zero; non-linear means require positive properties. regularized_fractions is explicit preprocessing of zeros, and is never applied to an inventory automatically. Partial-molar conversions distinguish unconstrained fractions, the n−1 simplex and mole numbers at a stated total amount; the extensive Hessian includes the required first-derivative contributions.

fluid_response supplies density/volume and mass/molar property conversion, specific gravity/API/Baume scales, Watson characterization, parachor, molecular radius of gyration, vapor mass quality and thermodynamic response identities. All use SI except molecular weight in g/mol and explicitly named gravity scales. acoustic_velocity returns m/s when molecular weight is provided, otherwise m·sqrt(kg/mol)/s. Pressure/volume derivatives must refer to the same state; derivative-based phase classification is not a phase-equilibrium calculation.

The fixed public comparison retains two discrepancies at power exponent 1.5: the native result follows the documented equation, verified independently with 60-digit arithmetic (26/26 power-mean inputs); chemicals 1.5.2 agrees on 24/26. The complete public comparison remains 203/205, not an all-pass claim. Six independent partial-molar states also verify amount scaling, Euler and Gibbs–Duhem identities. Input parsing and generic shape/copy/hash/JIT helpers are outside this scientific reproduction scope.

docs.title: Pure-fluid Helmholtz properties
docs.text:
chemworld.data.load_helmholtz_fluid imports an explicitly supplied public coefficient mapping and source. A multi-EOS source requires eos_index. fluid.state(temperature_K=..., molar_density_mol_m3=...) computes pressure, H/U/S, heat capacities, sound speed and response derivatives from the same native energy function; fluid.alpha_derivative(...) exposes mixed derivatives through order three. No CoolProp installation is used by this production path.

load_helmholtz_phase_model also imports critical values and ancillary guesses. Its saturation(T) solves equal pressure and chemical potential; solve_tp(...) selects an explicit or automatic homogeneous branch. A coexistence T/P pair does not determine a unique density. solve_homogeneous_state(inputs, initial_state=...) supports pairs drawn from T/P/rho/H/U/S with an explicit starting state and reports local closure, not a two-phase flash.

The existing ComponentPropertyPackage.evaluate_state(..., helmholtz_model=phase_model) returns normal unit-bearing property reports for the same component identity. EOS caloric offsets are preserved; do not also supply an unrelated reference or gas model. Branch diagnostics, source M/R and source identity remain in the report. Uniform-state checks establish local stability; they do not guarantee global phase equilibrium. Pseudo-pure phase closure and unprovided transport laws remain explicit unsupported requests.

Explicit viscosity, conductivity or liquid surface-tension correlations in the same component package can accompany these EOS properties. They retain their own source, phase, selection policy and validity range; the EOS supplies no implicit transport law.

HelmholtzIsochoricThermodynamics connects the same EOS to CoupledSystem for one homogeneous pure-fluid inventory at a declared fixed volume. Heating and material exchange use nU, nCv and the density-dependent inventory energy derivative; port enthalpy uses the same fluid reference. Both original ODE and residual strategies apply. Empty inventories, changing volumes, foreign fluids and duplicate reaction heat are rejected. Numerical tolerances must resolve the original energy balance; the adapter does not weaken that balance.

Install this thermodynamics object in the existing ThermalSystemSpec(..., pressure_law="helmholtz") for native heat, wait, pause/resume control and snapshots. The original vessel inventory owns n/T/V; pressure and pressure-stop events use the same EOS. Material replacement mixes the new fluid energy with retained support energy. This world mode accepts one pure-fluid inventory and no concurrent reaction or undeclared material port.

Choose HelmholtzEquilibriumIsochoricThermodynamics explicitly for liquid–gas equilibrium, supplying the phase model and the same fixed-volume inventory. Its heat capacity includes the latent-energy response along constant density; it is not an average of endpoint Cv values. A native world uses the aggregate phase="fluid" declaration: n/T/V remain the sole inventory, and equilibrium phase amounts are derived from the EOS. The original thermal actions, pressure events, material replacement and snapshots consume this declaration. Pseudo-pure glide, solids and changing volumes are outside this model. Independent tests cover heating and cooling across the coexistence boundary with both numerical forms.

solve_two_phase_state(model, inputs) closes independent pairs drawn from T/P/rho/H/U/S/Q on pure-fluid liquid–gas coexistence. T/P alone cannot determine quality; pairs without T or P require an explicit temperature guess. flash_at_pressure(model, pressure_Pa=..., coordinate="H", value=...) selects the two-phase or stable homogeneous branch; U, S and rho are also supported. Quality is vapor mole fraction, which equals mass fraction for one pure fluid. Volume mixes by phase volume, while H/U/S mix by amount. These APIs supply no unqualified two-phase Cp, sound speed or transport average.

HelmholtzPressureStage models an adiabatic throttle, compressor or expander using the same H/S reference. Its evaluate(HelmholtzStream(state, rate)) returns outlet state and shaft power; compression and expansion apply their declared isentropic efficiency to a PS reference state. A resolved two-phase outlet can be separated into conserving liquid and gas streams. A stream's contribution(port_id) supplies the existing material port's molar flow and enthalpy to CoupledSystem. Shaft work is already in outlet enthalpy and must not be added to the receiving tank again. Rates are explicit reservoir inputs; the stage supplies no pressure-driven flow law.

The implementation has exercised all 159 source EOS parameter sets for alpha and its derivatives, and the full 136-fluid default-EOS catalogue for phase and state-pair behavior. These are distinct coverage claims. The fixed phase block retains 21 exceptions: 20 targets outside the source's valid physical domain and one low-temperature propylene-glycol disagreement with the reference saturation solver. Separate source-domain and equal-pressure/equal-chemical-potential checks are recorded; those checks do not relabel the original exceptions as passes. Ancillary correlations provide initial guesses only. Extrapolating a guess is reported and never extends the EOS temperature or pressure validity range.

docs.title: Liquid valves and differential-pressure meters
docs.text:
LiquidControlValveSpec declares installed metric Kv, geometry, recovery and style factors. size_liquid_control_valve performs IEC engineering selection; liquid_valve_pressure_drop and liquid_valve_flow evaluate the installed single-liquid relation. Nominal conservative sizing is not an exact inverse. Low-Re flow with attached reducers remains unsupported.

LiquidOrificeSpec supports ISO 5167 corner, flange and D-D/2 taps, or an explicit calibrated coefficient with a declared Reynolds interval. Its pressure report separates measured differential pressure from permanent pressure loss. Mass-flow, bore and pressure-endpoint inverses share the same equation. Lab-scale geometry requires an explicit calibration; it does not inherit industrial ISO validity. All inputs are SI except explicitly named metric Kv in m³/h.

Set TransportPathSpec.control_valve and .orifice_meter to use these devices in the existing finite pump/pipe/receiver world. The installed valve requires a pure liquid package, an explicit vapor-pressure curve and component.metadata['critical_pressure_Pa']. Current properties determine the operating point. The original amount/enthalpy inventories, energy accounting, shared clock and snapshot restoration are retained. A closed valve blocks transfer and shaft work; a single-liquid path rejects flashing conditions.

LiquidTransportProperties(activity_model=...) can include the same declared activity model in liquid enthalpy, heat capacity and stream heat transfer. Nonideal mixing then changes the receiver temperature through its existing enthalpy inventory. The model and provenance survive ordinary world snapshots. This retains a homogeneous single-liquid assumption; liquid-liquid phase splitting and excess volume are separate models.

docs.title: Isothermal gas-pipe engineering
docs.text:
IsothermalGasState declares constant temperature, specific gas constant and Z. isothermal_gas_pipe(...) computes mass flow with density changing as P/(Z R T). solve_isothermal_gas_pipe(...) solves one missing mass flow, inlet pressure, outlet pressure, diameter or length using the same equation. Pressure inverses update inlet density. Darcy friction and Z are explicit constants, and the result reports the critical outlet pressure and capacity. Equal pressures give zero flow; outlets below the choking boundary are rejected. These steady engineering calculations do not create a dynamic gas inventory.

Constant-gamma engineering helpers also cover isothermal and isentropic work, compression/expansion efficiency, outlet temperature, polytropic exponent, stagnation states and critical conditions. ideal_gas_nozzle(...) reports subcritical or choked flow for an ideal converging nozzle. Work is positive into the gas, with separate compression and expansion efficiency conventions.

EmpiricalGasPipelineSpec selects IGT, Muller, Fritzsche, Panhandle A/B, Weymouth, Oliphant or Spitzglass high/low and records its applicability. solve_empirical_gas_pipeline(...) solves Q/P1/P2/D/L; Q is volume flow at the declared reference T/P, not local pipe volume flow. Pressure-squared models require absolute pressure. Oliphant has no efficiency or Z correction and rejects non-unity inputs instead of silently ignoring them.

docs.title: Uniform channels and free-discharge weirs
docs.text:
manning_velocity, chezy_velocity and their coefficient conversions use SI roughness in s/m^(1/3) and Chezy coefficients in m^0.5/s. uniform_channel_flow uses explicit area, wetted perimeter and energy slope; it is a steady relation. manning_roughness_table imports a source's nested minimum/normal/maximum values into the original ScientificTable, and select_manning_roughness selects an exact category path. These statistics are not standard uncertainties, and external roughness tables are not bundled.

weir_flow covers Shen V notches and the declared rectangular Kindsvater–Carter, Ackers and Rehbock relations with geometric domain checks. Both historical SIA expressions require reference_only=True and return explicit validity warnings; the full-width expression is dimensionally inconsistent and its source warns against use. Reproducing either expression does not qualify it as a flow meter. Submerged flow, water jumps and unprovided installation corrections are outside these free-discharge formulas.

docs.title: Gas control valves
docs.text:
GasControlValveSpec declares installed Kv, geometry, recovery, style and pressure-ratio factors. size_gas_control_valve selects nominal Kv; gas_valve_flow evaluates a fixed installed valve and returns reference volume flow, mass flow and actual inlet volume flow separately. Reference volume uses 273.15 K and 101325 Pa. Low-Re nominal selection is conservative and is not an exact inverse of installed flow.

The default expansion_basis="installed" uses the installed xTP in the expansion factor, including the choked plateau. gas_valve_outlet_pressure solves the unique subcritical branch and returns the highest choked outlet at capacity. bare_valve_reference explicitly reproduces fluids 1.3.1's fixed bare-xT expansion convention; pressure inversion requires the installed convention. Low-Re flow with attached reducers requires an additional declared correction and is rejected. These engineering functions do not introduce a dynamic gas inventory into the single-liquid transport world.

ValveOpeningCurve.apply(full_open_spec, opening) sets the original gas or liquid valve's effective Kv and closed state. Linear opening is exact; quick and equal-percentage curves require an explicit sourced TabulatedScalar. The curve and source survive JSON roundtrip. Scaling always starts from the full-open rating. Coefficient conversion supports Kv/Cv/Av, and the cavitation and choking helpers retain explicit pressure/recovery conventions.

liquid_control_valve_noise and gas_control_valve_noise consume declared ValveAcousticGeometry and operating properties. They report 33 frequency bands, total A-weighted level, peak frequency, sound power and flow regime. The gas model includes five regimes and the outlet-expander contribution. Its default outlet density includes the stated T1/T2 ratio at fixed Z; supply actual outlet density explicitly when the property model requires it. These are engineering acoustic predictions, not a spatial sound-field simulation.

docs.title: Pneumatic conveying thresholds
docs.text: saltation_velocity selects Rizk, Schade, Geldart-Ling, three Matsumoto variants or Weber using current gas FluidState, solid mass flow and declared geometry. Particle density and terminal velocity are explicit where required. Results include velocity, gas volume/mass flow, the selected branch and source warnings. Matsumoto 1974/1975 retain the reference's unresolved high-prediction warning. These are empirical transport thresholds, not evolving particle trajectories or a model of plugging and recovery.

docs.title: Straight, helical and plate friction
docs.text:
straight_friction_correlation exposes 34 named equations and explicit Darcy or Fanning factors. pipe_friction_factor adds a declared laminar transition; available_straight_friction_methods filters known source ranges. Colebrook and Clamond represent the same physical equation here and share the existing root solver. crane_fully_turbulent_friction uses its nominal-steel effective inputs.

helical_friction_factor supports 11 helical models, six transition correlations, Dean number and model-specific curvature/roughness limits. plate_friction_factor provides Kumar, Martin 1999/VDI and Muley-Manglik with explicit chevron geometry. Published fit discontinuities and undefined source ranges remain visible; formula evaluation outside recommended ranges requires an explicit choice.

docs.title: Screens and grills
docs.text:
filter_loss_coefficient covers round wire screens, four open-mesh patterns, square screens and square/round grills. filter_pressure_drop uses current FluidState density and viscosity, a declared Reynolds length and the upstream approach velocity. Long-grill friction requires thickness, passage hydraulic diameter and Darcy factor together; the extra term starts above 50 diameters.

FilterCurve wraps an existing sourced TabulatedScalar, with linear or quadratic interpolation and explicit raise/clip endpoint behavior. Blevins curve arrays are supplied by the caller. Recommended open fractions and turbulent mesh flow are checked. This is an engineering pressure calculation; it does not simulate particle capture or progressive filter fouling.

docs.title: Packed-bed pressure laws
docs.text:
PackedBedSpec selects one of 14 pressure correlations with explicit length, particle size, voidage, sphericity and, where consumed, tube diameter. packed_bed_pressure accepts the existing FluidState, reports particle and modified Reynolds numbers, and returns source-range notes. range_policy="raise" requires all available range qualifications. Ergun reuses the original kernel. packed_bed_voidage supplies the general, spherical and cylindrical Benyahia-O'Neil estimates within their declared geometry ranges.

The existing TransportPathSpec accepts bed_method, bed_sphericity and bed_tube_diameter_m. They feed its current-property pressure loss and pump working point while retaining the same material and enthalpy inventories. Guo-Sun requires a real tube diameter; negative predicted pressure loss is rejected. The cylindrical voidage law does not accept an unused sphericity.

docs.title: Gas/liquid holdup and mixture viscosity
docs.text:
TwoPhaseProperties declares both phase densities and any required viscosities, surface tension or pressure. two_phase_void_fraction exposes 29 named models; two_phase_mixture_viscosity exposes six. Mass quality and volumetric void fraction are separate inputs: at equal mass, a low-density vapor can occupy most of the volume. Density and its void-fraction inverse use the same declared phase values.

Availability functions describe input completeness. Known recommended ranges are checked by default; an explicit formula-analysis option can disable those range checks. Nonphysical void fractions still raise with the unmodified prediction. Pure phases use exact zero/one endpoints. These engineering correlations do not create a dynamic two-phase inventory or establish validity for every flow regime.

two_phase_pressure_drop evaluates 24 named pressure relationships with explicit properties, geometry and quality. Its report distinguishes friction-only loss from Beggs-Brill's coupled friction, holdup and gravity result. The primitive Beggs acceleration correction is an explicit option, off by default. Bankoff requires reference_only=True because its source warns against engineering use. Known recommended ranges are checked by default; an explicit formula-analysis request retains warnings. Model inputs are not a general validity certificate.

colebrook_friction_factor uses the shared root solver. The separate engineering pipe_friction_factor uses an explicit transition Reynolds number, default 2040; the existing transport auto/Haaland convention retains its original behavior.

Signed gravity and acceleration APIs operate on explicit phase endpoints or local derivatives. Expansion at constant density produces pressure recovery; the upstream reference's opposite area-term sign is recorded as a discrepancy. These functions preserve mass-quality versus void-fraction bases.

The Mandhane-Gregory-Aziz and Taitel-Dukler flow-map APIs return SI superficial velocities and the selected regime. Taitel-Dukler consumes three caller-supplied LogRegimeBoundary curves through existing sourced tables. Chart extrapolation is off by default. The selected Colebrook convention differs from the original paper's Blasius convention and is reported in the result.

docs.title: Relief sizing and flare noise
docs.text:
size_gas_relief_valve, size_liquid_relief_valve and size_steam_relief_valve solve API-style area or inverse mass flow with explicit pressure, discharge and correction factors. Steam service must be declared dry saturated or superheated; these engineering formulas do not classify phase. api526_select_orifice selects the next of 14 effective standard areas.

API520 correction tables are explicit, source-bearing TabulatedScalar inputs; standard table data are not bundled. Table domains are strict unless a supported call explicitly requests endpoint clipping, and standard model limits still apply. The liquid viscosity correction retains the declared two-step sizing convention. api521_flare_noise applies distance attenuation; vdi3732_flare_noise uses tonnes/hour converted from kg/s by 3.6. The latter intentionally differs from fluids 1.3.1's factor of 360. These are sizing/noise relations, not a dynamic two-phase relief model.

docs.title: Activity thermodynamics and liquid property consumption
docs.text:
The existing ActivityModelSpec supports ideal, Margules, Wilson, NRTL, UNIQUAC, regular solution, Flory–Huggins, Hansen and six UNIFAC variants through a shared excess Gibbs-energy contract. Request excess H, S, Cp, analytic temperature/composition derivatives and partial molar quantities with activity_thermodynamic_report(model, composition, temperature_K=...) from chemworld.physchem. activity_infinite_dilution(...) evaluates exact zero solute concentration in explicitly supplied remaining solvent proportions. The results are immutable and provide to_dict() for JSON output.

regular_solution_model(...) compiles explicit reference molar volumes, solubility parameters and directed interaction corrections. Without a correction request it records explicit zero corrections; incomplete supplied pairs fail. hansen_activity_model(...) consumes source-bearing HansenParameters and unit-bearing reference volumes, with an explicit alpha. These models hold reference volumes and cohesive parameters constant in temperature. The sum of opposite regular-solution corrections is identifiable; fitting cannot identify the two directions separately. Source data remain in the model's provenance.

Pass activity_model=model to the existing evaluate_property_state(...) liquid interface to combine these responses with declared pure-liquid caloric references. Supported requests include enthalpy, cp, entropy, chemical_potential and activity_coefficient. Component IDs must match the property packages. An activity-only request needs no unrequested heat-capacity data; entropy and chemical potentials require explicit entropy references. The model supplies neither a volume law nor a constant-volume energy closure.

chemworld.data.ActivityCalibration fits explicit model coefficients through the existing bounded calibration driver. Its ScientificTable conditions contain temperature and all component fractions; observations may contain ln-gamma, GE, HE, SE or CpE. Training and holdout groups remain separate, and fitting retains the actual evaluation ledger. These functions do not imply a complete interaction-parameter database, group-contribution coverage or measured material accuracy. Asymmetric Margules results now follow an integrable three-suffix equation; the former componentwise expression was thermodynamically inconsistent.

unifac_activity_model(...) accepts explicit molecular subgroup counts, source-bearing subgroup parameters and every directed unlike-main-group interaction. Versions 0–5 select original/LLE, Dortmund/NIST, PSRK, VTPR, Lyngby/Larsen and KT. The returned ActivityModelSpec uses the same caloric, derivative, dilution, calibration and liquid-property interfaces above. Group topology is discrete; only continuous interaction coefficients are fit.

The chemworld.data readers read_unifac_subgroups, read_unifac_interactions, iter_ddbst_text and iter_ddbst_sqlite consume explicit local source files. select_unifac_interactions requires an explicit choice for overlapping revisions and retains superseded records. unifac_model_from_assignments maps declared native component identities to source assignments; automatic DDBST numbering applies to versions 0/1/2 only. Missing interactions and invalid assignments fail explicitly. Source temperature ranges remain provenance; they are not automatically enforced as model domains. The source tables and the reference package are not runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Cubic EOS alpha and Bell2018 parameters
docs.text:
EOSComponentSpec retains its default Soave alpha and can explicitly select alpha_model="twu91" with the (L, M, N) coefficient tuple and source provenance. cubic_alpha_response reports alpha and its first three analytic temperature derivatives. The original PR/SRK state and departure-property calculations consume the selected alpha directly.

chemworld.data.twu_eos_component_from_record consumes an existing BELL_TWU phase-change record, preserving its InChIKey, Tc/Pc, coefficients and source. An optional native component must match that identity. Bell supplies no acentric factor; the legacy zero field is unused by this explicit Twu path. Full source consumption establishes equation compatibility, not transferability of fitted coefficients between EOS families or measured predictive accuracy.

docs.title: Predictive PR78 interactions
docs.text:
PPR78Spec binds explicit molecular groups to a selected original or extended interaction table and its provenance. Missing or asymmetric pairs are errors. ppr78_interaction_response supplies k and its first three temperature derivatives. Use CubicEOSSpec(pure_parameterization="pr78", predictive_interaction=...) to consume those predictions in the original EOS roots, fugacities and departure properties. Temperature-dependent k contributes to mixture da/dT and hence H/S.

This path uses exact PR78 constants and its high-acentric-factor branch with Soave alpha. It rejects SRK, Twu and simultaneous constant interactions; existing legacy PR/SRK defaults remain available. Explicit group assignment is required. Full source consumption verifies equations, not material prediction accuracy; combinations with negative mixture attraction are outside the admitted EOS domain.

docs.title: Excess-Gibbs cubic mixing
docs.text:
GibbsExcessMixingSpec connects the existing activity models to PR/SRK through Huron-Vidal, exact MHV, MHV1, MHV2 or Wong-Sandler. Set it as CubicEOSSpec.ge_mixing. MHV1/2 require explicit q coefficients; Wong-Sandler requires every unlike binary pair. Quadratic and predictive interactions cannot be silently combined with GE mixing. Exact MHV requires a differentiable zero-pressure liquid branch.

The original EOS roots remain the state solver. Fugacity, enthalpy and entropy differentiate one residual Helmholtz potential, including Wong-Sandler's temperature-dependent covolume. Thus selecting a new mixing rule changes both phase behavior and energy consistently. The existing activity families and all six UNIFAC variants can use this interface; model choice and material calibration remain explicit.

docs.title: Unified homogeneous phase properties
docs.text:
PhasePropertyModel freezes existing component packages, phase, references, activity/EOS choices and explicit transport declarations. For one component, use package.phase_model(phase=..., reference=...); a pure Helmholtz model may be supplied with its own caloric reference. capabilities() shows structurally available quantities. evaluate(amounts, temperature_K=..., pressure_Pa=..., quantities=...) reads caller-owned amounts and returns an immutable PhaseEvaluation with units, sources, validity and composition.

PhaseTransportSpec selects one of 12 existing mixture transport methods. Pure curves are evaluated at current conditions, with explicit method parameters; LBC consumes current volume, and Diguilio-Teja consumes pure surface tension at each boiling temperature. Fixed-composition correlations require composition binding. Missing sources or closures stay unavailable. This interface owns no inventory, clock or phase-split solver, and preserves existing JSON declarations.

docs.title: Properties from declared molecular groups
docs.text:
GroupContributionTable stores a selected source's coefficients, including explicit missing values. joback_estimate produces all eleven Joback outputs; structural_group_estimate handles Fedors critical volume, first/second-order Wilson–Jasperson critical properties and Bondi volume, surface, R and Q. Inputs are explicit molecular groups, atom counts and structural features. These APIs do not perform SMILES fragmentation.

GroupEstimateReport.critical_estimate(...) feeds the existing critical-property and cubic-EOS inputs. joback_property_correlations(...) compiles Cp and viscosity into the original property catalogue for an authored temperature interval. Missing increments remain unavailable; a partial area or arbitrary replacement critical temperature is not returned as a complete estimate. Predicted formation energy does not silently establish an absolute caloric reference, and source coverage does not establish predictive accuracy for every material.

docs.title: Formal SBML models on the native world
docs.text:
Given a provenance-bearing SBMLModel, declare its numerical profile and the quantities that an instrument may observe:

from chemworld.physchem.sbml_system import SBMLObservable
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.sbml_world import sbml_world

world = sbml_world(model, maximum_step_s=0.02,
                   observables=(SBMLObservable("amount", "A"),))
runtime = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=world, observation_noise_mode="keyed")
runtime.reset(seed=4)
runtime.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 0.25})
runtime.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "formal_quantity_meter"})
reading = runtime.observe()  # declared mol channel with detector uncertainty
saved = runtime.snapshot().to_dict()  # private continuation; keep outside agent payloads
restored = ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(saved)

The bounded Level 3 Version 2 profile supports explicit 3D compartments, source units, kinetic laws, initial/assignment/rate rules and transverse inequality events with delays, cancellation, captured assignments and execution priorities. Unsupported semantics are rejected. Events require an authored finite maximum step; arbitrarily fast crossings and tangencies have no general guarantee.

One existing equipment entity owns all live amounts, compartment volumes, parameters and pending events. The existing shared laboratory clock owns time. numerical_form="residual" selects the common residual solver. Source quantities become mol, L and seconds at explicit boundaries; model formulas retain their source basis. A concentration rate rule includes the volume chain term, and an event concentration assignment uses the volume immediately before execution.

The workspace has no physical chemical stock or liquid heat capacity. Formal coordinates do not establish elemental, charge, energy or carrier-mass closure, and heat/material sampling operations are unavailable. The gauge is instantaneous and consumes no sample; its allowed amount/concentration/volume channels carry mol, mol/L or L with declared Gaussian uncertainty. Public state omits evolving coordinates and queues. Material preparation preserves the formal entity; a full experiment reset initializes it again. A failed event cascade rolls back the complete advance. Full private snapshots preserve pending events and detector continuation across processes.

The fixed native-world block passed all 36 runtime contracts and 770 independent closed-form comparisons. Full SDK parity remains explicitly false: the 18-model COPASI block has three retained differences, and RoadRunner has one source-model initialization difference. Official SBML volume/event cases and all raw failed attempts are retained in the foundation evidence records.

SEDMLProtocol compiles bounded SED-ML L1V4 model changes, uniform time courses, finite parameter scans and ordered or nested tasks into existing native worlds. run_sedml_experiment executes their native waits, measurements and declared parameter controls, returning reports with source units, sample coordinates and repeat axes. SEDMLProtocol.from_archive accepts a validated CombineArchive; archive import retains the original XML and resolves local model references. It executes no archive code and fetches no external models. Unsupported algorithms, targets or experiment structures are rejected before creating native sessions.

The twelve-case development block passed 910 independent analytic comparisons and 910 exact archive round-trip report comparisons. Complete SDK interoperability remains unqualified: retained differences include species readout bases, computed model changes, nested clocks and SDK failures on functional ranges or unequal subtasks. Final native model snapshots preserve those sessions. For the complete finite experiment, SEDMLExperimentSession in chemworld.eval.sedml_continuation also preserves the task stack, collected observations and future reset identities. Call advance(max_courses=1) to pause after a complete time course, serialize to_dict(), then restore with from_dict() and continue. This checkpoint is private: it contains native model state and must not be exposed as an agent observation. Failed continuations remain terminal and retain the actual operation prefix. The fixed twelve-protocol process block and explicit pending/terminal cases pass complete private JSON continuation checks under both detector noise modes. The complete four-entry block passes 304 successful and 32 expected-failure histories, all 336 replays, and 84 native process continuations across ODE/residual forms and both detector noise modes. The original failed recorder attempt remains preserved. Neutral optional CPU declarations preserve real saved v2 checkpoints, with the four-entry block, whole protocols and installed wheel requalified after the fix. Non-default and unknown execution contracts remain strict. Retained independent SDK disagreements remain separate from continuation correctness; see the supported scope and full results.

docs.title: Multifluid mixtures, local criticality and fitting
docs.text:
MultifluidModel combines explicitly supplied pure Helmholtz equations, oriented binary reducing parameters and departure terms. Import a complete declaration with chemworld.data.read_multifluid_model(path, source=...), or select named components from a caller-provided MultifluidSourceCatalog. Missing pairs are errors. The gas constant convention, component order, original source constants and fitted parameters remain explicit. Production does not download parameters or depend on teqp/CoolProp.

The model's caloric_model() returns the existing MolecularCaloricModel with source-derived ideal references. Use it with MolecularIsochoricThermodynamics, MolecularStream and CoupledSystem to advance real inventories and account for heat and incoming enthalpy. Model selection does not create another inventory. These homogeneous consumers require a locally stable state. General phase selection is a separate calculation with explicitly declared density basins.

For an already imported methane/ethane declaration ordered in that sequence:

from chemworld.physchem import (
    molecular_composition_response, solve_molecular_critical,
    trace_molecular_critical,
)

response = molecular_composition_response(model, 450.0, (250.0, 250.0))
critical = solve_molecular_critical(
    model, (0.5, 0.5), initial_temperature_K=260.0,
    initial_density_mol_m3=9000.0,
    temperature_bounds_K=(180.0, 350.0),
    density_bounds_mol_m3=(3000.0, 20000.0),
)
if critical.success:
    print(critical.response["temperature_K"], critical.response["pressure_Pa"])
else:
    print(critical.failure_reason, critical.diagnostics)

curve = trace_molecular_critical(
    model, ((0.4, 0.6), (0.5, 0.5), (0.6, 0.4)),
    initial_temperature_K=260.0, initial_density_mol_m3=9000.0,
    temperature_bounds_K=(180.0, 350.0),
    density_bounds_mol_m3=(3000.0, 20000.0),
)

Composition responses include ideal mixing, the full chemical-potential density Hessian, fixed-temperature/pressure and fixed-temperature/density composition responses, pressure derivatives and a susceptibility only when invertible and locally stable. Exact zero components select an active composition face; they do not request absent-component insertion derivatives. Critical roots require one soft mode, zero cubic coefficient, positive transverse curvature and a positive fourth coefficient after transverse relaxation. Singular heat capacity is not replaced by a finite placeholder. Source pressure limits still apply. The curve follows the supplied composition path and stops at an unresolved station; it does not claim to continue through every fold or prove global phase stability. Keep the returned failure and completed/requested station counts.

MultifluidCalibration fits declared continuous coefficients using the shared ScientificTable measurement schema, uncertainties and train/validation/test splits. Conditions default to temperature, molar_density and x:<component>; observations map to state fields, mu:<component> or lnphi:<component>. Parameters address an exact oriented binary pair, a departure coefficient or a pure residual amplitude. For example, with a prepared measurement table:

from chemworld.data import MultifluidCalibration, MultifluidFitParameter
from chemworld.physchem import MultifluidModel

pair = model.binary_pairs[0]
parameter = MultifluidFitParameter(
    "binary", pair.component_ids, "gamma_T",
    bounds=(0.9 * pair.gamma_T, 1.1 * pair.gamma_T), initial=pair.gamma_T,
)
report = MultifluidCalibration(
    table, model, (parameter,), fitted_source="My declared training dataset",
).fit(max_nfev=100)
if report["status"] == "fitted":
    fitted = MultifluidModel.from_dict(report["fitted_model"])
    caloric = fitted.caloric_model()

Inspect held-out errors, parameter bounds and the local identifiability report before using a fit. Fitting does not change source validity limits or add missing terms. Synthetic parameter recovery demonstrates the fitting interface, not empirical accuracy for a material. The fitted result uses the original model codec and carries a new source description.

Two explicit model combinations share these consumers:

  • MultifluidAssociationModel adds reciprocal cross-component association using the existing masked SAFT site solver. Same-component bonds must be disabled so the already fitted pure-fluid EOS is preserved.
  • MultifluidActivityModel uses the Jaeger activity departure with declared covolumes, reference density parameter and residual-activity convention. wilson_volume_residual removes the Wilson volume contribution explicitly; declared_residual means the caller supplied the residual activity model.

Both require combination_policy="explicit_joint_parameterization" and a source description. They preserve pure-fluid limits and the common gas constant, but do not inherit empirical qualification of the original mixture parameters. caloric_model() and the common codec carry the complete coupled potential into the original heat/material consumers. Validation uses the final coupled pressure.

docs.title: Finite native gas mechanisms
docs.text: This is a development feature, not a general Cantera/RMG interpreter or a claim of experimentally validated chemistry. It uses ChemWorld's existing reaction network, common inventory/energy integrator, thermal device, transactions and replay. Native execution does not import Cantera.

docs.title: Import and run
docs.text:
From the repository's locked environment:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.physchem.mechanism_import \
  tests/fixtures/mechanisms/cantera-3.1.0/h2o2.yaml \
  --phase ohmech --output /tmp/native-h2o2.json
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_gas_mechanism \
  tests/fixtures/mechanisms/cantera-3.1.0/h2o2.yaml \
  --phase ohmech --amounts '{"H2":0.00002,"O2":0.00001,"AR":0.00007}'

The converter refuses to overwrite an existing output. load_mechanism reads the exported native JSON. Source thermo, units, original reaction declarations and source provenance survive the round trip. When installed outside the checkout, the same module commands accept an explicit local source path; test fixtures are not bundled as hidden runtime data.

The example authors a 10-mL vessel at 700 K, with finite-power heating to 750 K, heat → pressure measurement → wait → pressure measurement → terminate. The pressure instrument uses the existing physical acquisition duration, so the total physical time includes measurements. Only the generic pressure instrument is exposed: the existing CO/O2/CO2 assay is not relabelled as a generic H2/O2 or arbitrary-species analyzer. Inventory is private state, not a fabricated assay.

docs.title: Supported finite contract
docs.text:
• One explicitly selected ideal-gas phase; no artificial species/reaction count ceiling. Every selected species/reaction is retained, or the import fails. An explicitly nonreacting gas (reactions: none) retains its thermochemistry.
  • NASA7, NASA9, Shomate, constant-Cp and piecewise-Gibbs standard-state thermo; Arrhenius, third-body, Lindemann/Troe/SRI/Tsang, chemically activated falloff, P-log, Chebyshev and the declared Blowers–Masel branch. Collision partners retain their kinetic orders, even when they cancel from net stoichiometry. Duplicate channels remain separate reactions.
  • P-log sums all terms at the same pressure before log interpolation. Chebyshev uses inverse-temperature and log-pressure scaled coordinates. The imported source semantics clamp P-log at pressure endpoints and evaluate Chebyshev's polynomial outside its fitted pressure interval. These source rules do not extend species thermochemistry beyond its declared temperature interval or establish physical accuracy outside the fitted rate domain.
  • The native concentration/rate basis is mol/L and mol/(L·s). Input length m/cm/mm, amount mol/kmol, time s/min and supported activation-energy units are converted once. A finite extension units: {volume: L, quantity: mol} can be used instead of a length declaration; L is never treated as a length. Source file, list and entry unit scopes are retained during section resolution.
  • Pressure is computed from the current ideal-gas inventory and temperature. Reversible gas rates use the selected thermo and C° = P°/(1000 RT) in mol/L, rather than silently reusing the historical liquid standard concentration. Internal energy is Σ n_i (h_i(T)−RT) and heat capacity its derivative; reaction heat is counted once by the shared energy balance.
  • Native thermal component limits derive from the vessel's explicitly declared thermal model. Historical liquid defaults and the public minimum 1-second heat/wait duration are unchanged. The mathematical batch integrator also supports subsecond stiff trajectories.

Custom/negative/nonreactant orders and signed pre-exponential coefficients require their explicit source permissions. Executable rate code, unsupported thermo/kinetics and unbalanced mechanisms reject. Transport and non-selected phases remain source metadata. Source h2o2.yaml and its BSD license remain under tests/fixtures/mechanisms/cantera-3.1.0/.

docs.title: Named sections and local source files
docs.text:
The Python entry accepts explicit library directories. The current file's directory has priority; no Cantera installation path or network download is implicitly consulted:

from chemworld.physchem import import_mechanism

network = import_mechanism(
    "my-mechanism/main.yaml", phase_name="gas", search_paths=["my-library"]
)

The YAML/JSON CLI accepts repeated --search-path arguments in lookup order, after the input file's own directory:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.physchem.mechanism_import \
  my-mechanism/main.yaml --phase gas \
  --search-path my-library --search-path shared-library \
  --output native-gas.json

A phase can select species and reactions from local named sections or files:

phases:
- name: gas
  thermo: ideal-gas
  kinetics: gas
  species:
  - thermo.yaml/species: [H2, H, O, O2, OH, H2O, HO2, H2O2, AR, N2]
  reactions:
  - reactions.yaml/hydrogen: all

For an in-memory document, convert_mechanism(..., source_documents={...}) accepts an explicit mapping from referenced filenames to document dictionaries. Named sections preserve source order and each source's unit system. Duplicate species selections, ambiguous file keys, missing files or sections, and unsupported selected reactions produce errors.

declared-species, skip-undeclared-elements and skip-undeclared-third-bodies apply only when explicitly requested by the source. The returned network's metadata["source_resolution"] records selected entries, omissions, source phase selection and document digests. It survives JSON replay; the resulting network uses the original inventory, heat and runtime consumers. External element/adjacent-phase sections and other phase families remain outside this gas importer.

A separate experimental import_chemkin(mechanism_path, thermo_path) entry implements a bounded gas subset for NASA7 and elementary/third-body/Lindemann/ Troe declarations. It rejects unsupported directives such as REV, PLOG, CHEB, FORD/RORD and MOLECULES rather than silently dropping them. It is not selected by this YAML/JSON CLI. Standard CHEMKIN interoperability remains unresolved: an actual Cantera 3.2 export exposes rejected ELEM shorthand and an incorrect NASA7 temperature-field ordering in the current reader. The source-selection handoff report retains the reproducible input and failures. The YAML/JSON comparison below does not qualify that separate importer.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_pressure_dependent_mechanisms.py tests/test_reaction_rate_contracts.py -q
uv run --no-sync --with 'cantera==3.1.0' python scripts/validate_native_mechanisms.py \
  --output /tmp/mechanism-comparison.json

The optional reference command runs 45 rate-grid cases, nine heated trajectories and three equilibrium limits. The development note fixes denominators and tolerances before execution. Final evidence and the first failed endpoint run are retained beside NATIVE_MECHANISM_ACCEPTANCE.md. This does not certify other mechanisms, platforms, wet-lab outcomes or a release build.

The current source-selection qualification uses actual Cantera 3.2: complete h2o2 and GRI30 in three file layouts, an explicitly selected hydrogen subset, mixed source units and a nonreacting gas. All nine units and 12,552 checks pass; the original 3,520-check gas-thermo/rate block also passes unchanged. These static comparisons remain distinct from reactor trajectory qualification. The new file-imported gas is also exercised in a real heat/wait world with exact snapshot continuation. See the source-selection report under workstreams/world_foundation/reports/convergence/34-source/ for retained failures and the installed-package result.

docs.title: A finite shared laboratory clock
docs.text:
Run the self-contained example from the locked repository environment:

uv run --no-sync python examples/native_shared_lab.py

shared_lab_world() authors two distinct liquid bottles, one finite-power heater and one programmed HPLC. It uses the existing session, native local solvers, sampling law, apparatus memory and transaction. No external chemistry backend, model key or distributed scheduler is involved.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.lab_world import shared_lab_world

lab = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=shared_lab_world())
lab.reset(seed=17)
lab.execute({"operation": "queue_lab_heat", "duration_s": 30,
             "target_temperature_K": 350})
lab.execute({"operation": "queue_lab_measure"})
lab.execute({"operation": "select_vessel", "vessel": "sample"})
lab.execute({"operation": "queue_lab_measure"})
result = lab.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 120})
print(result.info["actual_duration_s"])  # 30: next heater completion
print(lab.lab_status())                  # analyzer result is not yet visible

The default CompositionPhysics.lab_clock=None is the original local clock. An explicit LabClockSpec selects shared mode for the whole session. All enabled vessels advance together, whether selected or not. A requested wait is an upper bound: it returns at the next completion event. Another wait starts the next FIFO job at that same physical time. Zero-time requests between waits can be queued, but never retroactively change a specimen already taken. At equal timestamps, persistent sequence numbers determine completion order.

Analysis samples at service start, not at queue submission or result release. The existing sampler handles true withdrawals and persistent chromatograph carryover. Results carry sampled_at and available_at on the lab clock; only completed packets appear in lab_status() or info["lab_clock"]. Polling consumes no resource or randomness. Detector failures produce an invalid completed job, not a restored sample. Process, sampling and detector RNG states are independent.

Physical seconds are charged once across vessels. Analysis effort counts actual busy seconds separately, and sampling cost is charged once at service start. Queue/control/wait calls consume the ordinary action budget; job records expose the separate acquisition history. A numerical failure discards the entire uncommitted slice. A physical stop first realigns all systems to the earliest endpoint, commits that slice, then requires a full lab reset before further advancement. Existing committed events remain in the record.

Private snapshot().to_dict() and ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(...) restore device ownership, queue order, pending SSA events and unpublished packets exactly. Never provide a private continuation snapshot to an agent as observation evidence.

docs.title: Explicit limits
docs.text:
One or two independent closed native thermal/SSA vessels; at most one heater and one nonterminal native offline analyzer. The default finite session admits at most 64 jobs (configurable to 256), preserving all completion records. Thermal and SSA may be separate vessels, never an implicit hybrid solver in one vessel. Only queue, select, wait and terminate actions are available in this initial shared mode. Partial entity reset, terminal/in-situ instruments, inter-vessel/open flow and alternate phase strategies are rejected rather than silently mixing clocks. Chromatograph method configuration is authored before the shared session. These are synthetic development examples, not fitted laboratory chemistry or a claim of robot orchestration.

Queued detector readouts support sequential and keyed noise. Keyed mode uses the existing observation-coordinate primitive with a laboratory namespace and the persistent queue sequence; polling does not change the key, physical sampling or SSA stream. The detector seed and coordinate inputs persist in private snapshots. The optional lab_schedule.duration_range_s declares the public wait range down to 1 microsecond; without it the ordinary one-second lower bound is unchanged. This allows stopping inside a short offline acquisition without altering the instrument's declared analysis time or the underlying physical rates.

docs.title: Native stochastic and mixed chemistry
docs.text:
Declare ReactionNetworkSpec(..., stochastic={"volume_L": 0.01, "temperature_K": 298.15}) and pass integer counts to chemworld.world.stochastic_world.stochastic_world(network, counts, seed=7). Use the returned composition with ChemWorldRuntime, reset(), then execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 10}). This is the same runtime, transaction and accounting path as the deterministic worlds.

The default algorithm is gillespie-direct-v1. Select "algorithm": "gibson-bruck-next-reaction-v1" in the same stochastic declaration to use exact dependency-updated reaction clocks. Both methods use the same stochastic_world, actions and advance_stochastic API. Pure callers also pass the chosen algorithm to initial_continuation(seed, algorithm=...).

Each elementary direction is a separate irreversible mass_action reaction with parameters={"k": ...}. A↔B is two channels, not a potentially negative net propensity. The rate constants retain the network's mol/L and seconds convention. For molecularity m, the stochastic constant multiplying combinations is k*(N_A*V)**(1-m)*prod(factorial(r_i)). Non-integer stoichiometry, custom orders, activities, continuous controls, implicit ODE/SSA mixtures and molecularity above three are outside this finite implementation.

The phase ledger owns all material. Its mol values represent exact integer molecule counts divided by the exact Avogadro constant; conversion allows only four floating-point ULPs, not fractional dosing. Counts are bounded by 2**40 to keep integer resolution unambiguous. Process continuation belongs to the vessel's ProcessLedger and contains no second inventory: PCG64 state, process time, event count and a rate/inventory signature. Direct stores one absolute pending event; next-reaction stores each channel's absolute event time, cached propensity and any dormant channel's remaining internal Poisson hazard. Public state projections omit it. A real instantaneous intervention invalidates its pending event while keeping the process RNG stream; a read does neither.

snapshot().to_dict() / ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(payload) preserves the pending clocks and exact continuation, including in another process. The pure advance_stochastic API also returns individual event times/identities for numerical verification. A numerical event budget rolls the entire candidate advance back, rather than reporting chemical failure or charging physical time. The common runtime still applies its declared request/measurement resource rules. StochasticAdvance.work and runtime stochastic_work expose propensity evaluations and random draws. Sparse dependencies can reduce work per event; the direct/next-reaction cost comparison does not establish a universal wall-time speedup.

Only constant volume and temperature are supported. There is no claim of a caloric/energy model or fitted biochemical accuracy. Fractional destructive instruments are rejected at compilation; dedicated integer sampling and the two biochemical presets are the separate NATIVE-EXT-37 task. No COPASI or other upstream simulator is loaded by the runtime.

Development qualification: uv run --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_stochastic_kinetics.py; uv run --no-sync python scripts/validate_native_ssa.py --output /tmp/ssa-new-attempt.json. The latter refuses to overwrite a previous attempt. The fixed 4000-run design, all outcomes and statistical criteria are in the world_foundation workstream.

The next-reaction development block completed 49,152 trajectories across both methods; all 29 units and 353 fixed distribution, continuation, world and work comparisons passed. Its fixed design and statistical resolution are recorded in the 51A delivery.

docs.title: Approximate adaptive tau-leaping
docs.text:
The same StochasticSpec also accepts algorithm="adaptive-explicit-tau-leap-v1" with an explicit TauLeapPolicy. It samples integer Poisson firing totals, protects critical channels and falls back to direct SSA when leaping is unsuitable. Negative candidates are rejected and retried with a smaller step; accepted counts are never clipped. Ordinary rejection is not claimed to give rejection-unbiased paths, and epsilon is a local step-selection control rather than a global error bound.

Pending batches retain their absolute interval, firing counts and process RNG in the original continuation. Observations are step-held until a batch endpoint; output_hold_s exposes that lag. Snapshot restoration preserves this approximate numerical path exactly. A batch records aggregate firings, without inventing the individual event times of an SSA trajectory.

chemworld.examples.stochastic_tau_leap.run_example() exercises original world waits and restored continuation. The 51C delivery records 30 units, 192 comparisons and 49,152 distribution trajectories in each of two retained attempts, including non-grid observation error and fallback costs. These results do not qualify implicit tau methods, SDE or automatic partition selection.

docs.title: Fixed-partition continuous and discrete chemistry
docs.text:
StochasticHybridSpec declares the integer species and stochastic reaction channels of one reaction network. The remaining material uses continuous mol coordinates in the same phase ledger. Integrated Poisson hazards respond to the continuous trajectory; pending hazards and RNG survive ordinary snapshots. The original profile allows rate feedback between the partitions while each partition's net elemental stock remains closed. Its actual world and shared-clock qualification is recorded in the 51B delivery.

CrossPartitionHybridSpec explicitly selects real material transfer: one jump can change integer molecules and continuous mol by the corresponding molecular quantum. The original stochastic_hybrid_world and native wait entry remain the consumer. The original process continuation records cumulative cross-partition firings; the material ledger remains the only inventory. A continuous reactant must contain enough material for the whole jump, and the numerical domain must resolve a single molecule. Transfer receipts and both partitions' atomic changes are checked together before committing a time slice.

This profile retains fixed volume, temperature and partition assignments. It does not supply a heat model, consuming hybrid sampling or automatic repartitioning. Same-prefix snapshot continuation and numerical agreement under different adaptive integration splits are distinct guarantees. The 51D delivery records 36/36 development units and 338/338 checks, with a separate complete shared-world/runtime snapshot consumer and all retained failures.

docs.title: One complete experiment
docs.text: An experimental agent does more than choose an endpoint. It reads a contract, makes a sequence of physically constrained requests, observes instruments, manages resources and decides when the lifecycle is complete.

docs.title: Explore the frozen 15-step trajectory
docs.text:
The controls below are generated from the sanitized agent-instrument-use report. Select a step with a mouse, touch or the arrow keys.

One persistent agent, one complete lifecycle Loading frozen public evidence…

docs.title: What changes after each action?
docs.text:
Three records stay separate:

  1. Transaction: whether the requested action committed or rolled back.
  2. Public observation: what the instrument-facing agent is allowed to see.
  3. Resource outcome: process time, sample use and registered consequences.

This separation prevents an endpoint score from erasing how the result was obtained.

docs.title: Failure remains part of the record
docs.text: The deterministic recovery example intentionally requests phase separation before the physical preconditions exist. The operation rolls back physical, RNG and ghost state, retains its declared attempt consequence, and is followed by a valid recovery path. The submitted failure is retained during exact replay.

docs.title: Same experiment, changed world
docs.text:
An experiment author can construct controlled parent–child worlds that share the public task, action schema, resources and typed action sequence while changing one registered private component. The agent is judged from public feedback—not from direct access to the component identity.

Open the complete static trajectory, rollback and fork tables

Interpretation boundary

The trajectory demonstrates interface use and auditable execution, not model superiority. The world-fork matrix qualifies registered software-model interventions; it does not establish physical-laboratory transfer.

docs.title: Operations and instruments
docs.text:
Use the current public schema, not guessed laboratory verbs:

{"operation": "heat", "target_temperature_K": 350.0,
 "duration_s": 1200.0, "stirring_speed_rpm": 800.0}

target_temperature_K is the jacket setpoint, not an instantaneous measured sample temperature. heat/wait continue the current vessel's process. quench does not create a new batch. cool, stir, crystallize and filter are not standalone action IDs: use the task's actual operations, such as cool_crystallize and filter_crystals.

add_solvent can accumulate allowed finite-catalog mixtures; some task contracts restrict pure media. add_reagent is the declared premixed feed; add_component selects a public feed_catalog component. Resources use actual molar input. Do not infer hidden species names or assume every first material choice locks all future additions. New vessel/port and persistent-control operations are available only under their declared task/composition contracts.

For every state, inspect task_info(), action_schema(operation), available_actions() and validate_action(action). Registry membership is not task permission, and task permission is not current-state legality. Never hard-code the action vector length or silently clip out-of-range values.

Base instrument IDs are hplc, gc, uvvis, ph_meter, final_assay. Current core also supports explicitly declared nmr, ir, ms; some full-process contracts permit particle_size. Read the task's allowed_instruments: registry membership alone is not permission. configure_instrument sets scans, resolution and dilution before measure. These are finite anonymous calibrated reporters, not structure-identification models. IR/NMR-like features inside an existing synthetic packet do not by themselves authorize a standalone acquisition.

End a process with terminate, then request {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"}. Neither an open record, a cancelled session nor a budget truncation is a completed final assay. Missing values remain null; read masks. A negative result is retained as an assay, not deleted. Native replay reconstructs actions and observations, not reasoning.

Start with the executable examples. These virtual model operations are not physical laboratory instructions.

docs.title: 5-minute quickstart
docs.text:
Install the environment, run three operations and receive an instrument reading. These examples use synthetic models and need no model key or optional upstream solver.

git clone https://github.com/sunyrain/ChemWorld-Public.git
cd ChemWorld-Public
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run --no-sync chemworld capabilities --format json
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.user_reward

The last command adds two feeds and measures pressure. Its optional reward is an ordinary user function; changing it does not change the acquired observation.

For a longer experiment with retained material, transfer and a terminal assay:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_surface_research --bulk --mobile --terminal-assay

Next, design an environment, connect your own agent, or browse the native workflows. Python 3.11 and 3.12 are the documented installation targets. The package is a development source distribution.

Historical tutorial notebooks retain their pinned runtime and recorded outputs; use the notebook guide for those examples.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The capability index is the interactive API reference for the current public foundation. Each implemented capability has an inline Python interface, parameter/default table, complete example, explicit input and output captured by executing that example. You can copy and run the code without opening the implementation source.

Select Usage for a complete walkthrough, API & parameters for signatures and action fields, or Examples & output for the runnable code and its results. Additional examples are expandable. Planned capabilities are labelled and have no callable API.

Inputs and outputs default to a field/value/unit table with expandable nested groups. Switch to JSON to inspect the full structure; Copy JSON works in either view.

Examples use synthetic inputs or packaged presets. Some demonstrate initialization, configuration or a rejected request; their scope is stated beside the code. They are representative entry points, not an exhaustive listing of every Python symbol or a new scientific qualification. Numerical last digits can vary with the platform and solver version. See the current foundation for delivery boundaries.

docs.title: Run an example
docs.text:
Install the current checkout using Getting started. Save the copied Python code as example.py, then run uv run --no-sync python example.py. For example, convert a temperature using the public quantity API:

from chemworld.foundation.units import Quantity

result = Quantity(26.85, "degC").to("K")
print(result.value, result.unit)

300.0 K

docs.title: Runtime and authoring contracts
docs.text:
Apparatus examples show the actual action_schema() fields for the initialized session, including units, required fields, bounds and choices. Bounds can change with state: use validate_action() before execution. A request's receipt distinguishes a committed action from a rejection. Reading observe() returns the cached public packet; acquiring a new measurement uses execute({"operation": "measure", ...}).

docs.title: Maintainer release settings
docs.text:
These settings describe the current development website. Package releases remain a separate action.

  • Pages serves the root of the gh-pages branch. Source remains on main; generated HTML, search indexes and guide bundles are confined to the hosting branch.
  • The Documentation workflow builds both MkDocs and the capability explorer, then updates gh-pages with a normal push and explicitly requests a Pages build. A workflow-token push alone does not trigger branch-based Pages publication. When account billing prevents a job from starting, run the same locked build locally; do not count the blocked job as a successful check.
  • Add repository description: Programmable chemical worlds for controlled, replayable agent experimentation.
  • Set the homepage to https://sunyrain.github.io/ChemWorld-Public/.
  • Add topics: ai4science, chemistry, agent-evaluation, gymnasium, world-model, reinforcement-learning.
  • Create releases by pushing a version-matching tag only after CI and Documentation both pass.

Local website publication after validation:

uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra docs
uv run --no-sync python scripts/build_site.py --output site
git fetch origin gh-pages:gh-pages
uv run --no-sync ghp-import --no-jekyll --branch gh-pages site
git push origin gh-pages

The integrated website is served at /?lang=en and /?lang=zh. Its original guide reader uses #guides/<capability>/<document>/<section> routes, rendered from docs/ Markdown. The former /explore/, /docs/ and published guide URLs redirect into that interface, retaining language and section. Static MkDocs output remains a fallback for technical pages outside the domain-guide collection. The recordings are historical test snapshots, not a live backend.

The release workflow creates a GitHub Release and attaches source and Python package artifacts. PyPI publication is deliberately not enabled until package ownership and trusted publishing are configured.

docs.title: Persistent agent lifecycle
docs.text:
